title: 弘治十四年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
憲
楊士雲
同考試官訓導張批此題預道申伯就封
之事而戎有良翰文武是憲二句盖體宣王
分封本意作者率多忽此是篇詞暢理明
宜取之以冠多士
同考試官教諭秦批題乃一篇之關楗作者
多於良翰為憲處不知照應保南土式南邦
意此篇體認親切挑剔分明且理致精到
===
而文采不浮盖嘗究心於本領者與
考試官教諭高批大雅義詞約理精者
無踰是篇故錄之
考試官教諭歐陽批四篇經義俱可觀而
惟錄此篇者譬諸嘗鼎一臠旨可知矣
詩人之贈親臣美其就封而有以慰乎人表其
重望而足以法乎人盖慰乎人而法乎人非威
望素著者不能也詩人於親臣之就封得不預
道以美之哉宣王之舅申伯出封于謝而尹吉
punctuated:
憲。

楊士雲

同考試官訓導張批：此題預道申伯就封之事，而「戎有良翰」、「文武是憲」二句，盖體宣王分封本意。作者率多忽此，是篇詞暢理明，宜取之以冠多士。

同考試官教諭秦批：題乃一篇之關楗，作者多於「良翰」、「為憲」處，不知照應「保南土」、「式南邦」意。此篇體認親切，挑剔分明，且理致精到，而文采不浮，盖嘗究心於本領者與！

考試官教諭高批：大雅義詞約理精者，無踰是篇，故錄之。

考試官教諭歐陽批：四篇經義俱可觀，而惟錄此篇者，譬諸嘗鼎一臠，旨可知矣。

詩人之贈親臣，美其就封而有以慰乎人，表其重望而足以法乎人。盖慰乎人而法乎人，非威望素著者不能也。詩人於親臣之就封，得不預道以美之哉？宣王之舅申伯出封于謝，而尹吉
translation_en:
…takes as his model.

Yang Shiyun

Comment by Associate Examiner Zhang, Assistant Instructor: This topic anticipates the Earl of Shen’s departure to take up his fief. The two phrases, “You have a worthy bulwark” and “He takes Kings Wen and Wu as his models,” convey King Xuan’s underlying intention in granting the fief. Most writers overlook this. This essay’s language flows smoothly and its reasoning is clear; it deserves to be selected to head the work of the assembled candidates.

Comment by Associate Examiner Qin, Instructor: The topic is the pivotal passage of the entire ode. In treating “worthy bulwark” and “taking as models,” most writers fail to connect them with the ideas of “protecting the southern lands” and “setting a pattern for the southern states.” This essay grasps the meaning closely and discriminates clearly. Moreover, its reasoning is exact and thorough, and its literary embellishment is not superficial. Surely its author has devoted careful thought to the fundamentals!

Comment by Examiner Gao, Instructor: Among essays interpreting the Greater Odes, none surpasses this one in concision of expression and precision of reasoning. Accordingly, it is included here.

Comment by Examiner Ouyang, Instructor: All four essays on the meaning of the Classics merit attention. That only this one is included is like tasting a single morsel from a cooking cauldron: from it, one can know the flavor of the whole.

In presenting a poem to a minister who was a royal kinsman, the poet praises his departure to take up his fief as something that could reassure the people, and proclaims his great prestige as sufficient to make him their model. Indeed, only someone whose authority and reputation were long established could reassure the people and serve as their model. When such a minister departed to take up his fief, how could the poet fail to anticipate the occasion and praise him? King Xuan’s maternal uncle, the Earl of Shen, went out to take up his fief at Xie, and Yin Ji…

title: 弘治十四年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
甫作詩以送之及此謂夫申伯以王朝之世臣
膺南土之重寄威武足以讋服乎人心勇畧足
以作新乎士氣觀其就封之時徒焉步行以從
者擁導前後何如此其衆也入謝之際御焉挽
車以行者環衛左右何如彼其盛也周邦之人
得於觀感之間交致喜慶之辭以為是申伯之
武必能鎮定南服所謂之屏之翰者有所賴矣
汝今不有良翰乎斯申伯之勇必能保障南土
所謂于蕃于宣者有所托矣汝今不有良榦乎
===
然是甚顯之申伯以言其親則姻連玉牒而為
王室之懿親其寵之隆也何如榮冠戚里而為
宣王之元舅其望之重也何若是則操觚染翰
南土未必無文士也莫不以其文是法焉披堅
執銳南國未必無武士也靡不以其武是憲焉
是則南土是保式是南邦固宣王分封之本意
戎有良翰文武是憲又申伯就封之能事尹吉
甫預道以贈其行其意不既深乎嗟夫愛人以
德所以贈人以言也吉甫一代文章之伯於申
punctuated: 甫作詩以送之，及此謂夫申伯以王朝之世臣，膺南土之重寄，威武足以讋服乎人心，勇畧足以作新乎士氣。觀其就封之時，徒焉步行以從者，擁導前後，何如此其衆也！入謝之際，御焉挽車以行者，環衛左右，何如彼其盛也！周邦之人得於觀感之間，交致喜慶之辭，以為是申伯之武，必能鎮定南服，所謂之屏之翰者有所賴矣。汝今不有良翰乎？斯申伯之勇，必能保障南土，所謂于蕃于宣者有所托矣。汝今不有良榦乎？然是甚顯之申伯，以言其親，則姻連玉牒而為王室之懿親，其寵之隆也何如！榮冠戚里而為宣王之元舅，其望之重也何若！是則操觚染翰，南土未必無文士也，莫不以其文是法焉；披堅執銳，南國未必無武士也，靡不以其武是憲焉。是則南土是保，式是南邦，固宣王分封之本意；戎有良翰，文武是憲，又申伯就封之能事。尹吉甫預道以贈其行，其意不既深乎？嗟夫！愛人以德，所以贈人以言也。吉甫一代文章之伯，於申
translation_en:
…Jifu composed a poem to send him off. At this point he says that Shen Bo, as a hereditary servant of the royal court, had been entrusted with weighty responsibilities in the southern lands. His martial authority was sufficient to awe people into submission, and his courage and strategic ability sufficient to renew the soldiers’ morale. Look at the time when he went to take up his fief: those who followed on foot thronged before and behind him as escorts—how numerous they were! When he entered Xie, those who drove and drew the carriages surrounded and guarded him on either side—how imposing their array! Moved by what they saw, the people of Zhou exchanged joyful congratulations. They believed that Shen Bo’s martial prowess would surely pacify the southern territories: the one spoken of as their “screen and support” could now be relied upon. “Do you not now have a worthy support?” Shen Bo’s courage would surely safeguard the southern lands: the duties described as “serving as a fence and spreading royal authority” could now be entrusted to him. “Do you not now have a worthy mainstay?”

Moreover, this illustrious Shen Bo was linked by marriage to the royal genealogy and was a cherished kinsman of the royal house. How great was the favor he enjoyed! His glory surpassed that of all other royal relatives, and he was King Xuan’s senior maternal uncle. How weighty was his prestige! As for those who held writing tablets and dipped their brushes, the southern lands surely had men of letters, and all took his civil accomplishments as their model. As for those who wore armor and wielded sharp weapons, the southern regions surely had warriors, and all took his martial accomplishments as their standard. Thus, “protecting the southern lands” and “being a model for the southern states” were indeed King Xuan’s original purposes in granting the fief; “you have a worthy support” and “his civil and martial accomplishments are the standard” also expressed what Shen Bo could accomplish upon taking up his fief. Yin Jifu spoke of these things in anticipation, offering them as a parting gift. Was his intention not profoundly meaningful? Ah! Loving others through virtue is the reason for offering them words at parting. Jifu was the foremost literary master of his age; when Shen…

title: 弘治十四年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
伯封謝則咏崧高於仲山甫城齊則咏烝民其
事實其情親與後世葩詞藻句者大不侔矣然
則二賢固有德行者矣吉甫其亦善於贈行者歟
儀式刑文王之典日靖四方
陳淳
同考試官訓導張批題本平易作者多襲
陳言令人厭觀此篇說出後王格先之由詞
理嚴整筆力老健其工於葩經者與
同考試官教諭秦批題意具於傳註作者
===
多體認不真此篇順題講義坦然明白
且氣充詞贍無片言陳腐使人望之而知
其為竒士矣
考試官教諭高批體貼周王所以格先
享祭之意無餘蘊矣
考試官教諭歐陽批詩正而葩此作得之
法前王之舊章安今日之天下此王者格先之
由也盖前人之所制後人之所法也今後王法
典以安天下其感格先王之神有由然哉此宗
punctuated:
伯封謝，則咏《崧高》；於仲山甫城齊，則咏《烝民》。其事實，其情親，與後世葩詞藻句者大不侔矣。然則二賢固有德行者矣，吉甫其亦善於贈行者歟？
儀式刑文王之典，日靖四方。
陳淳
同考試官訓導張批：題本平易，作者多襲陳言，令人厭觀。此篇說出後王格先之由，詞理嚴整，筆力老健，其工於葩經者與？
同考試官教諭秦批：題意具於傳註，作者多體認不真。此篇順題講義，坦然明白，且氣充詞贍，無片言陳腐，使人望之而知其為竒士矣。
考試官教諭高批：體貼周王所以格先享祭之意，無餘蘊矣。
考試官教諭歐陽批：詩正而葩，此作得之。
法前王之舊章，安今日之天下，此王者格先之由也。盖前人之所制，後人之所法也。今後王法典以安天下，其感格先王之神有由然哉！此宗
translation_en:
…when the Earl of Shen was enfeoffed at Xie, he sang “Lofty Mountains” (Songgao); when Zhongshan Fu fortified Qi, he sang “The Multitude of the People” (Zhengmin). The events were real and the feelings intimate: these poems differed greatly from the flowery diction and ornate phrases of later ages. Thus the two worthies certainly possessed virtuous conduct; was Jifu not also skilled at offering words upon a departure?
“Model yourself upon and follow King Wen’s statutes, daily bringing peace to the four quarters.”
Chen Chun
Comment by Associate Examiner Zhang, Assistant Instructor: The topic itself is straightforward, but writers mostly repeat stale expressions, making their work tiresome to read. This essay explains how a later king moves his royal ancestor’s spirit. Its language and reasoning are rigorous and orderly, its brushwork seasoned and vigorous. Surely its author is accomplished in the Classic of Poetry!
Comment by Associate Examiner Qin, Instructor: The meaning of the topic is fully set out in the commentaries, yet writers mostly fail to apprehend it truly. This essay follows the topic in expounding its meaning, plainly and clearly. Moreover, its spirit is full and its diction rich, without a single stale phrase. One can see at a glance that its author is a man of exceptional talent.
Comment by Examiner Gao, Instructor: It enters sympathetically into the reasons why the Zhou king could move his ancestor’s spirit to accept the sacrifice, leaving no underlying meaning unexplored.
Comment by Examiner Ouyang, Instructor: The Poetry is upright yet richly ornamented. This composition captures that quality.
To follow the established institutions of former kings and bring peace to the realm today: this is how a king moves his ancestors’ spirits. For what earlier men instituted is what later men take as their model. Now, when a later king follows these statutes to bring peace to the realm, surely there is a reason why he can move the spirits of former kings to respond! This is the ancestral…

title: 弘治十四年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
祀文王於明堂以配上帝之樂歌也想其登歌
之頃致其兾享之誠謂夫我之奉祭上帝之享
既不敢必文王之享則有可必然所以必我文
王之享豈無自耶誠以文王安民之心寓諸典
籍也今雖沒矣典不與之俱沒我則儀而式之
于以恪遵成憲罔敢有或違文王安民之政布
諸典冊也今雖往矣典不與之俱往我則式而
刑之于以率由舊章罔敢有或懈如懷保小民
典之行於岐者悉舉而行之使行於昔者行於
===
===
今焉如惠鮮鰥寡政之布於豐者咸遵而布之
俾布於前者布於後焉夫我之法典者豈徒然
哉蓋以文王之典安天下之典今日之天下文
王之天下故自西自東四方何大也舉是典日
以安之使咸蒙至治之澤地雖異而澤之所及
無或異自南自北四方何廣也布斯典日以靖
之俾悉囿咸和之治人雖殊而治之所被無或
殊于以保郊鼎於無虞而鳧鷖既醉之太平千
載猶一日也于以衍姬錄於不墜而棫樸卷阿
punctuated: 祀文王於明堂以配上帝之樂歌也。想其登歌之頃，致其兾享之誠，謂夫我之奉祭，上帝之享既不敢必，文王之享則有可必然。所以必我文王之享，豈無自耶？誠以文王安民之心寓諸典籍也。今雖沒矣，典不與之俱沒，我則儀而式之，于以恪遵成憲，罔敢有或違。文王安民之政布諸典冊也。今雖往矣，典不與之俱往，我則式而刑之，于以率由舊章，罔敢有或懈。如懷保小民，典之行於岐者，悉舉而行之，使行於昔者行於今焉；如惠鮮鰥寡，政之布於豐者，咸遵而布之，俾布於前者布於後焉。夫我之法典者，豈徒然哉？蓋以文王之典，安天下之典；今日之天下，文王之天下。故自西自東，四方何大也！舉是典日以安之，使咸蒙至治之澤，地雖異，而澤之所及無或異。自南自北，四方何廣也！布斯典日以靖之，俾悉囿咸和之治，人雖殊，而治之所被無或殊。于以保郊鼎於無虞，而鳧鷖既醉之太平，千載猶一日也；于以衍姬錄於不墜，而棫樸卷阿
translation_en: …is a ritual song for sacrificing to King Wen in the Hall of Light, associating him with the Lord on High. Imagine the moment when the song was performed in the hall, expressing the sincerity of the hope that the offerings would be accepted: “In presenting my sacrifice, I dare not presume that the Lord on High will accept it; yet there is reason to be certain that King Wen will accept it. Can my certainty that King Wen will accept it be without a basis? It is truly because King Wen’s concern to bring peace to the people resides in the canonical writings. Though he has now died, his canons have not died with him. I take them as my standard and model, thereby reverently observing the established statutes without daring to depart from them in any way. King Wen’s measures for bringing peace to the people are set forth in the written records. Though he has now departed, his canons have not departed with him. I model myself upon them and follow them, thereby adhering to the old regulations without daring to show any negligence. For example, in cherishing and protecting the common people, I put fully into practice the canons implemented in Qi, so that what was practiced in the past is practiced today. In showing kindness to widowers and widows and relieving their distress, I follow and promulgate all the measures instituted in Feng, so that what was instituted before is instituted again afterward. Can my emulation of these canons be without purpose? King Wen’s canons are the canons for bringing peace to All under Heaven, and All under Heaven today is King Wen’s All under Heaven. Thus, from west to east, how vast are the four quarters! Each day I apply these canons to bring them peace, so that all receive the blessings of consummate government. Though the places differ, none differs in receiving those blessings. From south to north, how extensive are the four quarters! Each day I promulgate these canons to bring them tranquility, so that all are encompassed within a government of universal harmony. Though the people differ, none differs in receiving the benefits of that government. Thereby the suburban sacrifices and the sacrificial tripods are preserved free from danger, and the great peace celebrated in Wild Ducks and Gulls (Fu yi) and Already Drunk (Ji zui) remains the same through a thousand years as through a single day. Thereby the dynastic fortunes of the Ji house are perpetuated without decline, and the Clustered Oaks (Yu pu) and Winding Mound (Juan a)…”

title: 弘治十四年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
之大化百世猶一朝也噫法典安民則所以感
格之者其有素矣配享之祭文王之神豈不既
右享乎考之明堂之祭周公以義起之也然於
天維庶其饗之不敢加一詞焉於文王則言儀
式其典日靖四方天不待賛法文王所以法天
也卒章惟言畏天之威而不及文王者統於尊
也畏天所以畏文王也天與文王夫何間之有
哉
春秋
===
諸侯遂圍許 曹伯襄復歸于曹遂會諸
侯圍許〔俱僖公二十八年〕
周希謙
同考試官學正王 批 題本胡傳晋討許不
臣曹復國不義人皆知之究其聖人所以予奪
者則難發揮是篇獨能組織傳註鋪叙明
白且有斷制真得屬比之教者况三場俱優
取冠本房公論恊矣
考試官教諭高 批 說曹許可責處讀之
punctuated:
之大化，百世猶一朝也。噫！法典安民，則所以感格之者，其有素矣。配享之祭，文王之神豈不既右享乎？考之明堂之祭，周公以義起之也。然於天，維「庶其饗之」，不敢加一詞焉；於文王，則言「儀式其典，日靖四方」。天不待賛，法文王所以法天也。卒章惟言「畏天之威」，而不及文王者，統於尊也。畏天所以畏文王也，天與文王夫何間之有哉？
春秋
諸侯遂圍許。曹伯襄復歸于曹，遂會諸侯圍許。〔俱僖公二十八年〕
周希謙
同考試官學正王批：題本胡傳，晋討許不臣，曹復國不義，人皆知之。究其聖人所以予奪者，則難發揮。是篇獨能組織傳註，鋪叙明白，且有斷制，真得屬比之教者。况三場俱優，取冠本房，公論恊矣。
考試官教諭高批：說曹、許可責處，讀之
translation_en:
…their great transforming influence makes a hundred generations seem like a single morning. Ah! By following the exemplary statutes and bringing peace to the people, one has long established the means of moving the spirits to respond. At the sacrifice in which King Wen receives offerings alongside Heaven, would not his spirit indeed come to receive them? Examining the sacrifice in the Hall of Light, we find that the Duke of Zhou instituted it according to what was right. Yet concerning Heaven, he said only, “May it accept the offerings,” not daring to add another word. Concerning King Wen, however, he said, “Follow and emulate his statutes, daily bringing peace to the four quarters.” Heaven requires no praise; taking King Wen as one's model is the means of taking Heaven as one's model. The final stanza speaks only of “fearing Heaven's might” and does not mention King Wen because both are subsumed under the more exalted. To stand in awe of Heaven is to stand in awe of King Wen. What distinction could there be between Heaven and King Wen?
Spring and Autumn Annals
“The regional lords thereupon besieged Xu.” “Xiang, Earl of Cao, returned to Cao and subsequently joined the regional lords in besieging Xu.” 〔Both entries are from the twenty-eighth year of Duke Xi.〕
Zhou Xiqian
Comment by Associate Examiner Wang, School Director: The topic is based on Hu's Commentary. Everyone knows that Jin attacked Xu for failing in its duties as a subject, and that Cao's restoration to his state was contrary to righteousness. Yet it is difficult to elucidate fully the grounds on which the Sage bestowed approval or disapproval. This essay alone succeeds in weaving together the commentary and annotations, presenting its exposition clearly, and offering decisive judgments. It truly grasps the teaching conveyed through arranging and comparing events. Moreover, his work in all three sessions was excellent. Selecting him as the foremost candidate in this examination section accords with the consensus.

〔利之意〕
諸侯討罪春秋正君臣之典諸侯復國春秋嚴
義利之別觀諸書法特予諸侯圍許深責曹襄
復國意斯見矣聖筆之精一何至哉昔者晋文
主伯吾聞其一戰勝楚兩朝于王矣迺今因許
不會率會温之師以討之禁其樵採絕其往來
文之圍許似亦過也經於此乃予晋文其意也
===
何按古者天子巡狩諸侯皆有方岳之朝周法
天子行幸三百里內有起居之問河陽踐土是
許之密邇者使許誠能膏車秣馬以會夫諸侯
端委弁冕以覲夫天子庶得人臣之職則亦無
可討者夫何諸侯再會也許則若罔聞知天子
再臨也許則畧不介意則於禮當討而在文問
罪之師不容緩矣雖曰環城而攻似為過舉然
不朝是討不臣是問以王法律之在貶爵削地
可也烏可執此以重文之咎耶故經於此書曰
punctuated:
凜然。
考試官教諭歐陽批：〔得聖人正名分嚴義〕〔利之意〕
諸侯討罪，春秋正君臣之典；諸侯復國，春秋嚴義利之別。觀諸書法，特予諸侯圍許，深責曹襄復國，意斯見矣。聖筆之精，一何至哉！昔者晋文主伯，吾聞其一戰勝楚，兩朝于王矣。迺今因許不會，率會温之師以討之，禁其樵採，絕其往來，文之圍許似亦過也。經於此乃予晋文，其意也何？按古者天子巡狩，諸侯皆有方岳之朝；周法，天子行幸，三百里內有起居之問。河陽、踐土，是許之密邇者。使許誠能膏車秣馬以會夫諸侯，端委弁冕以覲夫天子，庶得人臣之職，則亦無可討者。夫何諸侯再會也，許則若罔聞知；天子再臨也，許則畧不介意？則於禮當討，而在文問罪之師不容緩矣。雖曰環城而攻似為過舉，然不朝是討，不臣是問，以王法律之，在貶爵削地可也。烏可執此以重文之咎耶？故經於此書曰：
translation_en:
…makes one shudder with awe.

Comment by Examiner Ouyang, Instructor: 〔It captures the Sage’s intention to rectify names and status and strictly distinguish righteousness〕〔from profit.〕

When the regional lords punish wrongdoing, the Spring and Autumn Annals rectifies the norms governing ruler and minister; when a regional lord is restored to his state, the Spring and Autumn Annals draws a strict distinction between righteousness and profit. Examining its wording, we find that it specifically approves the regional lords’ siege of Xu and severely censures Xiang of Cao for his restoration to his state. Its intention is thus apparent. How consummate is the precision of the Sage’s brush!

Formerly, when Duke Wen of Jin presided as hegemon, I have heard that he defeated Chu in a single battle and twice paid court to the king. Now, because Xu failed to attend the assembly, he led the forces assembled at Wen to punish it, prohibiting its gathering of firewood and cutting off passage to and from it. Duke Wen’s siege of Xu would seem excessive. Yet the Classic here approves Duke Wen. What is its intention?

We find that in antiquity, when the Son of Heaven made a tour of inspection, the regional lords all attended court at the sacred peak of their region. Under Zhou law, when the Son of Heaven traveled, those within three hundred li were required to inquire after his well-being. Heyang and Jiantu were close to Xu. Had Xu truly been able to grease its carriages and feed its horses to assemble with the regional lords, and don ceremonial robes and caps to appear before the Son of Heaven, it would have come close to fulfilling a subject’s duty, and there would have been nothing to punish. Why, then, when the regional lords assembled twice, did Xu behave as though it had heard and knew nothing? When the Son of Heaven came twice, why did Xu pay no heed whatsoever? According to ritual propriety, Xu deserved punishment, and Duke Wen could not delay the dispatch of an army to call it to account.

Although surrounding and attacking its city might seem excessive, it was failure to attend court that was being punished, and failure to act as a subject that was being called to account. Judged by royal law, even reduction of its rank and loss of its territory would have been permissible. How could one seize upon this to increase Duke Wen’s culpability? Thus the Classic here writes: …

title: 弘治十四年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
遂傳曰其稱遂繼事之辭也其予夫晉文所以
責夫許者何如哉所謂正君臣之典者盖如此
若曹人從楚吾聞其見執於晉以畀於宋矣廼
今因晉見釋遂會諸侯以圍許位其固有國其
宜君曹之復國不亦可乎經於此於曹書名其
貶云何夫義者天理之公正其義必推之天下
國家而可行利者人欲之私放於利必至於奪
攘而後厭正義明道在諸侯所有事者使曹苟
能持詞執禮以請於王仗義執言以復其國庶
===
得歸國之道則亦無可議者奈何始之見執也
既不上告王室以求伸今之復國也又乃下貨
筮史而得釋則於利是行而於晉囚執之刑幸
而免矣借曰貨以藩身何愛之有然臨難苟免
以賂得國以大義律之誠匹夫賤者事也豈可
以此而薄曹之罪耶故經於此書其名曰襄傳
曰其歸之道非所以歸也其深責曹襄而所以
生名之者何若哉所謂嚴義利之別者又如此
雖然許曹不足言矣然晉文合四國能勝强大
punctuated:
遂。傳曰：「其稱遂，繼事之辭也。」其予夫晉文，所以責夫許者，何如哉？所謂正君臣之典者，盖如此。
若曹人從楚，吾聞其見執於晉，以畀於宋矣。廼今因晉見釋，遂會諸侯以圍許。位其固有，國其宜君，曹之復國不亦可乎？經於此於曹書名，其貶云何？夫義者，天理之公，正其義必推之天下國家而可行；利者，人欲之私，放於利必至於奪攘而後厭。正義明道，在諸侯所有事者。使曹苟能持詞執禮以請於王，仗義執言以復其國，庶得歸國之道，則亦無可議者。奈何始之見執也，既不上告王室以求伸；今之復國也，又乃下貨筮史而得釋，則於利是行，而於晉囚執之刑幸而免矣。借曰：「貨以藩身，何愛之有？」然臨難苟免，以賂得國，以大義律之，誠匹夫賤者事也。豈可以此而薄曹之罪耶？故經於此書其名曰襄。傳曰：「其歸之道，非所以歸也。」其深責曹襄，而所以生名之者，何若哉？所謂嚴義利之別者，又如此。
雖然，許曹不足言矣。然晉文合四國，能勝强大
translation_en:
…“thereupon.” The Commentary says: “Its use of ‘thereupon’ expresses the continuation of an undertaking.” How it approves Duke Wen of Jin for calling Xu to account! Such is what is meant by setting right the prescribed relationship between ruler and subject.
As for the ruler of Cao, who followed Chu, I have heard that he was seized by Jin and handed over to Song. Now, having obtained his release through Jin, he thereupon joined the other lords in besieging Xu. The rank was originally his, and the state was one he ought properly to rule: was his restoration to Cao not permissible? Yet here the Classic records the ruler of Cao by his personal name. What censure does this convey? Righteousness is the impartiality of Heaven’s principle: to set one’s conduct right according to righteousness, it must be practicable when extended throughout the world, its states, and its ruling houses. Profit is the selfishness of human desires: one who acts in pursuit of profit will not be satisfied until he resorts to seizure and plunder. Upholding righteousness and making the Way manifest are duties incumbent upon the feudal lords. Had the ruler of Cao presented his case in accordance with ritual propriety to petition the king, and spoken on the strength of righteousness to recover his state, he might have fulfilled the proper way of returning to his state, leaving nothing open to criticism. Why, then, when first taken prisoner, did he fail to appeal upward to the royal house to seek redress, and now, in recovering his state, stoop to bribing a diviner to secure his release? He thus acted for profit and escaped Jin’s punishment of imprisonment only by good fortune. Even if one says, “Why begrudge wealth used to protect oneself?”—merely seeking escape when faced with peril and obtaining a state through bribery are, judged by the standard of great righteousness, truly the acts of a contemptible common fellow. How could this lessen Cao’s guilt? Therefore, here the Classic records his personal name, Xiang. The Commentary says: “The means by which he returned were not the proper means of returning.” How severely it censures Xiang of Cao, recording his personal name while he was still alive! Such, again, is what is meant by drawing a strict distinction between righteousness and profit.
Nevertheless, Xu and Cao hardly merit further discussion. Yet Duke Wen of Jin united four states and was able to defeat the mighty…

title: 弘治十四年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
之楚合十一國之師不能服蕞爾之許何哉盖
踐土之盟血未乾又帥諸侯以會温城濮之大
勞甫息又帥諸侯以圍許禮煩威黷諸侯亦罷
於奔命矣况討許以不朝為名假公義以濟私
忿乎故曰晉文公譎而不正
冬十月壬午公子遂會晉趙盾盟于衡雍
乙酉公子遂會雒戎盟于暴俱文公八年
楊敷頤
同考試官學正王批内夏外夷作者類能
===
言之於盟會上講雒邑戎不當居處畧弗
之及此作詞不煩而理獨到必造詣之深
者取之
考試官教諭高批得謹嚴意
考試官教諭歐陽批春秋謹華夷之辨意
正如此
即春秋深别華夷之盟見春秋深謹華夷之辨
夫明族類別内外春秋法也得不於公子遂之
盟趙盾雒戎以深致意哉何則中國之有戎狄
punctuated:
之楚，合十一國之師，不能服蕞爾之許，何哉？盖踐土之盟血未乾，又帥諸侯以會温；城濮之大勞甫息，又帥諸侯以圍許。禮煩威黷，諸侯亦罷於奔命矣。况討許以不朝為名，假公義以濟私忿乎？故曰：「晉文公譎而不正。」
冬十月壬午，公子遂會晉趙盾，盟于衡雍。乙酉，公子遂會雒戎，盟于暴。俱文公八年。
楊敷頤
同考試官學正王批：「内夏外夷，作者類能言之。於盟會上講雒邑戎不當居處，畧弗之及。此作詞不煩而理獨到，必造詣之深者，取之。」
考試官教諭高批：「得謹嚴意。」
考試官教諭歐陽批：「春秋謹華夷之辨，意正如此。」
即春秋深别華夷之盟，見春秋深謹華夷之辨。
夫明族類，別内外，春秋法也。得不於公子遂之盟趙盾、雒戎，以深致意哉？何則？中國之有戎狄
translation_en:
…Chu, yet when he assembled the armies of eleven states, he could not subdue the tiny state of Xu. Why was this? The blood of the covenant at Jiantu had scarcely dried before he again led the feudal lords to assemble at Wen; the great exertions at Chengpu had barely ceased before he again led them to besiege Xu. Ceremonies became burdensome and the exercise of military might excessive; the feudal lords, too, were exhausted by rushing to obey his commands. Moreover, he attacked Xu on the pretext that it had failed to attend court, borrowing the name of public justice to satisfy his private resentment. Thus it is said: “Duke Wen of Jin was deceitful and not upright.”
“In winter, in the tenth month, on renwu, Prince Sui met Zhao Dun of Jin and covenanted at Hengyong.” “On yiyou, Prince Sui met the Luo Rong and covenanted at Bao.” Both entries are from the eighth year of Duke Wen.
Yang Fuyi.
Associate Examiner Wang, School Director, comments: “Treating the Xia as insiders and the Yi as outsiders is something most writers can discuss. In discussing these covenant meetings, however, they scarcely touch upon the point that the Rong ought not to reside at Luo. This composition is concise in wording yet uniquely penetrating in its reasoning. It must be the work of someone with profound attainment. Select it.”
Examiner Gao, Instructor, comments: “It captures the sense of scrupulous rigor.”
Examiner Ouyang, Instructor, comments: “Precisely this is the intent of the Spring and Autumn Annals in scrupulously distinguishing the Hua from the Yi.”
Through the Spring and Autumn Annals’ sharp distinction between covenants with the Hua and those with the Yi, we see how scrupulously it maintains the distinction between Hua and Yi.
To clarify distinctions of peoples and differentiate those within from those without is the rule of the Spring and Autumn Annals. Could it fail, then, to attach profound significance to Prince Sui’s covenants with Zhao Dun and the Luo Rong? Why is this? The presence of Rong and Di in the central states…

title: 弘治十四年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
猶君子之有小人在周公有膺懲之舉在大易
有否泰之分戎狄者豈可雜處於中國而中國
者安可混同於戎狄耶廼今魯文中葉仲遂執
政內焉欲免晉討外焉欲結戎援十月壬午既
偕趙盾而講盟衡雍是月乙酉復偕雒戎而結
盟于暴衡雍盟也以大夫而專諸侯之禮猶以
中國而交中國于暴盟也以戎醜而干中國之
事是以中國而交夷狄度彼叅此固無足取矣
夫春秋記約而志詳者也於是二盟而深別之
===
何詞之贅而不憚煩乎盖以雒邑天地之中王
畿之內四時陰陽之所和萬國衣冠之所萃斯
何地歟以戎醜而可居耶彼戎以西方之夷僻
在荒服之外氈毳其服侏㒀其語戎何人斯於
雒邑而可居耶以聲明文物之區雜被髮野祭
之俗華夷之族類泯然矣內外之藩籬蕩然矣
苟於此而不深別之謹嚴之法安在哉經於是
一則曰公子遂二則曰公子遂不使雒戎同於
趙盾一則曰壬午二則曰乙酉不使戎盟混於
punctuated: 猶君子之有小人。在周公，有膺懲之舉；在大易，有否泰之分。戎狄者，豈可雜處於中國，而中國者，安可混同於戎狄耶？廼今魯文中葉，仲遂執政，內焉欲免晉討，外焉欲結戎援。十月壬午，既偕趙盾而講盟衡雍；是月乙酉，復偕雒戎而結盟于暴。衡雍盟也，以大夫而專諸侯之禮，猶以中國而交中國；于暴盟也，以戎醜而干中國之事，是以中國而交夷狄。度彼叅此，固無足取矣。夫春秋記約而志詳者也，於是二盟而深別之，何詞之贅而不憚煩乎？盖以雒邑，天地之中，王畿之內，四時陰陽之所和，萬國衣冠之所萃，斯何地歟，以戎醜而可居耶？彼戎，以西方之夷，僻在荒服之外，氈毳其服，侏㒀其語，戎何人斯，於雒邑而可居耶？以聲明文物之區，雜被髮野祭之俗，華夷之族類泯然矣，內外之藩籬蕩然矣。苟於此而不深別之，謹嚴之法安在哉？經於是，一則曰公子遂，二則曰公子遂，不使雒戎同於趙盾；一則曰壬午，二則曰乙酉，不使戎盟混於
translation_en:
…just as gentlemen have petty men in their midst. The Duke of Zhou undertook punitive campaigns against them; the great Book of Changes distinguishes between Obstruction (Pi) and Peace (Tai). How could the Rong and Di be allowed to dwell intermingled with the central states, and how could the central states be confounded with the Rong and Di? Yet midway through the reign of Duke Wen of Lu, Zhong Sui held power. In domestic affairs he sought to avert punitive action by Jin; abroad he sought to secure Rong support. On the renwu day of the tenth month, he joined Zhao Dun in concluding a covenant at Hengyong; on the yiyou day of that same month, he again concluded a covenant, this time with the Luo Rong at Bao. In the covenant at Hengyong, a grand master usurped the ceremonial prerogatives of the feudal lords, yet it was still one central state dealing with another. In the covenant at Bao, the Rong rabble interfered in the affairs of the central states: here a central state was dealing with barbarians. Weighing the former against the latter, neither was worthy of approval.

The Spring and Autumn Annals is concise in its record yet detailed in its import. Why, then, does it distinguish these two covenants so carefully, undeterred by troublesome repetition? Luoyi lies at the center of Heaven and Earth, within the royal domain. It is where the yin and yang of the four seasons harmonize, and where the capped and robed representatives of the myriad states assemble. What sort of place is this, that the Rong rabble should be allowed to reside there? Those Rong are barbarians of the west, dwelling remotely beyond even the outermost zone of submission. Their clothing is felt and fur; their speech is unintelligible jabber. Who are these Rong, that they should be allowed to reside in Luoyi? To mingle customs of loose hair and sacrifices in the wild with a region of illustrious institutions and refined culture is to efface the distinction between the peoples of Hua and Yi and sweep away the barriers between inner and outer. If no careful distinction is made here, where is the principle of scrupulous rigor?

Thus the Classic says “Prince Sui” in the first entry and “Prince Sui” again in the second, refusing to place the Luo Rong on the same footing as Zhao Dun. It gives “renwu” in the first entry and “yiyou” in the second, refusing to let the covenant with the Rong be confused with…

title: 弘治十四年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
晉盟而又正其名與地以深別之者使人知華
夏之中雜邑之內此為華彼為夷猶薰蕕之不
可以同器涇渭之不可以同流則族類以明內
外以別名分截然確乎其不可雜矣立法之精
且嚴何如哉不特此也中國而夷狄則狄之夷
狄猾夏則膺之謹魯隱于唐之盟志楚子陸渾
之伐皆此意也觀於夾谷之會所謂裔不謀夏
夷不亂華之言則知春秋之旨矣噫以為經世
之典撥亂反正之書百王不易之大法信夫
===
禮記
故祭帝於郊所以定天位也
陳傑
考試官教諭高批作此義者類襲陳
言可厭而於定天位處亦欠明白詞理兩
得是篇其空群矣
考試官教諭歐陽批說出先王達禮教之意
先王行尊天之禮所以立尊君之禮盖莫尊於
天而君儗之也因尊天而尊君之禮立焉則禮
punctuated:
晉盟，而又正其名與地以深別之者，使人知華夏之中、雜邑之內，此為華，彼為夷，猶薰蕕之不可以同器、涇渭之不可以同流，則族類以明，內外以別，名分截然，確乎其不可雜矣。立法之精且嚴何如哉！不特此也，中國而夷狄則狄之，夷狄猾夏則膺之。謹魯隱于唐之盟，志楚子陸渾之伐，皆此意也。觀於夾谷之會，所謂「裔不謀夏，夷不亂華」之言，則知《春秋》之旨矣。噫！以為經世之典、撥亂反正之書、百王不易之大法，信夫！

禮記
故祭帝於郊，所以定天位也。
陳傑

考試官教諭高批：作此義者，類襲陳言，可厭，而於定天位處亦欠明白。詞理兩得，是篇其空群矣！

考試官教諭歐陽批：說出先王達禮教之意。

先王行尊天之禮，所以立尊君之禮，盖莫尊於天，而君儗之也。因尊天而尊君之禮立焉，則禮
translation_en:
…the covenant with Jin. Moreover, by correctly specifying the names and places to distinguish them sharply, it enables people to understand that, within the central Xia lands and within the mixed settlement [?], these are Hua and those are Yi. Just as fragrant and foul-smelling plants cannot share a vessel, and the Jing and Wei rivers cannot share a stream, so the peoples are clearly identified, the inner and outer domains distinguished, and distinctions of status sharply drawn and firmly secured against confusion. How precise and rigorous is this establishment of rules! Nor is this all: when the central states behave as barbarians, it treats them as barbarians; when barbarians bring disorder to the Xia, it strikes them down. Its circumspect treatment of Duke Yin of Lu’s covenant at Tang and its recording of the Viscount of Chu’s campaign against Luhun both convey this intention. Considering the meeting at Jiagu and the words, “Those of the distant regions must not plot against the Xia; the Yi must not disrupt the Hua,” one understands the purport of the Spring and Autumn Annals. Ah! Truly it is a canon for governing the world, a book for dispelling disorder and restoring proper order, and a great law that a hundred kings could not alter!

Record of Rites
“Thus, sacrificing to Di in the suburban precinct serves to establish Heaven’s position.”
Chen Jie

Comment by Examiner Gao, Instructor: Those who compose essays on this passage generally repeat stale expressions, which is tiresome; moreover, they fail to explain clearly the point about establishing Heaven’s position. This essay succeeds in both expression and reasoning: surely it stands above all the others!

Comment by Examiner Ouyang, Instructor: It brings out the intention of the former kings to make instruction through ritual prevail.

The former kings performed rites honoring Heaven in order to establish rites honoring the ruler, for nothing is more exalted than Heaven, and the ruler is its counterpart. When rites honoring the ruler are established through honoring Heaven, then ritual…

title: 弘治十四年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
教何患其不達哉記禮運者謂夫帝乃天之所
主天乃帝之所寓萬物資之以始功莫尚也先
王則儀物具陳駕鑾輿而有事於吉土之郊歲
功資之以成德莫加也先王則精誠懇到被龍
袞而大饗於泰壇之上攄報本之心於燔燎之
餘惴惴然恐帝之遠而難格也伸反始之念於
對越之頃勿勿乎冀天之聽而來饗也所以然
者盖以民之於君猶君之於天君而不知所以
尊天民而安知所以尊君哉今郊祭而尊天之
===
禮以行則天下之民莫不曰代天理物吾君之
功無間於帝知帝之至尊則知君之同尊也又
莫不曰繼天立極吾君之德配合於天知天之
當事則知君之當事也巍巍九重四海傾心而
仰之如帝位於是而定矣穆穆一人萬方拱極
而戴之如天分於是而正矣吁禮行而天道顯
位定而君分尊先王達禮教之意何其至哉抑
不特此耳祀社於國所以列地利也祖廟所以
本仁也擯禮鬼神而祀山川本諸事為而祭五
punctuated: 教何患其不達哉？記《禮運》者謂夫帝乃天之所主，天乃帝之所寓。萬物資之以始，功莫尚也，先王則儀物具陳，駕鑾輿而有事於吉土之郊；歲功資之以成，德莫加也，先王則精誠懇到，被龍袞而大饗於泰壇之上。攄報本之心於燔燎之餘，惴惴然恐帝之遠而難格也；伸反始之念於對越之頃，勿勿乎冀天之聽而來饗也。所以然者，盖以民之於君，猶君之於天。君而不知所以尊天，民而安知所以尊君哉？今郊祭而尊天之禮以行，則天下之民莫不曰：「代天理物，吾君之功無間於帝。」知帝之至尊，則知君之同尊也。又莫不曰：「繼天立極，吾君之德配合於天。」知天之當事，則知君之當事也。巍巍九重，四海傾心而仰之如帝，位於是而定矣；穆穆一人，萬方拱極而戴之如天，分於是而正矣。吁！禮行而天道顯，位定而君分尊，先王達禮教之意何其至哉！抑不特此耳，祀社於國，所以列地利也；祖廟，所以本仁也；擯禮鬼神而祀山川，本諸事為而祭五
translation_en:
…why fear that ritual instruction will not reach everywhere? The author of “The Conveyance of Rites” (Li yun) says that the Lord on High is Heaven’s governing power, and Heaven is where the Lord on High resides. All things depend upon him for their beginnings; no achievement surpasses this. Thus the former kings displayed all the ceremonial objects and rode in their bell-adorned carriages to perform sacrifices on auspicious ground in the suburbs. The year’s labors depend upon him for their completion; no virtue exceeds this. Thus the former kings brought their utmost sincerity, donned dragon robes, and offered the great sacrifice upon the Grand Altar. Amid the burning offerings, they expressed their desire to repay the source of their blessings, trembling lest the Lord on High be distant and difficult to draw near. As they stood reverently before him, they expressed their wish to return to the beginning, eagerly [?] hoping that Heaven would hear and come to enjoy the offerings.

The reason for this is that the people stand in relation to their ruler as the ruler stands in relation to Heaven. If the ruler does not know how to honor Heaven, how can the people know how to honor their ruler? Now, when the suburban sacrifice is performed and the rite of honoring Heaven is put into practice, all the people under Heaven say: “In ordering all things on Heaven’s behalf, our ruler’s achievements are indistinguishable from those of the Lord on High.” Knowing the supreme honor due to the Lord on High, they know that their ruler shares that honor. They also all say: “In carrying on Heaven’s work and establishing the supreme standard, our ruler’s virtue accords with Heaven.” Knowing that Heaven must be served, they know that their ruler must be served. Lofty within the ninefold palace, he is revered by all within the four seas, who turn their hearts toward him as toward the Lord on High; his position is thereby established. Reverent and majestic, the One Man is upheld by all regions, which gather about him as about the pole star and honor him as Heaven; his proper station is thereby rectified. Ah! When ritual is practiced, Heaven’s Way becomes manifest; when the ruler’s position is established, his station is honored. How consummate was the former kings’ intention to extend ritual instruction everywhere!

Yet this is not all. Sacrificing to the soil altar in the capital serves to set forth the benefits of the earth; the ancestral temple serves to root benevolence in its source. They ritually received [?] ghosts and spirits and sacrificed to mountains and rivers; taking practical affairs as their basis, they offered the five…

title: 弘治十四年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
祀皆是使禮教之四達廟有宗祝朝有三公學
有三老五更皆明禮教以淑天下至於君之一
身乃居巫史瞽侑之中而守至正焉則又以禮
自防示教於天下也先王以禮示教而以身為
率如此所以幽感神明感人而臻類應之效也
夫豈不宜
紀綱既正天下大定
趙儀
考試官教諭高批本傳註先序之以
===
禮為說有發揮有照應經義如此可錄矣
考試官教諭歐陽批得子夏告文侯意
惟禮得其序斯世極其治蓋禮乃世之大閑也
孰謂禮得其序而世有不治者哉子夏答魏文
侯推言古樂之所由作如此謂夫昔者聖王因
天下大當以興制作立父子君臣以為紀綱紀
則有六所謂諸父諸舅有善而有義族人昆弟
有敘而有親以至師長朋友有尊而有舊也紀
之所在禮莫大焉綱則有三所謂相臨而有君
punctuated:
祀，皆是使禮教之四達。廟有宗祝，朝有三公，學有三老五更，皆明禮教以淑天下。至於君之一身，乃居巫史瞽侑之中而守至正焉，則又以禮自防，示教於天下也。先王以禮示教，而以身為率如此，所以幽感神，明感人，而臻類應之效也。夫豈不宜？
紀綱既正，天下大定。
趙儀
考試官教諭高批：本傳註，先序之，以禮為說，有發揮，有照應。經義如此，可錄矣。
考試官教諭歐陽批：得子夏告文侯意。
惟禮得其序，斯世極其治。蓋禮乃世之大閑也，孰謂禮得其序而世有不治者哉？子夏答魏文侯，推言古樂之所由作如此。謂夫昔者聖王因天下大當以興制作，立父子君臣以為紀綱。紀則有六，所謂諸父諸舅有善而有義，族人昆弟有敘而有親，以至師長朋友有尊而有舊也。紀之所在，禮莫大焉。綱則有三，所謂相臨而有君
translation_en:
…sacrifices: all these serve to spread ritual instruction in every direction. In the ancestral temple there are ritual officials and invocators; at court, the Three Dukes; and in the school, the Three Elders and Five Experienced Men. All elucidate ritual instruction to better the world. As for the ruler himself, he dwells among spirit mediums, scribes, blind musicians, and assistants, preserving the utmost rectitude. In this too he uses ritual to guard his own conduct and instruct the world by example. Such was the way the former kings taught through ritual and made themselves models. Thus, in the unseen realm they moved spirits, and in the visible realm they moved people, achieving the effect whereby like responds to like. Was this not fitting indeed?
“When the guiding bonds and ordering relationships are rectified, all under Heaven is firmly settled.”
Zhao Yi
Comment by Examiner Gao, Instructor: Taking the canonical commentary and annotations as his basis, he first sets out their meaning and develops his explanation in terms of ritual. There is elaboration, and the parts answer one another. An interpretation of the Classics such as this merits selection.
Comment by Examiner Ouyang, Instructor: He captures the meaning of Zixia’s words to Marquis Wen.
Only when ritual attains its proper order does the world attain the fullest measure of good government. Ritual is the great restraint upon the world: who could say that ritual might attain its proper order while the world remained ill-governed? Such was Zixia’s explanation of the origins of ancient music in his reply to Marquis Wen of Wei. His meaning was that the sage kings of old, proceeding from the great propriety of all under Heaven [?], instituted regulations and established the relationships of father and son, ruler and minister, as ordering relationships and guiding bonds. There are six ordering relationships: paternal uncles and maternal uncles are treated with goodness and righteousness; fellow clansmen and brothers, with due precedence and affection; and teachers and elders, and friends, with respect and regard for old ties. Wherever these ordering relationships obtain, nothing is greater than ritual. There are three guiding bonds: where one presides over another, there is a ruler…

title: 弘治十四年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
臣君則為臣之綱相生而有父子父則為子之
綱以至相聚而有夫婦夫則為妻之綱也綱之
所在禮莫踰焉紀焉既正其必行之族黨鄉里
無反無側井然而有條矣綱焉既正其必施之
朝廷閨門無偏無黨秩然而有序矣夫禮所以
定民志也今紀綱正矣則自東以西天下雖大
孰不在於範圍之中自南以北疆域雖廣孰有
出於維持之外遠近乂安無復有乖爭凌犯之
風而世臻於極治矣不謂之天下大定可乎內
===
外寧謐無復有搶攘搖杌之勢而時底於太平
矣不謂之天下大定得乎夫禮序於上而化成
於下如此古樂之所由以作也不在是歟大抵
樂不可苟作也必禮序而後可作禮不可徒制
也必治定而後可制此古之帝王始之以飾治
功而終之以贊化育其所由來者不易而所以
致用者匪輕也否則區區文具而已嗚呼後之
人主有比湯武而幾成康者猶謂治之隆替不
在禮樂而莫之究彼文侯何人斯而足以與此
punctuated:
臣，君則為臣之綱；相生而有父子，父則為子之綱；以至相聚而有夫婦，夫則為妻之綱也。綱之所在，禮莫踰焉。紀焉既正，其必行之族黨鄉里，無反無側，井然而有條矣；綱焉既正，其必施之朝廷閨門，無偏無黨，秩然而有序矣。夫禮所以定民志也。今紀綱正矣，則自東以西，天下雖大，孰不在於範圍之中？自南以北，疆域雖廣，孰有出於維持之外？遠近乂安，無復有乖爭凌犯之風，而世臻於極治矣，不謂之天下大定可乎？內外寧謐，無復有搶攘搖杌之勢，而時底於太平矣，不謂之天下大定得乎？夫禮序於上而化成於下如此，古樂之所由以作也，不在是歟？

大抵樂不可苟作也，必禮序而後可作；禮不可徒制也，必治定而後可制。此古之帝王始之以飾治功，而終之以贊化育，其所由來者不易，而所以致用者匪輕也。否則區區文具而已。嗚呼！後之人主有比湯武而幾成康者，猶謂治之隆替不在禮樂而莫之究，彼文侯何人斯，而足以與此
translation_en:
…and minister: the ruler serves as the guiding bond for the minister. Through generation there are father and son: the father serves as the guiding bond for the son. And through their union there are husband and wife: the husband serves as the guiding bond for the wife. Wherever these guiding bonds obtain, nothing takes precedence over ritual propriety. Once the organizing relationships are rectified, they must be practiced among clans, neighborhoods, and villages; without contrariness or deviation, all will be properly regulated. Once the guiding bonds are rectified, they must be applied at court and within the household; without partiality or faction, all will stand in due order. Ritual propriety is what settles the people's hearts. Now that these relationships and bonds are rectified, from east to west, vast though all under Heaven may be, who does not fall within their bounds? From south to north, broad though the realm may be, who falls outside their sustaining influence? Far and near are well governed and at peace; the habits of discord, contention, oppression, and encroachment cease, and the world attains the utmost good order. Could this fail to be called the great settlement of all under Heaven? Within and without, all is tranquil; the conditions of turmoil and instability cease, and the age reaches universal peace. Could this fail to be called the great settlement of all under Heaven? When ritual propriety is thus ordered above and moral transformation accomplished below, is this not precisely the basis on which the music of antiquity was created?

In general, music must not be created carelessly: only after ritual propriety is ordered may it be created. Ritual must not be instituted as an empty undertaking: only after good government is firmly established may it be instituted. Thus the emperors and kings of antiquity began by embellishing the achievements of government and ended by assisting the transforming and nurturing work of Heaven and Earth. What brought these rites and music into being was no easy matter, and the purposes they served were no trifling ones. Otherwise, they would amount merely to paltry formalities. Alas! Among later rulers there were those who matched Tang and Wu and approached Cheng and Kang, yet they still maintained that the flourishing or decline of government did not depend on rites and music, and failed to investigate them thoroughly. What sort of man, then, was Marquis Wen, that he should be capable of participating in this …

title: 弘治十四年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
子夏之言祗見其托迹於簡冊之間也噫
第貳場
論
孟子以道自任
楊士雲
同考試官訓導張批論題本以道字為重
而於時字亦不可輕過作者類多忽畧此篇
有發揚有歸宿筆力高古自是一家議論
得士如此可以為秋闈慶矣
===
同考試官教諭秦批寫出孟子以道自任之
意有挽萬鈞筆力于其善於論者
考試官教諭高批以時與力二字推孟子
心事曲盡無餘而議論滾滾無一句一字
不切當者可以為論矣
考試官教諭歐陽批是作議論淵源筆
力蒼健反覆曲折發盡程子道孟子
之意末復發出程子自任之意其亦
學焉而有得者歟
punctuated:
子夏之言，祗見其托迹於簡冊之間也。噫！

第貳場
論
孟子以道自任
楊士雲

同考試官訓導張批：論題本以道字為重，而於時字亦不可輕過。作者類多忽畧，此篇有發揚，有歸宿，筆力高古，自是一家議論。得士如此，可以為秋闈慶矣。

同考試官教諭秦批：寫出孟子以道自任之意，有挽萬鈞筆力，于其善於論者。

考試官教諭高批：以時與力二字推孟子心事，曲盡無餘，而議論滾滾，無一句一字不切當者，可以為論矣。

考試官教諭歐陽批：是作議論淵源，筆力蒼健，反覆曲折，發盡程子道孟子之意。末復發出程子自任之意，其亦學焉而有得者歟？
translation_en:
…As for Zixia’s words, we see only that they have left their traces among the written records. Alas!

Second Session
Discourse
“Mencius Took Responsibility for the Way upon Himself”
By Yang Shiyun

Comment by Associate Examiner Zhang, Assistant Instructor: The topic of this discourse places its principal emphasis on the word “Way,” but the word “timing” must not be passed over lightly either. Writers commonly overlook this. This essay develops its meaning and brings it to a firm conclusion. Its writing is lofty and antique in manner, and its argument has a distinctive voice of its own. To obtain a scholar like this is cause for celebration at the autumn Provincial Examination.

Comment by Associate Examiner Qin, Instructor: It brings out what it meant for Mencius to take responsibility for the Way upon himself. Its writing has the strength to pull a weight of ten thousand jun. He is among those skilled in discourse writing [?].

Comment by Examiner Gao, Instructor: Through the two words “timing” and “capacity,” it explores Mencius’s thoughts and concerns, bringing out every subtlety and leaving nothing unexpressed. Its arguments flow in abundance, yet not a single sentence or word is inappropriate. This may indeed be called a discourse.

Comment by Examiner Ouyang, Instructor: This work’s arguments have deep foundations, and its writing is vigorous and mature. Through repeated exploration and intricate turns, it fully brings out Master Cheng’s meaning in speaking of Mencius. At the end, it further brings out Master Cheng’s own sense of responsibility. Is its author not also someone who has gained understanding through study?

title: 弘治十四年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
理有出於衆人之所同而聖賢獨任之此
必有不得已者矣道之在天下非一人之
所得私也衆人與聖賢之所同也衆人與
聖賢同有之則固宜衆人之分任之也然
不可以徒任也力能任則任之時可任則
任之力不足而任者愚非其時而任者妄
有其力遭其時而諉於不任者畫三者聖
賢不由也然則以衆人之所同而聖賢獨
任之其心豈得已哉程子曰孟子以道自
===
任予於是有以知孟子之不得已者矣請
終言之斯道也何道也原於天而具於人
天下古今所共由之道也韓子所謂堯傳
之舜舜傳之禹禹傳之湯湯傳之文武周
公文武周公傳之孔子皆是物也孔子之
道顏子盖得之矣簞瓢陋巷自樂其樂恝
然若無與於斯道者何也當是時任之者
有孔子故也若時無孔子則顏子亦必將
駕其說於天下舍陋巷之安而授室於列
punctuated:
理有出於衆人之所同而聖賢獨任之，此必有不得已者矣。道之在天下，非一人之所得私也，衆人與聖賢之所同也。衆人與聖賢同有之，則固宜衆人之分任之也。然不可以徒任也：力能任則任之，時可任則任之。力不足而任者愚，非其時而任者妄，有其力、遭其時而諉於不任者畫。三者聖賢不由也。然則以衆人之所同而聖賢獨任之，其心豈得已哉？程子曰：「孟子以道自任。」予於是有以知孟子之不得已者矣。請終言之。
斯道也，何道也？原於天而具於人，天下古今所共由之道也。韓子所謂「堯傳之舜，舜傳之禹，禹傳之湯，湯傳之文武周公，文武周公傳之孔子」，皆是物也。孔子之道，顏子盖得之矣。簞瓢陋巷，自樂其樂，恝然若無與於斯道者，何也？當是時，任之者有孔子故也。若時無孔子，則顏子亦必將駕其說於天下，舍陋巷之安而授室於列
translation_en:
There are principles shared by all for which sages and worthies alone assume responsibility. There must be something that leaves them no alternative. The Way in the world is not something any one person may possess exclusively: it is shared by ordinary people and sages and worthies alike. Since they possess it in common, it is surely fitting that ordinary people should share responsibility for it. Yet one cannot assume this responsibility merely at will: one should undertake it when one has the strength to do so, and when the times permit it. To undertake it without sufficient strength is foolish; to undertake it at the wrong time is reckless; to have the strength and encounter the right time, yet evade the responsibility, is to set limits on oneself. Sages and worthies follow none of these three courses. Thus, when sages and worthies alone assume responsibility for what everyone shares, could they in their hearts do otherwise? Master Cheng said: “Mengzi took responsibility for the Way upon himself.” From this I have come to understand why Mengzi had no alternative. Allow me to explain this fully.
What Way is this? It is the Way that originates in Heaven and is inherent in human beings, the common path followed throughout the world, past and present. What Master Han described as “Yao transmitted it to Shun; Shun transmitted it to Yu; Yu transmitted it to Tang; Tang transmitted it to Wen, Wu, and the Duke of Zhou; Wen, Wu, and the Duke of Zhou transmitted it to Kongzi” is in every instance this same thing. Master Yan had surely attained Kongzi’s Way. With his basket of food and gourd of drink in a humble lane, he delighted in his own joy, seemingly unconcerned, as though he had no part in this Way. Why was this? Because at that time Kongzi was there to bear responsibility for it. Had there been no Kongzi then, Master Yan too would surely have carried his teachings throughout the world, relinquishing the peace of his humble lane to take up residence among the various…

title: 弘治十四年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
國去簞瓢之樂而傳食於諸侯即欲退焉
若愚以終其身不可得已孟子之得孔子
之道猶顏子也而其時則非顏子之時也
不遭顏子之時而欲樂顏子之樂是固無
賢者也何足以為孟子孟子之在當時盖
有以好辯譏之者矣其曉之之言曰予豈
好辯哉予不得已也夫孟子之好辯將以
明道也非苟以求勝於人而已也即求勝
於人亦求孔子之道勝也非求勝其私說
===
也故曰不直則道不見我且直之此孟子
之所為以道自任者也且孟子之時何時
也邪說橫流之時也邪說橫流壞人心術
其禍盖有不可勝言者孟子以命世亞聖
之才生當其時目擊其禍力足以任之而
不為之圖則安在其為聖賢也夫聖賢之
於眾人其性同也其性同則其道無不同
者然天之生聖賢非如眾人之泛泛然而
已也生一聖賢者將以眾人付之也天以
punctuated: 國，去簞瓢之樂而傳食於諸侯，即欲退焉，若愚以終其身，不可得已。孟子之得孔子之道，猶顏子也，而其時則非顏子之時也。不遭顏子之時，而欲樂顏子之樂，是固無賢者也，何足以為孟子？孟子之在當時，盖有以好辯譏之者矣。其曉之之言曰：「予豈好辯哉？予不得已也。」夫孟子之好辯，將以明道也，非苟以求勝於人而已也。即求勝於人，亦求孔子之道勝也，非求勝其私說也。故曰：「不直則道不見，我且直之。」此孟子之所為以道自任者也。且孟子之時何時也？邪說橫流之時也。邪說橫流，壞人心術，其禍盖有不可勝言者。孟子以命世亞聖之才，生當其時，目擊其禍，力足以任之而不為之圖，則安在其為聖賢也？夫聖賢之於眾人，其性同也，其性同則其道無不同者。然天之生聖賢，非如眾人之泛泛然而已也。生一聖賢者，將以眾人付之也。天以
translation_en: …states, abandon the joy of his rice basket and drinking gourd, and receive sustenance in turn from the feudal lords. Even if he wished to withdraw and spend his remaining years seeming foolish, he could not do so. Mengzi attained the Way of Kongzi just as Yanzi did, but his times were not Yanzi’s times. To wish to enjoy Yanzi’s joy without encountering Yanzi’s times would surely show no worthiness; how could that befit Mengzi? In his day, some indeed criticized Mengzi for his fondness for disputation. Explaining himself to them, he said: “Do I delight in disputation? I have no choice.” Mengzi’s disputation aimed to illuminate the Way, not merely to prevail over others. Even when he sought to prevail over others, he sought the triumph of Kongzi’s Way, not that of his own private doctrines. Thus he said: “Unless it is set straight, the Way will not be manifest. I shall set it straight.” This is how Mengzi took responsibility for the Way upon himself. Moreover, what sort of age was Mengzi’s? It was an age when heterodox doctrines ran rampant. These doctrines corrupted people’s hearts and intentions, bringing calamities beyond telling. Mengzi, endowed with the talents of an epochal figure and Second Sage, was born into that age and witnessed its calamities. If, possessing the strength to shoulder this responsibility, he had made no effort to address them, wherein would his sageliness and worthiness have lain? Sages and worthies share the same nature as ordinary people; since their nature is the same, their Way must likewise be the same. Yet Heaven does not bring forth sages and worthies merely to live undistinguished lives like ordinary people. In bringing forth a sage or worthy, Heaven intends to entrust ordinary people to him. Heaven takes…

title: 弘治十四年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
衆人付之聖賢則聖賢視之猶一體也而
顧為獨善之計可乎今夫道路之間有遺
物焉其重百鈞問之路之人皆曰是烏獲
之物也過者日千百人力不能舉皆委而
去之不顧也烏獲過之而認得為己物將
委而去之乎抑亦舉而歸之其家乎孟子
之於道其認之也何以異此吾道之重不
啻百鈞而亦非孟子之所得私者然孔子
之嫡傳在孟子由孟子認之固若己物然
===
今而害於邪說之橫流則其為道路之遺
也久矣其私以為己任者政以舉其故物
耳而况其力又足以任之者乎其所以任
之者何也距楊墨也息邪說也當孟子時
邪說之害道者不止楊墨而楊墨為甚故
其距之最嚴其意以為人之所以為人者
以其有君父也孔子之道所以為正者以
其有仁義也楊氏為我是無君也墨氏兼
愛是無父也無父則不仁無君則不義不
punctuated: 衆人付之聖賢，則聖賢視之猶一體也，而顧為獨善之計，可乎？今夫道路之間有遺物焉，其重百鈞，問之路之人，皆曰：「是烏獲之物也。」過者日千百人，力不能舉，皆委而去之，不顧也。烏獲過之，而認得為己物，將委而去之乎？抑亦舉而歸之其家乎？孟子之於道，其認之也，何以異此？吾道之重，不啻百鈞，而亦非孟子之所得私者。然孔子之嫡傳在孟子，由孟子認之，固若己物然。今而害於邪說之橫流，則其為道路之遺也久矣。其私以為己任者，政以舉其故物耳，而况其力又足以任之者乎？其所以任之者何也？距楊墨也，息邪說也。當孟子時，邪說之害道者不止楊墨，而楊墨為甚，故其距之最嚴。其意以為，人之所以為人者，以其有君父也；孔子之道所以為正者，以其有仁義也。楊氏為我，是無君也；墨氏兼愛，是無父也。無父則不仁，無君則不義。不
translation_en:
…the multitude to the sages and worthies, then the sages and worthies regard them as forming one body with themselves. Could they nevertheless concern themselves only with perfecting their own virtue? Suppose an object lies abandoned along a road, weighing a hundred jun. When people on the road are asked about it, they all say, “This belongs to Wu Huo.” Hundreds or thousands pass it each day, but none has the strength to lift it; all leave it behind without another glance. If Wu Huo passes and recognizes it as his own, will he leave it behind? Or will he lift it and take it home? How does Mengzi’s recognition of the Way differ from this? The weight of our Way is far greater than a hundred jun, and it is something Mengzi could not possess exclusively. Yet the direct transmission of Kongzi’s teaching rested with Mengzi; when Mengzi recognized it as his responsibility, it was indeed as though it were his own possession.

Now that the Way had suffered from the unchecked spread of heterodox doctrines, it had long lain like an abandoned object on the road. In personally taking it as his responsibility, he was simply lifting up what had always been his own. How much more was this incumbent upon him when his strength was sufficient to bear it! How did he shoulder this responsibility? By opposing Yang Zhu and Mo Di and putting an end to heterodox doctrines. In Mengzi’s time, the heterodox doctrines that harmed the Way were not confined to those of Yang Zhu and Mo Di, but theirs were the most harmful; hence he opposed them most sternly. His reasoning was that what makes human beings human is their recognition of ruler and father, and what makes Kongzi’s Way correct is its benevolence and righteousness. Yang Zhu’s doctrine of acting for oneself amounts to acknowledging no ruler; Mo Di’s doctrine of universal love amounts to acknowledging no father. To acknowledge no father is to lack benevolence; to acknowledge no ruler is to lack righteousness. Lacking…

title: 弘治十四年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
仁不義則其去禽獸不遠矣使楊墨而非
人也則可楊墨亦人耳顧乃陷於禽獸而
不自知又以引吾同道之人使我坐視其
禍而不之救是縱之也助之也其去楊墨
幾何哉昌言極論必使天下之人曉然知
楊墨之害而後已楊墨之道息則孔子之
道著矣其他異端曲說私智小數凡可以
病吾正道者一一辭而闢之以塞其源若
為並耕之說者闢之為義外之說者闢之
===
為善戰之說者闢之為連諸侯之說者闢
之闢乎彼所以衞乎此也其惡之也切故
其闢之也嚴其任之也重故其衞之也力
於乎孟子之有功於斯道也大矣夫孟子
之功固大矣而其不得已之故則非知道
之君子有不能真知之者蓋其所遭之時
與其所賦之才力皆有不容不任焉者故
也使其幸而得為孔子之徒則陋巷之樂
當與顏子同之此任固無與也又不然使
punctuated:
仁不義，則其去禽獸不遠矣。使楊墨而非人也，則可；楊墨亦人耳，顧乃陷於禽獸而不自知，又以引吾同道之人。使我坐視其禍而不之救，是縱之也，助之也，其去楊墨幾何哉？昌言極論，必使天下之人曉然知楊墨之害而後已。楊墨之道息，則孔子之道著矣。其他異端曲說、私智小數，凡可以病吾正道者，一一辭而闢之，以塞其源。若為並耕之說者，闢之；為義外之說者，闢之；為善戰之說者，闢之；為連諸侯之說者，闢之。闢乎彼，所以衞乎此也。其惡之也切，故其闢之也嚴；其任之也重，故其衞之也力。
於乎！孟子之有功於斯道也大矣！夫孟子之功固大矣，而其不得已之故，則非知道之君子，有不能真知之者。蓋其所遭之時與其所賦之才力，皆有不容不任焉者故也。使其幸而得為孔子之徒，則陋巷之樂，當與顏子同之，此任固無與也。又不然，使
translation_en:
…without benevolence or righteousness, they are not far removed from birds and beasts. If Yang Zhu and Mo Di were not human, that might be permissible; but Yang and Mo are human too. Yet they have sunk to the level of birds and beasts without realizing it, and further draw into this condition those who share our Way. Were I to sit by watching this calamity without rescuing them, I would be indulging them and assisting them. How far removed would I then be from Yang and Mo? He spoke out openly and argued to the utmost, refusing to stop until everyone under Heaven clearly understood the harm caused by Yang and Mo. Once their teachings subsided, the Way of Kongzi would become manifest. As for other heterodox doctrines and distorted arguments, self-serving cleverness and petty devices—anything capable of harming our correct Way—he refuted and rejected each in turn, thereby blocking its source. Those who advocated that rulers till the fields alongside their people, he refuted; those who maintained that righteousness was external, he refuted; those who advocated skill in warfare, he refuted; and those who advocated forming alliances among the feudal lords, he refuted. Refuting those doctrines was how he defended this Way. Because his abhorrence of them was intense, his refutations were stern; because his responsibility was weighty, his defense was vigorous.
Ah! Great indeed was Mengzi’s service to this Way! His achievement was certainly great, yet unless one is a gentleman who understands the Way, one may fail truly to comprehend why he had no choice but to act. For both the age in which he lived and the abilities with which he was endowed made it impossible for him not to undertake this responsibility. Had he been fortunate enough to become a disciple of Kongzi, he would have shared with Master Yan the joy of living in a humble lane; this responsibility would assuredly not have fallen to him. Or, failing that, if…

title: 弘治十四年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
使顏子與之並生於戰國則孟子猶有可
諉者亦將退焉若愚以終其身而已耳今
孔顏既不可作而旁觀一世之人其才力
又皆無足與於斯者然則孟子不以身任
之而欲諉之誰哉故程子之言不徒曰任
道而必曰自任而又曰以道自任任者如
有所負而不釋之辭自者獨致其力而不
容人參之之辭以者如物在手而左右之
之辭非孟子之識時以察其幾量力以致
===
其決其孰能與於此哉程子生於千四百
年之後而推尊之如此其可謂深知孟子
之心者矣雖然斯言也程子非獨為孟子
發也蓋亦有自狀之意存焉程子之道上
接孟子之傳者也自孟子後以道自任者
非斯人吾誰與歸
表
擬宋龍圖閣直學士趙汝愚進名臣奏議
表〔淳熙十三年〕
punctuated:
使顏子與之並生於戰國，則孟子猶有可諉者，亦將退焉，若愚以終其身而已耳。今孔顏既不可作，而旁觀一世之人，其才力又皆無足與於斯者，然則孟子不以身任之，而欲諉之誰哉？故程子之言，不徒曰任道，而必曰自任，而又曰以道自任。任者，如有所負而不釋之辭；自者，獨致其力而不容人參之之辭；以者，如物在手而左右之之辭。非孟子之識時以察其幾，量力以致其決，其孰能與於此哉？程子生於千四百年之後，而推尊之如此，其可謂深知孟子之心者矣。雖然，斯言也，程子非獨為孟子發也，蓋亦有自狀之意存焉。程子之道，上接孟子之傳者也。自孟子後，以道自任者，非斯人，吾誰與歸？

表

擬宋龍圖閣直學士趙汝愚進名臣奏議表〔淳熙十三年〕
translation_en:
…If Master Yan had lived alongside him in the Warring States period, Mengzi would still have had someone to whom he could entrust this responsibility. He too would then have withdrawn, appearing foolish, and simply passed the rest of his life that way. But Kongzi and Master Yan could no longer be brought back, and, surveying the people of his age, he found none whose talents and powers were sufficient to share in this undertaking. If Mengzi did not assume the responsibility himself, to whom could he entrust it? Thus Master Cheng did not merely speak of “taking responsibility for the Way”; he insisted on saying “taking responsibility oneself,” and further, “taking responsibility for the Way upon oneself.” “Taking responsibility” conveys bearing a burden without laying it down. “Oneself” conveys devoting one’s own powers alone, without allowing another to share the task. “For” conveys having something in hand and directing it. Without Mengzi’s understanding of his times, through which he discerned their incipient tendencies, and his assessment of his own powers, through which he reached a firm resolve, who could have attained this? Master Cheng lived fourteen hundred years later, yet revered him so highly: he may indeed be said to have understood Mengzi’s heart profoundly. Nevertheless, Master Cheng did not utter these words solely about Mengzi; they also contain an intention to describe himself. Master Cheng’s Way carried forward the transmission from Mengzi. Among those who took responsibility for the Way upon themselves after Mengzi, if not this man, whom should I follow?

Memorial

A memorial composed in the person of Zhao Ruyu, Auxiliary Academician of the Longtu Pavilion under the Song, presenting Memorials of Eminent Ministers.〔Thirteenth year of Chunxi [1186].〕

title: 弘治十四年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
王仲仁
同考試官教諭王批造語精而用事核
表製佳矣
考試官教諭高批得宋臣忠愛意
考試官教諭歐陽批詞語醇正得四六
之體可嘉
伏以
責難陳善懋昭建極之休納諫聽言丕闡
用中之懿義雖出於往古文則述於
===
先朝竊惟治道之盛衰寔關言路之通塞堯設
諫鼓聿臻於變之風武置戒鼗爰致永清
之化自時厥後理亂相尋循之則興違之
則壞粤稽
祖宗之立法固於諫諍而留心增置諫員大振
敢言之氣崇獎直節深懷不諱之朝許給
舍以封還責侍從以獻納故當時之士咸
思學古通經而投匭之章皆欲惠民保國
顧往事之可為法戒即今日之在所依歸
punctuated:
王仲仁

同考試官教諭王批：造語精而用事核，表製佳矣。
考試官教諭高批：得宋臣忠愛意。
考試官教諭歐陽批：詞語醇正，得四六之體，可嘉。

伏以：責難陳善，懋昭建極之休；納諫聽言，丕闡用中之懿。義雖出於往古，文則述於先朝。竊惟治道之盛衰，寔關言路之通塞。堯設諫鼓，聿臻於變之風；武置戒鼗，爰致永清之化。自時厥後，理亂相尋，循之則興，違之則壞。粤稽祖宗之立法，固於諫諍而留心。增置諫員，大振敢言之氣；崇獎直節，深懷不諱之朝。許給舍以封還，責侍從以獻納。故當時之士，咸思學古通經；而投匭之章，皆欲惠民保國。顧往事之可為法戒，即今日之在所依歸。
translation_en:
Wang Zhongren

Comment by Associate Examiner Wang, Instructor: “The phrasing is refined and the historical references accurate. This is a fine memorial.”
Comment by Examiner Gao, Instructor: “It captures the loyal devotion of a Song minister.”
Comment by Examiner Ouyang, Instructor: “The language is pure and correct, and conforms to the style of four-and-six parallel prose. Commendable.”

I humbly submit: By urging the sovereign to undertake difficult duties and setting forth what is good, ministers splendidly manifest the excellence of establishing the supreme standard; by accepting remonstrance and heeding counsel, the sovereign greatly displays the virtue of applying the mean. Although these principles originated in remote antiquity, the writings expounding them were composed under earlier reigns.

I venture to reflect that the flourishing or decline of good government truly depends upon whether the channels of counsel are open or blocked. Yao established a drum for remonstrance, thereby bringing about a transformation of the people's ways; King Wu provided a warning rattle-drum, thereby achieving the civilizing influence of lasting peace. Thereafter, order and disorder succeeded one another: following this course brought prosperity, while departing from it brought ruin.

Examining the institutions established by Your Majesty's imperial ancestors, we find that they indeed gave careful attention to remonstrance. They increased the number of remonstrance officials, greatly encouraging the spirit of speaking boldly; they honored and rewarded upright integrity, earnestly cherishing the ideal of a court where nothing need be left unsaid. They permitted Supervising Secretaries and Secretariat Drafters to return imperial directives under seal, and charged attendant officials with presenting counsel. Thus the scholars of those times all aspired to study antiquity and master the Classics, while the memorials deposited in the petition boxes all sought to benefit the people and safeguard the state. The events of the past that can serve as models and warnings are precisely what we should look to for guidance today.

title: 弘治十四年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
因粹成百餘卷之書亦既閱二十年之久
分門列類則自君道而訖邊防據事繫時
則由
欽宗而泝
藝祖豈但易求政事得失之跡盖亦可推
國家隆替之由顧効力於涓埃曷叩塵於
進御恭惟
〇〇〇〇孝隆
德壽澤洽黔黎圖作敬天恐起居之或懈禮嚴
===
敵國猶恢復之靡忘肆寤寐以思賢恒優
容而受諫惟哲后多求古訓而聖人不棄
邇言彼充棟之藏萬幾諒未暇及若連屏
之繪一目則已無遺妄意此書殊切人主
臣身違
象魏心係
龍墀才不如徵莫紀帝王之政忠惟慕相敢
陳晁董之文伏願
鑒此辛勤
punctuated:
因粹成百餘卷之書，亦既閱二十年之久。分門列類，則自君道而訖邊防；據事繫時，則由欽宗而泝藝祖。豈但易求政事得失之跡，盖亦可推國家隆替之由。顧効力於涓埃，曷叩塵於進御？
恭惟〇〇〇〇孝隆德壽，澤洽黔黎；圖作敬天，恐起居之或懈；禮嚴敵國，猶恢復之靡忘。肆寤寐以思賢，恒優容而受諫。惟哲后多求古訓，而聖人不棄邇言。彼充棟之藏，萬幾諒未暇及；若連屏之繪，一目則已無遺。妄意此書殊切人主。臣身違象魏，心係龍墀；才不如徵，莫紀帝王之政；忠惟慕相，敢陳晁董之文。伏願鑒此辛勤。
translation_en:
…I therefore compiled a work of more than a hundred juan, a task that has taken twenty years. Arranged by subject and category, it extends from the ruler’s way to frontier defense; attaching events to their dates, it traces backward from Qinzong to Yizu, the dynastic founder. It not only makes the evidence of successes and failures in government readily accessible, but also enables one to deduce the causes of the state’s flourishing and decline. Hoping to contribute even a minute measure of service, how might I venture to submit it for imperial perusal [?]?
I reverently consider that Your Majesty [four circles in the transcription] displays exalted filial devotion toward Deshou [?], and that your beneficence reaches the common people. You have had a picture made concerning reverence for Heaven [?], fearing any lapse in your daily conduct; although rigorously observing diplomatic propriety toward the rival state, you never forget the recovery of lost territory. Thus, waking and sleeping, you think of worthy men, and constantly receive remonstrance with generous tolerance. An enlightened sovereign seeks instruction widely from antiquity, and a sage does not discard commonplace words. Amid your myriad affairs, you surely have no leisure to consult collections that fill whole buildings; yet, as with pictures across adjoining screens, a single glance can encompass everything here. I presumptuously believe that this book is especially pertinent to a ruler.
Your servant’s person is far from the palace gate towers, but his heart remains bound to the imperial steps. My talents fall short of Zheng’s, and I cannot record the governance of emperors and kings; in loyalty I aspire only to emulate Xiang, and venture to present the writings of Chao and Dong. I humbly beg that you look upon these painstaking labors…

title: 弘治十四年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
留神乙覽不必泛求而寡要但常致力以精
思對
列聖於遺編當有因往知來之益屈群策而決
事不效尋章摘句之為用躋世道於昇平
以復
祖宗之隆盛臣無任瞻
天仰
聖激切屏營之至謹以所撰皇朝名臣奏議一
百五十卷奉
===
表隨
進以
聞
第叁塲
策
第一問
楊士雲
同考試官訓導張批寫出
聖祖創治之難頌
punctuated:
留神乙覽，不必泛求而寡要，但常致力以精思。對列聖於遺編，當有因往知來之益；屈群策而決事，不效尋章摘句之為。用躋世道於昇平，以復祖宗之隆盛。臣無任瞻天仰聖、激切屏營之至，謹以所撰《皇朝名臣奏議》一百五十卷，奉表隨進以聞。
第叁塲
策
第一問
楊士雲
同考試官訓導張批：寫出聖祖創治之難，頌
translation_en:
…bestow Your attention upon it in Your imperial reading. There is no need to search broadly while missing the essentials; rather, continually apply Yourself to careful reflection. Encountering the successive sage emperors in the writings they left behind, You will gain insight into the future through knowledge of the past. Drawing upon the various counsels to decide affairs, do not imitate those who merely hunt out passages and extract phrases. Thereby bring the realm to peace and prosperity and restore the flourishing greatness of Your ancestors. Your servant, gazing toward Heaven and looking up to Your Sagely Majesty, cannot contain his fervent emotion and trembling awe. I respectfully submit the work I have compiled, Memorials of Eminent Ministers of the Imperial Dynasty, in 150 juan, together with this memorial, for Your Majesty’s attention.
Third Session
Policy Essay

Yang Shiyun
