title: 弘治十四年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
誥之意粲然有章足見所學
同考試官教諭秦批
聖製一策敷荅詳盡斷制明白真策手也
考試官教諭高批
皇祖與湯武時勢之難易化導之異同士子間知其畧然未有如
此卷敷陳具盡者况他策俱稱魁多士知
無愧矣
考試官教諭歐陽批
聖祖創造之難垂訓之意揄揚殆盡其服膺而有得者歟
===
知我
聖祖定天下之難當知我
聖祖致太平之難盖武功以定天下文教以致
太平此湯武與我
聖祖之所同也時異勢殊道有升降取之既難
化之亦不易此我
聖祖與湯武之所以異也知乎此則
聖神功德之盛庶可窺其萬一矣請因明問而
敬對之自古大亂之後必有聖人起而掃
punctuated:
誥之意，粲然有章，足見所學。
同考試官教諭秦批：聖製一策，敷荅詳盡，斷制明白，真策手也。
考試官教諭高批：皇祖與湯武時勢之難易、化導之異同，士子間知其畧，然未有如此卷敷陳具盡者。况他策俱稱，魁多士知無愧矣。
考試官教諭歐陽批：聖祖創造之難、垂訓之意，揄揚殆盡，其服膺而有得者歟？
知我聖祖定天下之難，當知我聖祖致太平之難。盖武功以定天下，文教以致太平，此湯武與我聖祖之所同也。時異勢殊，道有升降，取之既難，化之亦不易，此我聖祖與湯武之所以異也。知乎此，則聖神功德之盛，庶可窺其萬一矣。請因明問而敬對之。自古大亂之後，必有聖人起而掃
translation_en:
…the meaning of the proclamations is brilliantly and coherently expressed, amply demonstrating his learning.
Associate Examiner Qin, Instructor, comments: “In the essay responding to the imperially composed policy question, the exposition and response are thorough, and the judgments clear. He is truly an adept at policy essays.”
Examiner Gao, Instructor, comments: “Among the candidates, some know the broad outlines of the relative difficulties of the times and circumstances faced by our imperial ancestor and by Tang and Wu, and of the similarities and differences in their transforming and guiding the people. Yet none has set these out as fully as this script. Moreover, his other policy essays are all of comparable quality; he may deservedly rank foremost among the candidates [?].”
Examiner Ouyang, Instructor, comments: “He has almost exhaustively extolled the difficulty of the sagely ancestor’s founding achievement and the intent of the teachings he bequeathed. Has he not taken them to heart and gained understanding from them?”
To understand the difficulty with which our sagely ancestor pacified All-under-Heaven, one must understand the difficulty with which he brought about Great Peace. Military achievements serve to pacify All-under-Heaven, while civil instruction serves to bring about Great Peace: this is what Tang and Wu shared with our sagely ancestor. Yet their times differed and their circumstances were distinct; the Way rose and declined. Winning the realm was difficult, and transforming its people was no easy matter either: this is where our sagely ancestor differed from Tang and Wu. If one understands this, one may perhaps glimpse a ten-thousandth part of the greatness of his sagely and divine achievements and virtue. Allow me respectfully to respond to your illuminating question. Since antiquity, after great disorder, a sage has invariably arisen to sweep away…

title: 弘治十四年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
除其禍若湯之放桀武王之伐紂皆神武
不殺一怒而安天下之民者然其為功則
未有若我
太祖之難者也是故夏之德衰于桀成湯于是
乎有鳴條之役罪人既黜則兆民允殖矣
未聞放桀之後復别有所攻伐也商之德
衰于紂武王于是乎有牧野之師凶殘既
取則四海永清矣未聞伐紂之後復别有
所戡定也元政不綱群雄訌亂驅烏合之
衆逞鴟張之威淫名僭號相望于天下甲
僨而乙起東討而西叛恣為荼毒賊我良
民時勢之難為未有甚于此時者也我
太祖以江淮聖人應運而起恭天成命伐暴救
民一征而顛賊亮再征而搘偽吳三征而
披閩粵四征而卷齊魯遂擣元都掇秦晋
掀巴蜀復中國帝王所自立之地况不階
寸土一民呼吸響應以成大業簡冊所載
未之前聞較之資亳衆以興師藉西師而
punctuated: 除其禍。若湯之放桀、武王之伐紂，皆神武不殺，一怒而安天下之民者。然其為功，則未有若我太祖之難者也。是故夏之德衰于桀，成湯于是乎有鳴條之役；罪人既黜，則兆民允殖矣。未聞放桀之後，復别有所攻伐也。商之德衰于紂，武王于是乎有牧野之師；凶殘既取，則四海永清矣。未聞伐紂之後，復别有所戡定也。元政不綱，群雄訌亂，驅烏合之衆，逞鴟張之威，淫名僭號，相望于天下。甲僨而乙起，東討而西叛，恣為荼毒，賊我良民。時勢之難為，未有甚于此時者也。我太祖以江淮聖人應運而起，恭天成命，伐暴救民。一征而顛賊亮，再征而搘偽吳，三征而披閩粵，四征而卷齊魯，遂擣元都，掇秦晋，掀巴蜀，復中國帝王所自立之地。况不階寸土一民，呼吸響應，以成大業，簡冊所載，未之前聞。較之資亳衆以興師、藉西師而
translation_en:
…eliminate its calamities. Tang’s banishment of Jie and King Wu’s campaign against Zhou were both instances of divine martial power that did not resort to killing: a single outburst of wrath brought peace to the people of the realm. Yet neither accomplished his deeds under difficulties comparable to those faced by our Taizu. Thus, when the virtue of Xia declined under Jie, Cheng Tang fought the battle of Mingtiao. Once the guilty ruler had been expelled, the myriad people truly flourished. We have never heard that, after banishing Jie, he had further campaigns to undertake. When the virtue of Shang declined under Zhou, King Wu deployed his army at Muye. Once the cruel tyrant had been captured, all within the Four Seas enjoyed lasting peace. We have never heard that, after campaigning against Zhou, he had further territories to pacify.

The Yuan government lost its governing order, and rival strongmen stirred up strife and disorder. Driving their motley crowds before them and flaunting their overbearing power, they assumed extravagant titles and usurped sovereign designations, appearing everywhere throughout the realm. One fell and another arose; while an expedition went east, rebellion broke out in the west. They inflicted suffering without restraint and preyed upon our good people. Never had circumstances been more difficult to deal with than at this time. Our Taizu arose in response to Heaven’s appointed destiny as the sage of the Jiang–Huai region. Reverently obeying Heaven’s settled mandate, he attacked the violent and rescued the people. In his first campaign he overthrew the rebel Liang; in his second he subdued [?] the illegitimate Wu regime; in his third he swept through Min and Yue; in his fourth he overran Qi and Lu. He then struck the Yuan capital, seized Qin and Jin, swept through Ba and Shu, and recovered the lands in which the emperors and kings of the Central Realm had established themselves. Moreover, he began without so much as an inch of territory or a single subject to build upon; people responded to his call as swiftly as an echo, enabling him to accomplish his great undertaking. Nothing like this had previously been heard of in the historical records. Compared with those who drew upon the people of Bo to raise an army, or relied upon an army from the west to…

title: 弘治十四年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
舉事者其難易又何如也嗚呼盛矣
祖訓有曰羣雄之強盛至難服也而朕以服之
觀于此豈不益信矣乎自古帝王之興必
有施命以告天下若成湯之誕告萬方武
王之明大命于妹邦皆渙其大號風動而
教化之者然其為教亦未有若我
太祖之難者也是故當桀之時同惡相濟者雖
有其人然止于簡賢附勢者耳其餘則皆
良民也故成湯之誥無費詞商之餘民染
===
紂之惡者亦不過妹土之人耳其他故家
遺俗尚多有之故武王之誥專妹土元以
夷狄入主中國變我綱常汙我衣冠盡天
下之民耳濡目染日改月化相率而為鳥
獸之羣者幾百年教化之難行未有甚于
此時者也我
太祖用夏變夷駸駸至于十八九年之後其風
猶未盡革于是有
三編之誥頒示天下一不已而至于再再不已
punctuated:
舉事者，其難易又何如也？嗚呼，盛矣！《祖訓》有曰：「羣雄之強盛，至難服也，而朕以服之。」觀于此，豈不益信矣乎？
自古帝王之興，必有施命以告天下。若成湯之誕告萬方，武王之明大命于妹邦，皆渙其大號，風動而教化之者。然其為教，亦未有若我太祖之難者也。是故當桀之時，同惡相濟者雖有其人，然止于簡賢附勢者耳，其餘則皆良民也，故成湯之誥無費詞。商之餘民，染紂之惡者，亦不過妹土之人耳，其他故家遺俗尚多有之，故武王之誥專妹土。元以夷狄入主中國，變我綱常，汙我衣冠，盡天下之民耳濡目染，日改月化，相率而為鳥獸之羣者幾百年。教化之難行，未有甚于此時者也。我太祖用夏變夷，駸駸至于十八九年之後，其風猶未盡革。于是有三編之誥，頒示天下，一不已而至于再，再不已
translation_en:
…those who launched their enterprises—how did the difficulty or ease of their undertaking compare with his? Ah, how magnificent! The Ancestral Instructions says: “The rival warlords were powerful and exceedingly difficult to subdue, yet I subdued them.” Looking at this, can we fail to believe it all the more firmly?
Since antiquity, whenever emperors and kings arose, they invariably issued commands to proclaim their will to all under Heaven. Thus Cheng Tang made his great announcement to the myriad regions, and King Wu made the great mandate clear in the land of Mei. Both disseminated their great proclamations, moving the people like the wind and transforming them through instruction. Yet none faced such difficulties in teaching the people as did our Taizu. In Jie’s time, there were indeed men who aided one another in wrongdoing, but they were confined to those who scorned the worthy and attached themselves to the powerful. The rest were all good people, so Cheng Tang’s announcement required no lengthy wording. Among the surviving people of Shang, those tainted by Zhou’s wickedness were likewise merely the people of Mei. Elsewhere, many old families and inherited customs still remained, so King Wu’s announcement concerned Mei alone. The Yuan, as barbarians, entered and ruled the Central Kingdom, altering our fundamental human relationships and constant moral principles, and defiling our robes and caps. Throughout the realm, the people absorbed these influences through what they heard and saw, changing day by day and month by month, and leading one another into becoming flocks of birds and beasts for nearly a hundred years. Never had it been harder to put moral instruction into effect than at this time. Our Taizu used the ways of Chinese civilization to transform the barbarians. Yet even after eighteen or nineteen years had swiftly passed, their customs had still not been entirely reformed. Thus the three compilations of the Grand Pronouncements were promulgated throughout the realm. The first did not suffice, so there was a second; the second did not suffice…

title: 弘治十四年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
而至于三如父母臨之師保誨之必欲與
斯世同躋于皇極之五福而後已其曰申
明五常即克綏厥猷之旨也其曰為民造
福即輯寧邦家之心也其曰誥如擒惡受
賞即群飲勿佚盡執拘以歸于周之說也
其曰輕生易死復出
三誥以示之即勿庸殺之姑惟教之之意也勝
殘去殺已見於創業之時禮樂可興不待
於繼世之後於乎盛矣
===
祖訓又曰民經世亂務習奸猾至難齊也而朕
已齊之觀于此又豈不益信矣乎夫湯武
皆古聖人也其功德之盛復何間然顧其
所遇之時視我
聖祖則有不同焉者此我
聖祖之所以為難也百三十餘年來至于今日
天下之民皆得以安養于大順大化之域
優游于遵道遵義之天者果誰之力歟用
之而不知習之而不察者此凡民也非豪
punctuated:
而至于三，如父母臨之，師保誨之，必欲與斯世同躋于皇極之五福而後已。其曰「申明五常」，即「克綏厥猷」之旨也；其曰「為民造福」，即「輯寧邦家」之心也；其曰「誥如擒惡受賞」，即「群飲勿佚，盡執拘以歸于周」之說也；其曰「輕生易死」，復出三誥以示之，即「勿庸殺之，姑惟教之」之意也。勝殘去殺，已見於創業之時；禮樂可興，不待於繼世之後。於乎盛矣！
《祖訓》又曰：「民經世亂，務習奸猾，至難齊也，而朕已齊之。」觀于此，又豈不益信矣乎？夫湯武皆古聖人也，其功德之盛，復何間然？顧其所遇之時，視我聖祖，則有不同焉者。此我聖祖之所以為難也。百三十餘年來，至于今日，天下之民皆得以安養于大順大化之域，優游于遵道遵義之天者，果誰之力歟？用之而不知，習之而不察者，此凡民也，非豪
translation_en:
…and proceeded to a third. He watched over them as a parent and instructed them as a teacher and guardian, determined not to rest until he and the people of this age together attained the five blessings of the August Ultimate. His injunction to “reaffirm the Five Constant Virtues” expresses the purport of “being able to establish their proper way.” His injunction to “create blessings for the people” expresses the intent of “bringing peace to the state and its households.” His words, “the Announcement, as [?], apprehending evildoers and receiving rewards,” convey the teaching: “Do not let those who drink in groups escape; arrest and bind them all and bring them back to Zhou.” His reference to “holding life cheap and lightly courting death,” followed by his issuing the Three Announcements to instruct them, conveys the intent of “not putting them to death, but for the time being teaching them.” The overcoming of brutality and the elimination of killing were already evident during the founding of the dynasty; rites and music could flourish without awaiting the reigns of his successors. Ah, how magnificent!
The Ancestral Instructions further states: “The people have lived through disorder in the realm and devoted themselves to deceit and cunning. They are exceedingly difficult to bring into order, yet I have brought them into order.” In light of this, how could we fail to believe these words all the more firmly? Tang and Wu were both sages of antiquity. What fault could one possibly find with the greatness of their achievements and virtue? Yet the circumstances of their times differed from those encountered by our sagely ancestor. This is what made our sagely ancestor’s task so difficult. For more than one hundred and thirty years, down to the present day, the people throughout the realm have all been able to live securely and prosper within a domain of supreme harmony and moral transformation, at ease beneath a heaven where the Way and righteousness are followed. Whose efforts, indeed, have made this possible? Those who benefit from it without knowing it, and grow accustomed to it without examining it, are ordinary people, not outstanding…

title: 弘治十四年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
傑之士也愚也何敢自擬于豪傑執事倘
與其進尚能歌猗那之詩誦下武之章以
揚厲
神功聖德于商周之世
第二問
楊敷頥
同考試官學正王批具事核立詞正讀之
令人起敬其亦兩省之傑者
考試官教諭高批西京人才枚數幾盡
===
而評品亦當是真尚友者乎可敬
考試官教諭歐陽批古帝王用賢圖治子能
一二品第言之亦可以覘子之所養矣
帝王之治世必資乎賢而賢才之行誼當
究其實蓋君以臣興臣以君出名以實著
實以名求也然欲評品其高下不於行誼
之實其何以哉執事發策下詢承學請勉
對其萬一粤稽諸古虞舜之帝也雖曰以
玄德之升聞而其所以致風動之休則有
punctuated:
傑之士也。愚也何敢自擬于豪傑？執事倘與其進，尚能歌《猗那》之詩，誦《下武》之章，以揚厲神功聖德于商周之世。
第二問
楊敷頥
同考試官學正王批：具事核，立詞正，讀之令人起敬，其亦兩省之傑者。
考試官教諭高批：西京人才，枚數幾盡，而評品亦當，是真尚友者乎！可敬。
考試官教諭歐陽批：古帝王用賢圖治，子能一二品第言之，亦可以覘子之所養矣。
帝王之治世，必資乎賢，而賢才之行誼，當究其實。蓋君以臣興，臣以君出，名以實著，實以名求也。然欲評品其高下，不於行誼之實，其何以哉？執事發策下詢，承學請勉對其萬一。粤稽諸古，虞舜之帝也，雖曰以玄德之升聞，而其所以致風動之休，則有
translation_en:
…men of outstanding talent. How could I, in my ignorance, dare compare myself with such men? If you, honored examiners, should approve my advancement, I could yet sing the ode “Ah, How Splendid” (Yi na) and recite “Following in the Martial Footsteps” (Xia wu), thereby extolling the divine achievements and sagely virtue alongside those of the Shang and Zhou ages.
Second Policy Question
Yang Fuyi
Comment by Associate Examiner Wang, Instructor: “The facts he adduces are well substantiated, and his wording is upright. Reading it inspires respect. He is indeed an outstanding talent of the two provinces.”
Comment by Examiner Gao, Instructor: “He enumerates nearly all the talented men of the Western Han, and his assessments are also fitting. Is he not truly one who befriends the worthies of antiquity? Admirable.”
Comment by Examiner Ouyang, Instructor: “You can discuss and rank, one by one, the worthy men whom ancient emperors and kings employed in seeking good government. This also gives us a glimpse of your own cultivation.”
Emperors and kings must rely upon worthy men to govern the world, and the actual conduct of such men must be investigated. For rulers flourish through their ministers, and ministers come forth through their rulers; reputation becomes manifest through substance, and substance is sought through reputation. Yet if one wishes to assess and rank them, on what could one rely other than the substance of their conduct? You, honored examiners, have issued a policy question and condescended to inquire of us students. Allow me to endeavor to answer even a small part of it. Looking back into antiquity, when Shun of Yu became emperor, although it is said that this was because word of his profound virtue had reached the ruler above, his achievement of the glorious transformation that moved the people like the wind depended upon such men as …

title: 弘治十四年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
禹稷契皐陶之輩焉周文之王也雖曰以
明德之肇造而其所以培王業之基者則
有太顛閎夭散宜生之徒焉是古之帝王
未有不資賢人而共理者載諸典籍漫無
可議姑舉漢世言之嬴秦鹿失漢室龍興
方其草昧之初則張良蕭何韓信之力居
多及其建儲之際則東園公夏黃公綺里
季甪里先生之功為最之數子者固皆一
時之偉人至其優劣則有可言者氣象近
===
儒良獨優矣出處不易四皓有焉而絾繫
夷族者又其下也及夫孝武繼世雄材大
略維時茂材應舉學富天人則董仲舒其
人也賢良有策名重經術則公孫弘兒寬
其人也之三儒者雖皆一代之英俊而其
優劣亦有可較者正誼明道董最高矣中
和立論寬其次焉而曲學阿世者風斯下
也自是之外則曹參之將相可觀也周昌
之剛正可取也王陵之仗義直言劉章之
punctuated: 禹、稷、契、皐陶之輩焉。周文之王也，雖曰以明德之肇造，而其所以培王業之基者，則有太顛、閎夭、散宜生之徒焉。是古之帝王，未有不資賢人而共理者。載諸典籍，漫無可議，姑舉漢世言之。嬴秦鹿失，漢室龍興，方其草昧之初，則張良、蕭何、韓信之力居多；及其建儲之際，則東園公、夏黃公、綺里季、甪里先生之功為最。之數子者，固皆一時之偉人，至其優劣，則有可言者。氣象近儒，良獨優矣；出處不易，四皓有焉；而絾繫夷族者，又其下也。及夫孝武繼世，雄材大略，維時茂材應舉，學富天人，則董仲舒其人也；賢良有策，名重經術，則公孫弘、兒寬其人也。之三儒者，雖皆一代之英俊，而其優劣亦有可較者。正誼明道，董最高矣；中和立論，寬其次焉；而曲學阿世者，風斯下也。自是之外，則曹參之將相可觀也，周昌之剛正可取也，王陵之仗義直言、劉章之
translation_en:
…there were men such as Yu, Ji, Xie, and Gao Yao. When King Wen of Zhou became king, although he was said to have founded his rule through luminous virtue, it was men such as Tai Dian, Hong Yao, and San Yisheng who helped lay the foundations of his royal enterprise. Thus none of the ancient emperors and kings failed to rely upon worthy men to govern together with them. Their deeds are recorded in the classics and histories and leave little room for dispute; let us therefore take the Han era as our example.

When the Ying house of Qin lost the deer of empire, the Han house rose like a dragon. In the unsettled beginnings of its enterprise, Zhang Liang, Xiao He, and Han Xin contributed the most. When it came to establishing the heir apparent, Lord Dongyuan, Lord Xiahuang, Qili Ji, and Master Luli rendered the greatest service. These men were certainly all outstanding figures of their time, yet their relative merits can be discussed. In bearing close to that of a Confucian scholar, Zhang Liang alone excelled. In holding steadfast to their principles in serving or withdrawing from office, the Four Hoary Elders distinguished themselves. Those who were bound in fetters [?] and whose clans were exterminated ranked below them.

Then Emperor Xiaowu succeeded to the throne, possessing commanding talents and grand designs. Among those recommended for outstanding talent, whose learning encompassed Heaven and humankind, Dong Zhongshu was the man. Among the worthy and good who presented policy essays and won renown for mastery of the classics, Gongsun Hong and Ni Kuan were the men. Though these three Confucian scholars were all eminent talents of their age, their relative merits can also be compared. In rectifying right conduct and illuminating the Way, Dong ranked highest. In grounding his arguments in balance and harmony, Kuan came next. As for the one who distorted learning to curry favor with his age, his standing was lower still [?].

Besides these men, Cao Can’s service as general and chancellor merits attention, and Zhou Chang’s firmness and uprightness deserve esteem. Wang Ling’s championship of righteousness and forthright speech, and Liu Zhang’s…

title: 弘治十四年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
托田進諫賢可知矣卒之諸吕盡滅劉氏
無虞致治之功可少乎賈誼之治安時政
賈山之至言懇切賢可見矣卒之帝心知
嚮風俗少移致治之功可短乎軍法嚴明
則有周亞夫矣明習律曆則有張蒼者矣
斷獄明允終致無冤之譽非張釋之之能
乎而于定國則繼美者也性資忠直竟寢
淮南之謀非汲黯之賢乎而申屠嘉則庶
幾者也以霍光之性資重厚則立宣而有
===
功以嚴延年之正直不阿則彈劾而莫避
魏相之嚴毅廉正丙吉之深厚不伐則宰
相之得人也趙充國之料敵制勝張安世
之宿衞忠貞則將帥之得人也如黃霸龔
遂之善政如延壽文翁之教化非守令之
得人乎二疏之去有以長恬退之風龔勝
之死有以勵志行之士以至忠誠則有劉
向議論則有匡衡與夫或以文章顯或以
篤行聞或擅一職之勞或專一節之美璧
punctuated: 托田進諫，賢可知矣。卒之諸吕盡滅，劉氏無虞，致治之功可少乎？賈誼之治安時政，賈山之至言懇切，賢可見矣。卒之帝心知嚮，風俗少移，致治之功可短乎？軍法嚴明，則有周亞夫矣；明習律曆，則有張蒼者矣。斷獄明允，終致無冤之譽，非張釋之之能乎？而于定國則繼美者也。性資忠直，竟寢淮南之謀，非汲黯之賢乎？而申屠嘉則庶幾者也。以霍光之性資重厚，則立宣而有功；以嚴延年之正直不阿，則彈劾而莫避。魏相之嚴毅廉正，丙吉之深厚不伐，則宰相之得人也；趙充國之料敵制勝，張安世之宿衞忠貞，則將帥之得人也。如黃霸、龔遂之善政，如延壽、文翁之教化，非守令之得人乎？二疏之去，有以長恬退之風；龔勝之死，有以勵志行之士。以至忠誠則有劉向，議論則有匡衡，與夫或以文章顯，或以篤行聞，或擅一職之勞，或專一節之美，璧
translation_en: …offering remonstrance through an analogy with farming: his worthiness can thus be known. In the end, the Lü clan was entirely destroyed and the Liu house was free from danger. Could his contribution to good government be considered slight? Jia Yi’s discussions of securing peace and of contemporary government, and Jia Shan’s earnest Ultimate Counsel, reveal their worthiness. In the end, the emperor understood the course to follow, and customs changed somewhat. Could their contributions to good government be belittled? For strict and clear military discipline, there was Zhou Yafu; for thorough knowledge of pitch standards and calendrical science, there was Zhang Cang. Was it not Zhang Shizhi’s ability that made his judgments discerning and impartial, ultimately earning him a reputation for leaving no one unjustly treated? Yu Dingguo carried on this excellence. Was it not Ji An’s worthiness—his loyal and upright disposition—that ultimately forestalled the plot of the Prince of Huainan? Shentu Jia approached him in these qualities. Huo Guang, with his grave and steady disposition, rendered meritorious service by enthroning Emperor Xuan; Yan Yannian, upright and unbending, spared no one in his impeachments. Wei Xiang’s stern resolve, integrity, and rectitude, and Bing Ji’s depth of character and freedom from boastfulness, show that the right men were found to serve as chief ministers. Zhao Chongguo’s skill in assessing the enemy and securing victory, and Zhang Anshi’s loyalty and steadfastness in guarding the palace, show that the right men were found as military commanders. Do not the good administration of Huang Ba and Gong Sui, and the moral instruction of Yanshou and Wen Weng, likewise show that the right men were found as governors and magistrates? The withdrawal of the two Shus fostered a spirit of serene retirement; Gong Sheng’s death encouraged men of firm purpose and virtuous conduct. For loyalty and sincerity there was Liu Xiang; for reasoned discussion there was Kuang Heng. Others distinguished themselves through literary composition, became known for steadfast conduct, excelled in the service of a particular office, or possessed an outstanding virtue—like jade discs …

title: 弘治十四年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
峙林立弗可僂指是皆西漢得人之盛而
當時致治之隆未有舍此而得之者也雖
然亦有憾焉迹近儒矣終於黃老之歸論
固高矣不免災異之惑忘親立功識者有
譏洛陽少年君子興嘆近社稷臣者失之
褊迫比伊尹功者病於不學數君子皆一
代人物之楚楚者其失如此他何道哉此
其回視五臣四友蓋有不可同年而語者
矣然則玉必琢磨而後可成瑚璉之器人
===
必自勵而後可希賢聖之域愚也脫與幸
進而竊祿于
朝以立玉堦方寸地誓當尚友古人以虞周
之臣自期待區區漢臣何足言哉管見如
斯惟執事進而教之幸甚
第叁問
王仲仁
同考試官教諭王批說出弭災之意詳盡
無遺該博之學經綸之才純正之識於此
punctuated:
峙林立，弗可僂指。是皆西漢得人之盛，而當時致治之隆，未有舍此而得之者也。雖然，亦有憾焉：迹近儒矣，終於黃老之歸；論固高矣，不免災異之惑；忘親立功，識者有譏；洛陽少年，君子興嘆；近社稷臣者，失之褊迫；比伊尹功者，病於不學。數君子皆一代人物之楚楚者，其失如此，他何道哉！此其回視五臣四友，蓋有不可同年而語者矣。然則玉必琢磨而後可成瑚璉之器，人必自勵而後可希賢聖之域。愚也脫與幸進而竊祿于朝，以立玉堦方寸地，誓當尚友古人，以虞周之臣自期待，區區漢臣何足言哉！管見如斯，惟執事進而教之，幸甚。
第叁問
王仲仁
同考試官教諭王批：說出弭災之意，詳盡無遺。該博之學，經綸之才，純正之識，於此
translation_en:
…standing like jade discs and rising like trees in a forest, too numerous to count on one’s fingers. All these attest to the Western Han’s abundance of worthy men; the flourishing governance of that time could not have been achieved without them. Yet there are grounds for regret. One whose conduct approached that of the Confucians ultimately turned to the teachings of Huang-Lao; another whose arguments were indeed lofty could not escape delusion concerning calamities and anomalies. One forgot his parents in pursuit of achievement, earning the criticism of discerning men; the young man of Luoyang occasioned sighs among gentlemen. One who approached the stature of a minister safeguarding the altars of soil and grain fell short through narrowness and impatience; another whose achievements were compared to Yi Yin’s suffered from a lack of learning. These gentlemen were all outstanding figures of their age. If their failings were such, what need is there to speak of the others? Looking back to the Five Ministers and Four Friends, they can hardly be mentioned in the same breath.
Thus jade must be carved and polished before it can become a hu or lian ritual vessel; people must exert themselves before they can aspire to the realm of worthies and sages. If I, ignorant as I am, should happen to gain advancement through good fortune and undeservedly draw a salary at court, securing a tiny foothold upon the jade steps, I pledge to take the ancients as my friends and to measure my aspirations against the ministers of Yu and Zhou. What need would there be to speak of the mere ministers of the Han? Such is my limited view. I would be most grateful if you would advance me with your instruction.
Third Policy Question
Wang Zhongren
Comment by Associate Examiner Wang, Instructor: The meaning of averting calamities is explained thoroughly, with nothing omitted. His extensive learning, his talent for ordering affairs, and his sound and upright judgment—in this…

title: 弘治十四年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
策見之他日效用其風采必自有動人者
考試官教諭高批弭災一事議論是識
見高可以觀子之志矣
考試官教諭歐陽批召災有由弭災有術
此策言之甚悉錄之以為
今日脩省之助
天人不能無交感之理君臣當盡乎交修
之誠盖天人本乎一理而君臣貴於一心
也天之變異固將示戒於人使或君臣之
===
間所以消弭之者有一未至則亦何以收
格天之功哉此愚於明問之及而不能不
重有所感必欲吾
君臣上下更相戒飭以盡應天之實庶乎天意
可回民心可得而和氣可應也夫地何為
而震也周太史伯陽甫曰陽伏而不能出
陰迫而不能升則地震劉向五行傳曰治
宫室飾臺榭則稼穡不成土失其性而為
災則地震之異固非無自而然也然自古
punctuated:
策見之。他日效用，其風采必自有動人者。
考試官教諭高批：弭災一事，議論是，識見高，可以觀子之志矣。
考試官教諭歐陽批：召災有由，弭災有術，此策言之甚悉。錄之以為今日脩省之助。
天人不能無交感之理，君臣當盡乎交修之誠。盖天人本乎一理，而君臣貴於一心也。天之變異，固將示戒於人，使或君臣之間所以消弭之者有一未至，則亦何以收格天之功哉？此愚於明問之及而不能不重有所感，必欲吾君臣上下更相戒飭，以盡應天之實，庶乎天意可回，民心可得，而和氣可應也。夫地何為而震也？周太史伯陽甫曰：「陽伏而不能出，陰迫而不能升，則地震。」劉向《五行傳》曰：「治宫室，飾臺榭，則稼穡不成，土失其性而為災。」則地震之異，固非無自而然也。然自古
translation_en:
…can be seen in this policy essay. When he enters service in the future, his bearing will surely have something that moves others.
Examiner Gao, Instructor, comments: On the matter of averting calamities, the reasoning is sound and the insight elevated. From this one can discern your aspirations.
Examiner Ouyang, Instructor, comments: Calamities have causes that bring them on, and there are methods for averting them. This policy essay explains these matters most fully. It is included here to aid present efforts at self-cultivation and self-examination.
Heaven and humanity necessarily act upon and respond to one another; ruler and ministers must fully exercise sincerity in mutually cultivating themselves. For Heaven and humanity are rooted in a single principle, while what matters for ruler and ministers is unity of purpose. Heaven’s anomalies are surely intended to warn human beings. If, in the efforts of ruler and ministers to dispel them, even one thing falls short, how can they achieve the result of moving Heaven? Thus, when your discerning question touches upon this matter, I cannot but feel deeply stirred once more. I earnestly wish our ruler and ministers, high and low, to admonish one another, fully carrying out substantive measures in response to Heaven. Then perhaps Heaven’s intentions may be turned, the people’s hearts won, and harmonious vital forces may respond.
Why does the earth quake? Boyang Fu, Grand Astrologer of the Zhou, said: “When yang lies hidden and cannot emerge, and yin is constrained and cannot rise, the earth quakes.” Liu Xiang’s Commentary on the Five Phases says: “When palaces and residences are built and terraces and pavilions embellished, crops fail to mature; earth loses its proper nature and brings calamity.” The anomaly of an earthquake, then, certainly does not occur without a cause. Yet from antiquity…

title: 弘治十四年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
以來無代無之姑即其已甚者言之則在
漢文帝同日地震二十六處在宣帝地震
河南以東四十七郡太宗貞觀之時京師
地震松業二州靈州河東地震穆宗之時
京師地震屋瓦皆墜戸牖間有聲是其在
治世則欲以警動人君使因之而戒懼不
以既治而驕也在季世則欲以譴告人君
使因之而修省不以有事而怠也是天之
於君誠如父母於子者矣方今
===
聖天子致中致和於上大臣奉職守法於下宜
乎災異無自而生而雲南之異乃如此豈
非天心仁愛所以答吾君敬天勤民之意
固有加而無已者哉惟人子事親之心無
所不至不以喜而少縱其心不以怒而少
衰其孝君之事天亦何異此則所以消災
弭異之心固不能不厪於
上矣然君者出令者也臣者行君之令而致之
民者也比者
punctuated:
以來，無代無之。姑即其已甚者言之，則在漢文帝，同日地震二十六處；在宣帝，地震河南以東四十七郡；太宗貞觀之時，京師地震，松業二州、靈州、河東地震；穆宗之時，京師地震，屋瓦皆墜，戸牖間有聲。是其在治世，則欲以警動人君，使因之而戒懼，不以既治而驕也；在季世，則欲以譴告人君，使因之而修省，不以有事而怠也。是天之於君，誠如父母於子者矣。
方今聖天子致中致和於上，大臣奉職守法於下，宜乎災異無自而生，而雲南之異乃如此，豈非天心仁愛，所以答吾君敬天勤民之意，固有加而無已者哉！惟人子事親之心，無所不至，不以喜而少縱其心，不以怒而少衰其孝。君之事天，亦何異此？則所以消災弭異之心，固不能不厪於上矣。然君者，出令者也；臣者，行君之令而致之民者也。比者，
translation_en:
…since antiquity, no dynasty has been without them. To speak only of the most severe instances: under Emperor Wen of the Han, earthquakes occurred in twenty-six places on the same day; under Emperor Xuan, earthquakes struck forty-seven commanderies from Henan eastward. During Emperor Taizong’s Zhenguan reign, earthquakes struck the capital, the two prefectures of Song and Ye [?], Lingzhou, and Hedong. Under Emperor Muzong, an earthquake struck the capital: all the roof tiles fell, and sounds arose among the doors and windows. In well-governed ages, Heaven thereby seeks to alert the ruler, making him take warning and feel apprehension, lest established good government make him arrogant. In a dynasty’s declining years, Heaven seeks thereby to admonish the ruler, making him reform himself and examine his conduct, lest troubles make him remiss. Heaven’s relationship to the ruler is indeed like that of parents to their child.
At present, our sage Son of Heaven brings equilibrium and harmony to fulfillment above, while the great ministers discharge their duties and observe the laws below. Calamities and anomalies ought therefore to have no cause to arise. Yet the anomalies in Yunnan are such as these. Is this not the benevolence and love of Heaven’s heart, responding with ever-increasing and unceasing concern to our ruler’s intention to revere Heaven and labor for the people? A child’s devotion in serving his parents must extend to everything: their pleasure must not make him relax his vigilance in the slightest, nor their anger diminish his filial devotion in the slightest. How is a ruler’s service to Heaven any different? Thus the concern to dispel calamities and quell anomalies must assuredly weigh upon His Majesty. Yet the ruler is the one who issues commands; ministers are those who carry out his commands and bring them to bear upon the people. Recently…

title: 弘治十四年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
聖天子一聞地震之異遂遣祭告之使凡所以
奉承天意以荅天譴者或自得於
聖心或建白於臣庶無不極力行之則所以應
天者固至矣第不知奉行於下者果能一
一如此乎執事謂政事或有所缺失者愚
固不敢謂盡無也誠使為之臣者上以率
下下以事上一皆以奉法循理為意各懷
愛
君憂國之誠禁奢惜費不敢盡民之財止工節
===
役不敢盡民之力黜奸貪之官進循良之
吏民之所利在於必興不為流俗因循之
論所惑民之所弊在於必革不為讒邪柔
佞之人所沮則庶幾應天以實所謂上下
交而德業成也天意安有不回變異安有
不弭者哉迂疎之見固非特為一方言之
而亦未知是否惟執事進而教之
第四問
高輔
punctuated:
聖天子一聞地震之異，遂遣祭告之使。凡所以奉承天意以荅天譴者，或自得於聖心，或建白於臣庶，無不極力行之，則所以應天者固至矣。第不知奉行於下者，果能一一如此乎？執事謂政事或有所缺失者，愚固不敢謂盡無也。誠使為之臣者，上以率下，下以事上，一皆以奉法循理為意，各懷愛君憂國之誠，禁奢惜費，不敢盡民之財；止工節役，不敢盡民之力；黜奸貪之官，進循良之吏。民之所利，在於必興，不為流俗因循之論所惑；民之所弊，在於必革，不為讒邪柔佞之人所沮。則庶幾應天以實，所謂上下交而德業成也。天意安有不回，變異安有不弭者哉？迂疎之見，固非特為一方言之，而亦未知是否，惟執事進而教之。
第四問
高輔
translation_en:
…As soon as the sagely Son of Heaven heard of the anomalous earthquake, he dispatched envoys to offer sacrifices and report to Heaven. Every measure for reverently carrying out Heaven’s will and responding to its rebuke, whether conceived in his sagely mind or proposed by officials and commoners, has been implemented with the utmost effort. His response to Heaven has thus indeed been thorough. Yet I do not know whether those charged with carrying out these measures below have truly fulfilled each one accordingly. You suggest that there may be shortcomings in government; I certainly dare not claim that there are none.
If those serving as his ministers—their superiors leading their subordinates, their subordinates serving their superiors—were all intent on upholding the law and following principle, each cherishing sincere love for the ruler and concern for the state; if they prohibited extravagance and restrained expenditure, not daring to exhaust the people’s wealth; halted construction and moderated labor service, not daring to exhaust the people’s strength; dismissed corrupt and unscrupulous officials and promoted conscientious and upright ones; if they were determined to undertake whatever benefited the people, undeluded by conventional arguments for merely carrying on as before, and determined to reform whatever harmed the people, undeterred by slanderous, wicked, ingratiating flatterers—then they might respond to Heaven through substantive action. This is what is meant by those above and below communicating with one another so that achievements in virtue and governance are brought to completion. How could Heaven’s disposition fail to turn favorable, and how could anomalous events fail to subside? These impractical and ill-informed views of mine are certainly not offered for one region alone, yet I do not know whether they are correct. I ask that you favor me with further instruction.
Fourth Policy Question
Gao Fu

title: 弘治十四年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
同考試官訓導潘批此策援據前代考課
之法無遺而摸寫
今日考核得宜之意殆盡非積學有待者不能是用錄出
考試官教諭高批論考課之法有考據
有斟酌子之學其博而通者歟
考試官教諭歐陽批歷代考課之法惟我
朝為最善是策條答詳明且一本於得人可謂知要者矣
歷代之考課各有其法而操之在乎人今
日之考課雖主于嚴而行之在乎恕蓋人
===
以濟法則或嚴或恕皆足以舉一時之吏
治而不必泥其迹恕以濟嚴則一張一弛
皆足以鼓天下之人才而不必求其備愚
也於歷代之法與今日之事蓋甞畧聞之
矣請為執事一言之考課之法其所由來
者遠矣品式之疎密不同事權之分合亦
異虞有三考之黜陟周有歲終之大計計
簿之察責之御史州牧之奏下之三公此
漢之法也六載之考委之達官優劣之等
punctuated:
同考試官訓導潘批：此策援據前代考課之法無遺，而摸寫今日考核得宜之意殆盡，非積學有待者不能，是用錄出。

考試官教諭高批：論考課之法，有考據，有斟酌，子之學其博而通者歟？

考試官教諭歐陽批：歷代考課之法，惟我朝為最善。是策條答詳明，且一本於得人，可謂知要者矣。

歷代之考課各有其法，而操之在乎人；今日之考課雖主于嚴，而行之在乎恕。蓋人以濟法，則或嚴或恕，皆足以舉一時之吏治，而不必泥其迹；恕以濟嚴，則一張一弛，皆足以鼓天下之人才，而不必求其備。愚也於歷代之法與今日之事，蓋甞畧聞之矣，請為執事一言之。考課之法，其所由來者遠矣。品式之疎密不同，事權之分合亦異。虞有三考之黜陟，周有歲終之大計；計簿之察，責之御史，州牧之奏，下之三公，此漢之法也；六載之考，委之達官，優劣之等，
translation_en:
Comment by Associate Examiner Pan, Assistant Instructor: This policy essay draws comprehensively upon the methods of evaluating officials under earlier dynasties, and conveys almost exhaustively the principles by which present-day evaluations are made appropriate. Only someone who has accumulated learning in readiness for an opportunity could achieve this. It has therefore been selected for inclusion.

Comment by Examiner Gao, Instructor: Your discussion of methods for evaluating officials offers both historical substantiation and considered judgment. Is your learning not both broad and penetrating?

Comment by Examiner Ouyang, Instructor: Among the methods for evaluating officials under successive dynasties, those of our dynasty are the best. This policy essay answers point by point, fully and clearly, and grounds everything in securing the right people. Its author may be said to understand what is essential.

Each successive dynasty has had its own methods for evaluating officials, but their administration depends upon people. Although present-day evaluations emphasize strictness, their implementation depends upon forbearance. When people complement the regulations, either strictness or forbearance can improve the administration of officials in a given age, without requiring rigid adherence to outward forms. When forbearance complements strictness, both tightening and relaxing can encourage talented people throughout the realm, without demanding perfection of them. In my humble ignorance, I have heard something of the methods of successive dynasties and the practices of the present day. Allow me to explain them to you.

Methods for evaluating officials have a long history. Their grading procedures have differed in their degree of detail, and the division or concentration of administrative authority has also varied. Under Yu, demotion and promotion followed three evaluations; under the Zhou, there was a comprehensive assessment at the year's end. Scrutiny of the accounts was entrusted to the Censors, and reports from Regional Governors were referred to the Three Dukes: these were the methods of the Han. Evaluations held every six years were entrusted to high officials, and the rankings of superior and inferior performance …

title: 弘治十四年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
上之每歲此晉之法也唐制則百司之長
歲較其屬之功過而差以九等宋制則內
外選人周一歲為一考而磨勘叙遷其甲
乙之等則若河南吳公之第一茂陵蕭育
之第六皆是也其批書之辭則若官無異
稱之中上催科政拙之考下皆是也法之
行于上也因時而損益法之用于下也因
人而操縱以丙吉之寬大好禮則掩惡揚
善而無所按驗以袁安之仁信道孚則不
===
鞠臧罪而猾惡自禁條奏貪殘而天下肅
然者楊秉之風裁可想也舉奏貪汙而四
海翕然者黃瓊之精明可尚也趙宗儒懲
至德之黜陟則考中上者纔五十人而不
為刻是亦矯枉之意也盧承慶重督運者
之雅量則改判註之語至一再變而不為
專是亦觀人之法也選人匿喪者賈黯廢
之終身將以振風義也韓億之意則不欲
錮人于聖世而以捃拾小過為大戒然但
punctuated: 上之每歲，此晉之法也。唐制則百司之長，歲較其屬之功過，而差以九等。宋制則內外選人，周一歲為一考，而磨勘叙遷。其甲乙之等，則若河南吳公之第一、茂陵蕭育之第六，皆是也。其批書之辭，則若官無異稱之中上、催科政拙之考下，皆是也。法之行于上也，因時而損益；法之用于下也，因人而操縱。以丙吉之寬大好禮，則掩惡揚善，而無所按驗；以袁安之仁信道孚，則不鞠臧罪，而猾惡自禁。條奏貪殘，而天下肅然者，楊秉之風裁可想也；舉奏貪汙，而四海翕然者，黃瓊之精明可尚也。趙宗儒懲至德之黜陟，則考中上者纔五十人，而不為刻，是亦矯枉之意也。盧承慶重督運者之雅量，則改判註之語，至一再變，而不為專，是亦觀人之法也。選人匿喪者，賈黯廢之終身，將以振風義也。韓億之意，則不欲錮人于聖世，而以捃拾小過為大戒。然但
translation_en:
…the rankings of superior and inferior performance were submitted each year: this was the Jin system. Under the Tang system, the heads of the various offices annually compared their subordinates’ merits and faults and ranked them in nine grades. Under the Song system, junior officials serving within and outside the capital underwent one evaluation for each full year, and their records were scrutinized to determine advancement. Examples of such rankings include Lord Wu of Henan being placed first and Xiao Yu of Maoling being placed sixth. Examples of the wording of written assessments include an upper-middle rating for “no exceptional reputation in office” and a low rating for “inept administration in collecting taxes.”

When laws are implemented by those above, they are modified according to the times; when applied to those below, they are administered strictly or leniently according to the person. Bing Ji, being magnanimous and devoted to ritual propriety, concealed faults and proclaimed virtues, conducting no investigations. Yuan An, being humane and trustworthy, with his moral principles inspiring confidence, did not investigate offenses involving illicit gains, yet the cunning and wicked restrained themselves. That itemized accusations against greedy and oppressive officials brought solemn order throughout the realm allows us to imagine Yang Bing’s authoritative bearing and judgment. That impeachments of corrupt officials won unanimous approval throughout the land makes Huang Qiong’s discernment worthy of esteem.

Zhao Zongru, taking warning from the demotions and promotions of the Zhide era, awarded upper-middle ratings to only fifty men, yet this did not constitute harshness: his intention was to correct past abuses. Lu Chengqing valued the composure of an official supervising transport and revised the wording of his assessment once and then again, yet this did not constitute arbitrary conduct: it too was a method of judging a person.

Jia An permanently barred from office a junior official who had concealed a bereavement, intending thereby to invigorate moral conduct and the sense of duty. Han Yi’s view, however, was that people should not be barred from office in an age of sage rule, and he regarded ferreting out minor faults as something especially to be guarded against. Yet merely…

title: 弘治十四年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
曰小過而已則大者之不赦可知也監司
不才者范仲淹付之一筆將以利生民也
杜衍之意則欲使人改過遷善而以摘發
小節為不恕然但曰小節而已則大者之
必懲可知也嗟夫水火之用不同而同于
利物醎酸之用不同而同于適口寛嚴之
用不同而同于奉法二者之用惟視其人
何如耳得其人則嚴者足以飭吏治而寛
者亦足以鎮雅俗不得其人則其嚴也或
===
至于矯激有假擊搏之威以肆其殘忍之
性者矣其恕也或流于姑息有借持重之
名以濟其不斷之私者矣我
朝考課之法一以虞周為準品式周詳體統
不紊以藩臬察郡守以郡守察縣令有巡
按者以莅之有巡撫者以總之行部則亷
其臧否之實代還則上其批書之語其後
恐風聞之失實而使人坐被空文也則令
嵗終奏報下之吏部而明著于冊又其後
punctuated:
曰小過而已，則大者之不赦可知也。監司不才者，范仲淹付之一筆，將以利生民也。杜衍之意，則欲使人改過遷善，而以摘發小節為不恕。然但曰小節而已，則大者之必懲可知也。嗟夫！水火之用不同，而同于利物；醎酸之用不同，而同于適口；寛嚴之用不同，而同于奉法。二者之用，惟視其人何如耳。得其人，則嚴者足以飭吏治，而寛者亦足以鎮雅俗；不得其人，則其嚴也或至于矯激，有假擊搏之威以肆其殘忍之性者矣；其恕也或流于姑息，有借持重之名以濟其不斷之私者矣。
我朝考課之法，一以虞周為準，品式周詳，體統不紊。以藩臬察郡守，以郡守察縣令，有巡按者以莅之，有巡撫者以總之。行部則亷其臧否之實，代還則上其批書之語。其後，恐風聞之失實而使人坐被空文也，則令嵗終奏報，下之吏部，而明著于冊。又其後，
translation_en:
…he spoke only of minor faults; thus it is clear that serious ones would not be pardoned. Fan Zhongyan struck out the names of incompetent surveillance officials with a stroke of his brush, intending thereby to benefit the people. Du Yan’s intention, however, was to allow people to correct their faults and turn toward goodness; he regarded exposing minor failings as unforgiving. Yet he spoke only of minor failings; thus it is clear that serious ones must be punished. Alas! Water and fire differ in their uses, yet both benefit things; saltiness and sourness differ in their uses, yet both please the palate; leniency and severity differ in their uses, yet both serve to uphold the law. The application of these two approaches depends solely on the character of the person employing them. With the right person, severity can put official administration in order, while leniency can likewise bring stability to the cultivated and the common alike. With the wrong person, severity may become excessive and extreme: some use the intimidating power of punitive action to indulge their cruel disposition. Forbearance may likewise lapse into indulgence: some borrow the reputation of being circumspect to accommodate their own weakness of indecision.
Our dynasty’s system for evaluating officials takes the institutions of Yu and Zhou as its standard throughout. Its classifications and procedures are comprehensive and detailed, and its administrative hierarchy is orderly. Provincial Administration and Surveillance Commissioners scrutinize prefects, and prefects scrutinize district magistrates; Regional Inspectors oversee them, and Grand Coordinators exercise general supervision. When touring their jurisdictions, they investigate the actual merits and failings of officials; when returning upon replacement, they submit their written evaluations. Later, out of concern that hearsay might be inaccurate and cause people to suffer accusations based on empty documentation, it was ordered that reports be submitted to the throne at year’s end, referred to the Ministry of Personnel, and clearly entered in registers. Still later …

title: 弘治十四年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
恐胥吏之漏言而使人因緣為姦也則吏
部取每歲所報犢而藏之臨事而後啓大
約總計所報以三分為率三分俱報其賢
者為上二分者次之俱無焉者為下其防
之也可謂周而察之也可謂審矣仕者雖
欲飾名以求功巧文以逃罪不可得也
皇上端居九重之上而遊念四海之遠愛惜人
才之意常寓于綜核名實之中往年吏部
上罷黜之數
===
聖諭則曰人才難得如有不公許其伸理于是
行覆考之令止欲去其太甚而新任者皆
復其官繼後臺諫言黜陟之事
聖諭又曰考察重事毋得偏聽致有枉抑于是
申明批考之法止據見任開報而既往者
不追其過盖立法雖嚴而行之甚恕即古
昔聖王使人以器與人不求備之盛心也
一時奉法之臣皆能將順
德意嚴重者有黄瓊范仲淹之風寬厚者有
punctuated:
恐胥吏之漏言而使人因緣為姦也，則吏部取每歲所報犢而藏之，臨事而後啓。大約總計所報，以三分為率：三分俱報其賢者為上，二分者次之，俱無焉者為下。其防之也可謂周，而察之也可謂審矣。仕者雖欲飾名以求功，巧文以逃罪，不可得也。
皇上端居九重之上，而遊念四海之遠，愛惜人才之意常寓于綜核名實之中。往年吏部上罷黜之數，聖諭則曰：「人才難得，如有不公，許其伸理。」于是行覆考之令，止欲去其太甚，而新任者皆復其官。繼後臺諫言黜陟之事，聖諭又曰：「考察重事，毋得偏聽，致有枉抑。」于是申明批考之法，止據見任開報，而既往者不追其過。盖立法雖嚴，而行之甚恕，即古昔聖王使人以器、與人不求備之盛心也。一時奉法之臣皆能將順德意，嚴重者有黄瓊、范仲淹之風，寬厚者有
translation_en:
…fearing that subordinate clerks might disclose information and thereby enable people to exploit it for wrongdoing, the Ministry of Personnel took the documents [?] submitted each year and stored them away, opening them only when a case required action. Broadly speaking, the reports were tallied on a three-part basis: those whose worthiness was affirmed in all three parts ranked highest; those affirmed in two ranked next; and those with no such affirmation ranked lowest. These safeguards may indeed be called comprehensive, and this scrutiny thorough. Even if officeholders wished to embellish their reputations to claim merit or manipulate wording to escape punishment, they could not do so.
His Majesty sits in dignity within the palace’s ninefold precincts, yet his thoughts range to the distant reaches of the realm. His concern to cherish talented men is always embodied in his comprehensive examination of whether reputation accords with actual performance. In a previous year, when the Ministry of Personnel submitted the number of officials to be dismissed, an imperial instruction declared: “Talented men are hard to find. If there has been any injustice, permit those concerned to seek redress.” An order for reassessment was therefore implemented, with the intention of removing only the most egregious offenders; all newly appointed officials were restored to their posts. Subsequently, when the censors and remonstrance officials spoke about dismissals and promotions, another imperial instruction declared: “The evaluation of officials is a weighty matter. You must not listen to one side alone and thereby cause anyone to suffer unjust treatment.” Accordingly, the procedures for written evaluations were clarified: reports were to concern only those currently serving, and the faults of those who had already left office were not pursued retrospectively. Although the rules were strict, their application was exceedingly lenient. This was precisely the generous intention of the sage kings of antiquity, who employed people according to their capacities and did not demand perfection of them. The officials charged with enforcing the rules at that time could all carry out and further this benevolent intention. Those who were stern and grave had the bearing of Huang Qiong and Fan Zhongyan; those who were generous and lenient had…

title: 弘治十四年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
丙吉杜衍之譽所以吏稱其職民安其業
治化之盛比隆虞周而非漢唐宋之所能
及也執事于此猶過為借聽之謀欲求可
以裨益時政者迂儒不知通變將何說以
應雖然言及之而不言亦君子所不與也
竊有所見願終言之蓋聞異時之考課也
吏部就來
朝各官中簡其治行尤異者具疏以
聞寵以異數或陪祀于
===
南郊或賜燕于南宮或別記其姓名或亟擢
其顯位一時之仕者傾耳而聽企踵而睹
往往咨嗟歎羨而耻己之不與則交相磨
礪勉修職業以冀後日之或與焉此所謂
賞一人而千萬人勸亦轉移感動之一機
也其事未遠其効可徵不知今日亦可舉
而行之否乎僭妄之言承問而對執政者
聞之或有取焉則豈惟仕者之幸
第五問
punctuated:
丙吉、杜衍之譽。所以吏稱其職，民安其業，治化之盛，比隆虞周，而非漢唐宋之所能及也。執事于此，猶過為借聽之謀，欲求可以裨益時政者，迂儒不知通變，將何說以應？雖然，言及之而不言，亦君子所不與也。竊有所見，願終言之。蓋聞異時之考課也，吏部就來朝各官中，簡其治行尤異者，具疏以聞，寵以異數：或陪祀于南郊，或賜燕于南宮，或別記其姓名，或亟擢其顯位。一時之仕者，傾耳而聽，企踵而睹，往往咨嗟歎羨，而耻己之不與，則交相磨礪，勉修職業，以冀後日之或與焉。此所謂賞一人而千萬人勸，亦轉移感動之一機也。其事未遠，其効可徵，不知今日亦可舉而行之否乎？僭妄之言，承問而對，執政者聞之，或有取焉，則豈惟仕者之幸？

第五問
translation_en:
…the reputation of Bing Ji and Du Yan. Thus officials fulfill their duties and the people pursue their livelihoods in peace. The flourishing of governance and moral transformation rivals the ages of Shun and the Zhou, surpassing anything the Han, Tang, or Song could attain. Yet you, sir, still extend your consideration so far as to solicit opinions, seeking something that might benefit present governance. What can a pedantic scholar, ignorant of how to adapt to changing circumstances, offer in reply? Nevertheless, to remain silent when invited to speak is also something a gentleman disapproves of. I have some humble observations and beg leave to state them fully.

I have heard that, in former performance evaluations, the Ministry of Personnel selected, from among the officials coming to court, those whose administrative achievements were especially outstanding. It submitted memorials reporting them to the throne, and they were favored with exceptional honors: some attended the sacrifices at the Southern Suburb; some were granted banquets at the Southern Palace; some had their names specially recorded; and some were swiftly promoted to prominent positions. Officials of the time strained their ears to listen and stood on tiptoe to watch. They would often sigh in admiration and envy, ashamed that they themselves were not among those honored. They therefore encouraged one another and diligently attended to their official duties, hoping that they might be included on some future occasion. This is what is meant by rewarding one person and thereby encouraging thousands upon thousands. It is also one means of moving people and bringing about change. These precedents are not remote, and their effectiveness can be verified. Might they also be put into practice today? These presumptuous words are offered in response to your question. If those who govern hear them and find something worth adopting, would the benefit accrue only to those holding office?

Fifth Question

title: 弘治十四年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
趙儀
考試官教諭高批禦戎之策據古酌今
非尋常敷演者比充積如此明春
大廷之對知不多讓
考試官教諭歐陽批歷陳古人禦戎之法
參酌時勢非有卓見者能之耶
莫難於禦戎而得其法也易莫難於用法
而得其人也易不得其法則所以備於豫
者不固謀於變者不神戎狄之來也無以
===
應之不得其人則靜而玩愒無繫桑之謀
動而畏縮無鷹揚之勇法何從而出也必
既得其法又得其人以守則固以戰則克
尚何戎狄之足慮哉愚也草茅下士曷足
以與
廟堂之訏謨顧明問下及有不敢默焉者請
復其萬一夫中國之有夷狄猶晝之有夜
陽之有陰君子之有小人也故邊境自古
為患而備禦代不乏人試以自周而後者
punctuated:
趙儀

考試官教諭高批：「禦戎之策，據古酌今，非尋常敷演者比。充積如此，明春大廷之對，知不多讓。」

考試官教諭歐陽批：「歷陳古人禦戎之法，參酌時勢，非有卓見者能之耶？」

莫難於禦戎，而得其法也易；莫難於用法，而得其人也易。不得其法，則所以備於豫者不固，謀於變者不神，戎狄之來也，無以應之。不得其人，則靜而玩愒，無繫桑之謀；動而畏縮，無鷹揚之勇。法何從而出也？必既得其法，又得其人，以守則固，以戰則克，尚何戎狄之足慮哉！愚也，草茅下士，曷足以與廟堂之訏謨？顧明問下及，有不敢默焉者，請復其萬一。夫中國之有夷狄，猶晝之有夜，陽之有陰，君子之有小人也。故邊境自古為患，而備禦代不乏人。試以自周而後者
translation_en:
Zhao Yi

Comment by Examiner Gao, Instructor: “This policy essay on repelling the Rong draws on antiquity while weighing present circumstances. It cannot be compared with ordinary elaborations of a theme. With learning so richly accumulated, I am sure that in responding before the imperial court next spring you will yield little to others.”

Comment by Examiner Ouyang, Instructor: “He sets out in detail the ancients’ methods of repelling the Rong and assesses them against the circumstances of the times. Could anyone without outstanding insight accomplish this?”

Nothing is harder than repelling the Rong, yet with the right methods it becomes easy; nothing is harder than applying methods, yet with the right men it becomes easy. Without the right methods, preparations made beforehand will lack firmness, and plans for responding to unforeseen changes will lack inspired adaptability. When the Rong and Di arrive, there will be no means of responding to them. Without the right men, in quiet times they will idle away their days, having no plan to secure the state as firmly as if bound to a mulberry tree; when action is required, they will shrink back in fear, lacking the courage of a soaring hawk. How, then, can methods be put into effect? One must obtain both the right methods and the right men: in defense one will then be secure, and in battle victorious. What further cause will there be to fear the Rong and Di?

I am but an unworthy, humble scholar living outside official service. How could I be fit to participate in the grand deliberations of the court? Yet since your enlightened question has reached down to me, I dare not remain silent. Allow me to offer a reply covering some tiny part of the matter. The existence of the Yi and Di alongside the Central Kingdom is like that of night alongside day, yin alongside yang, and petty men alongside gentlemen. Thus the frontier regions have been a source of trouble since antiquity, yet no age has lacked men who prepared defenses against them. Let us take examples from the Zhou onward…

title: 弘治十四年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
言之若居代鴈門而匈奴十餘歲不敢犯
邊者李牧也為雲中太守而匈奴深畏其
略者李廣也祭肜誘鮮卑擊弱匈奴而邊
無寇警盖恩惠所感焉陳禪於學行禮陳
說道義而單于懷服盖天理所孚焉都督
并州而邊塵不驚比之長城者李勣之功
何著哉刺史隴州設為譙櫓以禦虜暴者
馬燧之威何震哉請城方渠以遏吐蕃歸
路楊朝晟萬金之計審矣縂十一軍而築
===
三城於要路李德裕措置之方密矣定州
練兵精勁齊一而聲動虜中非韓琦之謀
猷克壯而致是乎以詔書犒賞諸羌受命
而始為漢用非范仲淹之能服人心而得
是乎之數君子者忠義著聞恩威並用其
一時邊塞寧謐未必非其功也洪惟我
國家之於夷狄來則厚金幣以賚之間又遣
使臣以慰之綏之之道既善矣嚴城壘之
設以為之防命文武之臣以為之守馭之
punctuated:
言之，若居代鴈門而匈奴十餘歲不敢犯邊者，李牧也；為雲中太守而匈奴深畏其略者，李廣也。祭肜誘鮮卑擊弱匈奴，而邊無寇警，盖恩惠所感焉；陳禪於學行禮，陳說道義，而單于懷服，盖天理所孚焉。都督并州而邊塵不驚，比之長城者，李勣之功何著哉！刺史隴州，設為譙櫓以禦虜暴者，馬燧之威何震哉！請城方渠以遏吐蕃歸路，楊朝晟萬金之計審矣；縂十一軍而築三城於要路，李德裕措置之方密矣。定州練兵精勁齊一，而聲動虜中，非韓琦之謀猷克壯而致是乎？以詔書犒賞諸羌，受命而始為漢用，非范仲淹之能服人心而得是乎？之數君子者，忠義著聞，恩威並用，其一時邊塞寧謐，未必非其功也。
洪惟我國家之於夷狄，來則厚金幣以賚之，間又遣使臣以慰之，綏之之道既善矣。嚴城壘之設以為之防，命文武之臣以為之守，馭之
translation_en:
…to speak of them: it was Li Mu who was stationed at Yanmen in Dai, so that the Xiongnu dared not violate the frontier for more than ten years; it was Li Guang who served as Governor of Yunzhong, so that the Xiongnu deeply feared his strategic skill. Ji Rong induced the Xianbei to attack and weaken the Xiongnu, leaving the frontier free of alarms of invasion: this was surely the effect of his kindness and generosity. Chen Chan performed rites at the school and expounded the Way and righteousness, so that the chanyu submitted willingly: this was surely the trust inspired by heavenly principle. Serving as Commander-in-chief at Bingzhou, he kept the frontier undisturbed and was likened to the Great Wall—how illustrious were Li Ji’s achievements! Serving as Regional Inspector of Longzhou, he established watchtowers to resist the enemy’s violence—how awe-inspiring was Ma Sui’s might! Proposing to fortify Fangqu to block the Tibetans’ route of return, Yang Chaosheng devised a well-considered plan worth ten thousand pieces of gold. Commanding eleven armies and building three fortified towns on vital routes, Li Deyu made meticulous arrangements. At Dingzhou, the troops were trained to be skilled, strong, and disciplined, and their reputation shook the enemy’s lands. Was this not achieved through Han Qi’s vigorous strategic planning? The various Qiang were rewarded by imperial edict, accepted the imperial command, and began to serve the Chinese state. Was this not achieved through Fan Zhongyan’s ability to win people’s allegiance? These gentlemen [?] were renowned for loyalty and righteousness and employed both generosity and authority. The peace of the frontier in their respective times may well have been their achievement.
When we consider our dynasty’s dealings with the non-Chinese peoples, whenever they come, it rewards them generously with money and silks; from time to time it also dispatches envoys to reassure them. Its means of pacifying them are already excellent. It establishes strong fortified defenses to guard against them and appoints civil and military officials to keep watch over them. Its means of controlling them…

title: 弘治十四年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
之法又至矣奈何比來北虜負
恩敢於犯順及遣將出師也逐之則潛蹤而去
緩之則乘間而來此所以致厪
宵旰之慮然竊聞之夷狄不義縱暴必亡在
備禦之得其法將帥之得其人耳誠使為
邊將者如李牧之在鴈門廣儲積慎烽火
練習騎射恩遇士卒勿輕舉以損其威謹
妄動以蓄其銳俟彼之來也則以逸待勞
可一鼓而破之其鋒一挫自爾逺遁敢復
===
來乎如祭肜之處鮮卑結以恩惠示以財
利諭以逆順禍福諉以交相攻伐使於我
各售其功於彼各分其志若彼之動也則
以衆當寡可不戰而屈之其黨既散自然
孤立敢為患乎以至凡握兵守土者皆陳
禪李勣之流韓琦仲淹之輩或以德化或
以威畧而
國家明旌别之典嚴黜陟之條功多有厚賞
不迪有顯戮則人皆自奮爭樹功業將使
punctuated: 之法又至矣。奈何比來北虜負恩，敢於犯順？及遣將出師也，逐之則潛蹤而去，緩之則乘間而來，此所以致厪宵旰之慮。然竊聞之，夷狄不義，縱暴必亡，在備禦之得其法、將帥之得其人耳。誠使為邊將者如李牧之在鴈門，廣儲積，慎烽火，練習騎射，恩遇士卒，勿輕舉以損其威，謹妄動以蓄其銳，俟彼之來也，則以逸待勞，可一鼓而破之。其鋒一挫，自爾逺遁，敢復來乎？如祭肜之處鮮卑，結以恩惠，示以財利，諭以逆順禍福，諉以交相攻伐，使於我各售其功，於彼各分其志。若彼之動也，則以衆當寡，可不戰而屈之。其黨既散，自然孤立，敢為患乎？以至凡握兵守土者，皆陳禪、李勣之流，韓琦、仲淹之輩，或以德化，或以威畧，而國家明旌别之典，嚴黜陟之條，功多有厚賞，不迪有顯戮，則人皆自奮，爭樹功業，將使
translation_en:
…the methods for controlling them are likewise fully developed. Why, then, have the northern barbarians recently betrayed imperial favor and dared to attack those obedient to the throne? When generals are dispatched and troops sent out, the enemy disappear without a trace if pursued, but exploit any opening to return if pressure is relaxed. This is what burdens Your Majesty with anxiety from before dawn until late at night. Yet I have humbly heard that barbarians who act unrighteously and indulge in violence must perish. It is simply a matter of adopting proper defensive methods and choosing the right commanders. If only our frontier generals were like Li Mu at Yanmen, amassing provisions, carefully maintaining beacon signals, training in mounted archery, treating their soldiers with kindness, avoiding rash advances that diminish their authority, and guarding against reckless action [?] to conserve their fighting strength, then, when the enemy arrived, they could meet an exhausted foe with rested troops and defeat them at a single beat of the drum. Once the enemy’s offensive strength had been blunted, they would flee far away of their own accord. Would they dare return?

If they were like Ji Rong in his dealings with the Xianbei, binding them through kindness, showing them opportunities for material gain, explaining the calamities and blessings that follow rebellion and obedience, and charging them to attack one another, each group would seek recognition from us for its achievements, while their purposes would become divided among themselves. If the enemy then made a move, we could bring superior numbers against their few and subdue them without fighting. Once their confederates had dispersed, they would naturally stand isolated. Would they dare cause trouble?

If, moreover, all those commanding troops and defending territory were men of the caliber of Chen Chan and Li Ji, Han Qi and Fan Zhongyan, some transforming people through virtue and others employing military might and strategy, while the state clearly applied its rules for recognizing distinctions and strictly enforced its provisions for dismissal and promotion, granting generous rewards for great achievements and publicly executing the disobedient, then everyone would exert himself and compete to establish meritorious accomplishments. This would bring about…

title: 弘治十四年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
隻輪匹馬絕跡於邊徼鬼馘獸形退伏於
窮荒保金甌之全勢紓
宵旰之憂勤恐於此而得其萬一矣雖然愚
又有說焉七旬苗格於誕敷文德之後四
夷咸賓於明王慎德之時今日夷狄之患
安知非天心仁愛欲如虞周之盛乎人事
修則天意得天意得則邊釁弭此只在
聖天子加之意而已區區芹曝之誠敢以是為
篇終獻
punctuated: 隻輪匹馬絕跡於邊徼，鬼馘獸形退伏於窮荒，保金甌之全勢，紓宵旰之憂勤，恐於此而得其萬一矣。雖然，愚又有說焉：七旬苗格於誕敷文德之後，四夷咸賓於明王慎德之時。今日夷狄之患，安知非天心仁愛，欲如虞周之盛乎？人事修則天意得，天意得則邊釁弭，此只在聖天子加之意而已。區區芹曝之誠，敢以是為篇終獻。
translation_en:
…not a single enemy chariot or horse will leave a trace along the frontier, and those with demonic heads and beastlike forms [?] will withdraw into submission in the remotest wilderness. The realm’s integrity, like an unbroken golden bowl, will be preserved, and the anxious toil that occupies Your Majesty from before dawn until late at night will be eased. Perhaps these measures may accomplish some tiny portion of that aim.
Nevertheless, I have a further observation to offer. The Miao submitted after seventy days, following the extensive propagation of civil virtue; the barbarians of the four quarters all came as guests when the enlightened king attended carefully to his virtue. How can we know that today’s troubles with the barbarians are not an expression of Heaven’s benevolent concern, intended to bring about prosperity like that of the Yu and Zhou? When human affairs are properly ordered, Heaven’s favor is secured; when Heaven’s favor is secured, frontier strife subsides. This requires only that the sagely Son of Heaven give it his attention. With the humble sincerity of one offering celery or the warmth of the sun, I venture to present these words as the concluding offering of my essay.

title: 弘治十四年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
雲貴鄉試錄後序
弘治辛酉秋八月壬申雲貴
鄉試事竣取士五十人刻其
文之尤者二十篇合為錄以
獻于
上皆成法也巡按雲南監察御史
何琛實監臨之防範之嚴去
===
取之審盖有法外意焉故事
錄有序儼幸與有司列謹序
其後日於乎雲貴之取士至
此亦云盛矣嘗考之其初舉
者纔十數人而止漸益之至
四十有五人又再益之乃如
今日之數至今又三科矣士
punctuated:
雲貴鄉試錄後序

弘治辛酉秋八月壬申，雲貴鄉試事竣，取士五十人，刻其文之尤者二十篇，合為錄，以獻于上，皆成法也。巡按雲南監察御史何琛實監臨之，防範之嚴，去取之審，盖有法外意焉。故事，錄有序。儼幸與有司列，謹序其後日：于乎！雲貴之取士，至此亦云盛矣！嘗考之，其初舉者纔十數人而止，漸益之至四十有五人，又再益之，乃如今日之數。至今又三科矣。士
translation_en:
Postface to the Record of the Yunnan-Guizhou Provincial Examination

On the renshen day of the eighth month, in autumn of the xinyou year of the Hongzhi reign (1501), the Yunnan-Guizhou Provincial Examination was concluded, and fifty men were selected. Twenty of their finest essays were printed and compiled into a record for presentation to His Majesty. All this followed established regulations. He Chen, Investigating Censor on an inspection tour of Yunnan, served as Supervising Official. The rigor of his precautions and the care with which he rejected or selected candidates reflected an intent extending beyond the regulations themselves.

By precedent, the record has a preface. I, Yan, have been fortunate to be numbered among the officials responsible, and respectfully append this postface, saying [?]: Ah! The selection of scholars in Yunnan and Guizhou may indeed be called flourishing at this stage! I have examined its history: initially, only a dozen or so men were recommended. The number was gradually increased to forty-five, then increased once more to the present number. Another three examination cycles have now elapsed. The scholars…

title: 弘治十四年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
之進脩日益盛由今之試者
觀之雖更益數人亦可也然
而有不可者法也法之所在
不得以私意出入之者也豈
惟取士之數為然由今錄中
所刻及諸得雋之文觀之為
易義者不得如書如詩而春
===
秋不得如禮如易也為論者
不得如義而為判為策對亦
不得如詔誥之類也何者亦
各有法故也夫取士之數裁
定於今因時而損益作文之
格沿習於古與時而高下是
二者皆以成法所在不容以
punctuated: 之進脩日益盛，由今之試者觀之，雖更益數人亦可也。然而有不可者，法也。法之所在，不得以私意出入之者也。豈惟取士之數為然？由今錄中所刻及諸得雋之文觀之，為《易》義者不得如《書》、如《詩》，而《春秋》不得如《禮》、如《易》也。為論者不得如義，而為判、為策對，亦不得如詔誥之類也。何者？亦各有法故也。夫取士之數，裁定於今，因時而損益；作文之格，沿習於古，與時而高下。是二者皆以成法所在，不容以
translation_en: …their advancement in learning and self-cultivation grows ever more flourishing. Judging by those who sat this examination, it would be possible to increase the number selected by several more. Yet what prevents this is the established rule. Where a rule applies, one may not depart from it according to personal wishes. Is this true only of the number of men selected? Judging from the writings printed in this record and the other essays of successful candidates, an exposition on the Book of Changes must not resemble one on the Book of Documents or the Book of Odes; nor may an exposition on the Spring and Autumn Annals resemble one on the Book of Rites or the Book of Changes. A discourse must not resemble a classical exposition; likewise, a legal judgment or a response to a policy question must not resemble an imperial edict or proclamation. Why? Because each also has its own rules. The number of men selected is determined in the present, reduced or increased as circumstances require; the forms of essay writing are inherited from antiquity, rising or declining with the times. In both matters, established rules apply, and it is impermissible to…

title: 弘治十四年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
私意參之而况於士之自立
無時而可變者而獨無成法
乎哉盖自修己以至于安百
姓自一命以上至於宰天下
自戒慎恐懼以至于位天地
育萬物君子小人之分義利
公私之辨皆有聖賢之成法
===
在焉為士者當從事於此以
終其身隨其職守才力所至
以敬其事非可因時勢而為
之高下損益者也夫以取士
之有法也外之則罪矣作文
之有法也失之則黜矣士之
自立萬有一焉或悖於聖賢
punctuated: 私意參之，而况於士之自立，無時而可變者，而獨無成法乎哉？盖自修己以至于安百姓，自一命以上至於宰天下，自戒慎恐懼以至于位天地、育萬物，君子小人之分，義利公私之辨，皆有聖賢之成法在焉。為士者當從事於此，以終其身，隨其職守才力所至，以敬其事，非可因時勢而為之高下損益者也。夫以取士之有法也，外之則罪矣；作文之有法也，失之則黜矣。士之自立，萬有一焉或悖於聖賢
translation_en: …interference by private opinion. How much more, then, must there be established standards for a scholar’s moral self-establishment, which can never be altered at any time? From cultivating oneself to bringing peace to the common people, from the first appointment to office up to governing all under Heaven, and from vigilance and apprehension to bringing Heaven and Earth into their proper places and nurturing the myriad things—in distinguishing the gentleman from the petty man, and discerning righteousness from profit and public from private interests—there are established standards of the sages and worthies in all these matters. A scholar should devote himself to these throughout his life, attending reverently to his duties as far as his official responsibilities, abilities, and strength extend. These standards cannot be raised or lowered, diminished or augmented, according to the circumstances of the times. Now, since there are rules for selecting scholars for office, those who step outside them are punished; since there are rules for composition, those who fail to meet them are rejected. In a scholar’s moral self-establishment, should he, even in a single instance out of ten thousand, depart from the sages and worthies’…

title: 弘治十四年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
之成法縱幸不為有司之所
罪與黜如內愧何如天下之
公議何諸生皆誦法孔氏者
孔氏之法士莫重乎其始進
故於其始進也以是瀆告之
有司者将考其後焉
湖廣長沙府湘陰縣儒學教
===
諭高巖謹序
punctuated:
之成法，縱幸不為有司之所罪與黜，如內愧何？如天下之公議何？諸生皆誦法孔氏者，孔氏之法，士莫重乎其始進。故於其始進也，以是瀆告之。有司者将考其後焉。
湖廣長沙府湘陰縣儒學教諭高巖謹序。
translation_en:
…the established standards of the sages and worthies—even if one is fortunate enough to escape punishment and rejection by the responsible officials, how can one face one's inner shame? How can one face the public judgment of all under Heaven? You students all recite the teachings of Confucius and take him as your model. According to Confucius's standards, nothing matters more for a scholar than his first entry into official life. Thus, at this initial step, I venture to trouble you with these admonitions. The responsible officials will assess your subsequent conduct.
Preface respectfully written by Gao Yan, Instructor in the Confucian School of Xiangyin County, Changsha Prefecture, Huguang.

title: 弘治十四年雲貴鄉試錄
弘治十四年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
雲貴鄉試錄序
皇上臨御十有四年秋雲貴例當
大比先期雲南藩臣舉令典
請於前巡按監察御史林〔世遠〕
禮聘儒紳以司考校維時兩
藩鎮守太監劉〔昶〕楊〔友〕總戎
黔國公沐〔崑〕豐潤伯曹〔愷〕咸
===
雅重斯文巡撫都御史陳〔金〕
拓新試院規模宏敞申飭百
司悉遵罔怠刑部員外郎蔡
〔鍊〕適慮囚于斯監察御史何
〔琛〕陳〔恪〕分地巡按而激勸之
及期〔琛〕寔監臨焉凡場屋事
既極力脩舉乃八月將試前
punctuated:
雲貴鄉試錄序

皇上臨御十有四年秋，雲貴例當大比。先期，雲南藩臣舉令典，請於前，巡按監察御史林〔世遠〕禮聘儒紳，以司考校。維時，兩藩鎮守太監劉〔昶〕、楊〔友〕，總戎黔國公沐〔崑〕、豐潤伯曹〔愷〕，咸雅重斯文。巡撫都御史陳〔金〕拓新試院，規模宏敞，申飭百司，悉遵罔怠。刑部員外郎蔡〔鍊〕適慮囚于斯，監察御史何〔琛〕、陳〔恪〕分地巡按，而激勸之。及期，〔琛〕寔監臨焉。凡場屋事，既極力脩舉，乃八月將試前
translation_en:
Preface to the Record of the Yunnan-Guizhou Provincial Examination

In the autumn of the fourteenth year of His Majesty’s reign, Yunnan and Guizhou were due, according to established practice, to hold the Provincial Examination. In advance of the appointed time, the provincial officials of Yunnan invoked the prescribed regulations and submitted their request. The Regional Inspector, Investigating Censor Lin Shiyuan, ceremonially invited scholars of the gentry to oversee the examination and assessment. At that time, the eunuch Grand Defenders of the two provinces, Liu Chang and Yang You, and the military commanders Mu Kun, Duke of Qian, and Cao Kai, Earl of Fengrun, all held literary learning in high esteem. Grand Coordinator and Censor-in-chief Chen Jin expanded and renovated the examination compound, making it spacious and imposing. He issued renewed admonitions to all the offices, which complied without negligence. Cai Lian, Vice Director in the Ministry of Justice, happened to be reviewing prisoners’ cases there. Investigating Censors He Chen and Chen Ke, conducting inspection tours in their respective jurisdictions, encouraged these efforts. When the appointed time arrived, He Chen served as Supervising Official. Once every effort had been made to put the examination arrangements in order, then, in the eighth month, before the examination was to begin…

title: 弘治十四年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
二日率諸執事者入院遂昌
言于庭曰賓興俊乂
國家用人第一途脫毫髮弗公
弗慎即逃憲典能違物議乎
即違物議能逭鬼責乎凡有
事於此者各矢心滌慮以共
成我
===
國家之盛典以甄拔兩藩之真
才俾獲効用其尺寸固吾黨
以人事
君之心也僉曰敢不用命爰合提
學副使王臣沈垕所校士如
式圍棘試之越旬日誥等手
披目閱晝夜罔敢一息懈既
punctuated: 二日，率諸執事者入院，遂昌言于庭曰：「賓興俊乂，國家用人第一途。脫毫髮弗公弗慎，即逃憲典，能違物議乎？即違物議，能逭鬼責乎？凡有事於此者，各矢心滌慮，以共成我國家之盛典，以甄拔兩藩之真才，俾獲効用其尺寸，固吾黨以人事君之心也。」僉曰：「敢不用命！」爰合提學副使王臣、沈垕所校士，如式圍棘試之。越旬日，誥等手披目閱，晝夜罔敢一息懈。既
translation_en:
…two days before the examination, he led the functionaries into the examination compound and proclaimed in the courtyard: “Recommending worthy and talented men is the foremost means by which the state recruits men for service. Should there be the slightest unfairness or carelessness, even if one escapes the penalties of the law, can one evade public criticism? Even if one evades public criticism, can one escape the reproach of the spirits? All who have duties here must pledge their hearts and cleanse their thoughts, so that together we may bring this grand ceremony of our state to fulfillment and select the truly talented men of the two provinces, enabling them to put even their modest abilities to use. This is indeed our intention in serving the ruler by providing him with worthy men.” All replied: “We would not dare disobey!”
They then assembled the candidates whom Wang Chen and Shen Hou, surveillance vice commissioners for education, had assessed, enclosed the examination grounds with thorn barriers as prescribed, and examined them. Over the next ten days, Gao and his colleagues personally opened and read the scripts, not daring to relax for even a moment, day or night. Having…

title: 弘治十四年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
得其文理之優等者三倍額
數猶不敢自專復會衆校閱
一以理到辭達為主乃遵
制額祗取五十人既錄其名氏邑
里復取其文之優者錄於後
將獻諸
天子以傳示四方誥當序諸首惟
===
我
祖宗致治之道大綱小紀雖罔遺
闕而於學校科目尤慎且至
肆雲貴古滇國西南夷地自
漢歷唐雖載版圖然越居荒
逖勢不得比內郡而其人材
之著往牒者僅可僂指尋為
punctuated:
得其文理之優等者三倍額數，猶不敢自專，復會衆校閱，一以理到辭達為主，乃遵制額，祗取五十人。既錄其名氏邑里，復取其文之優者錄於後，將獻諸天子，以傳示四方。誥當序諸首。
惟我祖宗致治之道，大綱小紀，雖罔遺闕，而於學校科目尤慎且至。肆雲貴，古滇國西南夷地，自漢歷唐，雖載版圖，然越居荒逖，勢不得比內郡，而其人材之著往牒者，僅可僂指。尋為
translation_en:
…having selected papers outstanding in composition and reasoning, numbering three times the quota, we still did not dare decide on our own authority. We again assembled the examiners to review them, taking sound reasoning and clear expression as our sole criteria. We then complied with the prescribed quota and selected just fifty men. After recording their names and native localities, we also selected the best of their writings and transcribed them below. These will be presented to the Son of Heaven and circulated throughout the realm. It falls to me, Gao 誥, to place a preface at the beginning.
Considering the way our imperial ancestors brought about good government, nothing was omitted, whether in its broad principles or its detailed provisions; yet they were especially careful and thorough in matters of schools and civil-service examinations. Now Yunnan and Guizhou were formerly the territory of the ancient kingdom of Dian and the southwestern Yi. From the Han through the Tang, although included in the imperial domain, they lay far away in remote wilds, and their circumstances could not compare with those of the interior commanderies. The talented men from these lands whose names appeared in earlier records could be counted on one’s fingers. Before long, the region was…

title: 弘治十四年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
蒙段所據由宋及元淪胥異
域幾四百年竟遼邈無聞逮
我
太祖高皇帝綏定華夷然後盡入
職方顧惟百有三十年來治
化雖漸被而習俗猶未革宜
其人材之出未可遽倫諸藩
===
也而乃垂聲震烈濟濟彬彬
不相上下邇年守臣請加取
士之額
皇上慨賜允俞以獎進之是何其
鼓舞之神變化之速若此耶
誥聞之人才之生於世猶五
穀之植於壟畝也五穀之植
punctuated:
蒙段所據，由宋及元，淪胥異域幾四百年，竟遼邈無聞。逮我太祖高皇帝綏定華夷，然後盡入職方。顧惟百有三十年來，治化雖漸被，而習俗猶未革，宜其人材之出未可遽倫諸藩也。而乃垂聲震烈，濟濟彬彬，不相上下。邇年守臣請加取士之額，皇上慨賜允俞以獎進之，是何其鼓舞之神、變化之速若此耶？
誥聞之：人才之生於世，猶五穀之植於壟畝也。五穀之植
translation_en:
…occupied by the Meng and Duan houses, it remained in an alien domain from the Song through the Yuan, for nearly four hundred years, remote and unheard of throughout. Only when our Emperor Taizu Gao pacified the Chinese and the non-Chinese peoples did the entire region enter the empire’s territorial registers. Yet over these hundred and thirty years, although the transforming influence of good government has gradually spread there, local customs have still not been reformed. One might therefore expect that the talent emerging there could not immediately match that of the other provinces. Nevertheless, its men have won renown and displayed brilliant accomplishments; numerous and richly cultivated, they stand on an equal footing with their counterparts elsewhere. In recent years, the officials governing the region requested an increase in the quota for selecting examination graduates. His Majesty generously granted their request to encourage their advancement. How could such wonderfully effective encouragement and such rapid transformation have come about?
I, Gao, have heard that the emergence of talented men in the world resembles the planting of the five grains in the fields. The planting of the five grains…

title: 弘治十四年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
雖與凡卉均霑天地之氣化
然其培植長養得於人力者
為多故其成就視他草木獨
異無弗濟世用者若雲貴之
士被我
祖宗天涵地育之化無間諸藩而
列聖之所以陶鎔興作之者益有
===
加焉則其顒顒而出遠陋前
古而並軼諸藩者夫豈偶然
哉然則諸士子登名是錄者
回視前古之遭際何如而其
圖惟報稱豈可自儕於庸衆
人而已耶昔人有言以爵祿
榮遇之故而思効忠於上者
punctuated: 雖與凡卉均霑天地之氣化，然其培植長養得於人力者為多，故其成就視他草木獨異，無弗濟世用者。若雲貴之士，被我祖宗天涵地育之化，無間諸藩，而列聖之所以陶鎔興作之者益有加焉，則其顒顒而出，遠陋前古而並軼諸藩者，夫豈偶然哉？然則諸士子登名是錄者，回視前古之遭際何如？而其圖惟報稱，豈可自儕於庸衆人而已耶？昔人有言：「以爵祿榮遇之故而思効忠於上者，
translation_en:
…although they share equally with ordinary plants in the transforming forces of Heaven and Earth, their cultivation and growth depend largely on human effort. Thus, in their maturity they differ markedly from other vegetation: none fails to serve the needs of the world. Likewise, the scholars of Yunnan and Guizhou have received the transforming influence of our imperial ancestors, encompassing them like Heaven and nourishing them like Earth, no differently from those of the other provinces. Successive sage emperors have made ever greater efforts to mold and encourage them. How, then, could it be mere chance that they emerge in such dignified array, far surpassing their predecessors and matching or outstripping those of the other provinces?
Now, you scholars whose names appear in this record: looking back, how do your opportunities compare with those of earlier times? As you consider how to repay the favor you have received, can you be content merely to rank yourselves among ordinary men? Someone of old said: “Those who think of rendering loyal service to their sovereign because they have received rank, emoluments, honor, and favor …

title: 弘治十四年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
中人以下者之所為也若夫
豪傑之士雖無爵禄榮遇猶
思効忠况崇階厚給
湛恩渥典迥出他途萬萬者乎諸
生當有所處矣鄉試之錄凡
有事塲屋如提調監試考試
下逮受卷諸執事例得書則
===
既見於次簡如布政梁方黃
璉閻鉦按察使陳孜劉福叅
政黃東山徐節陳春副使王槐
王一言陳嵩毛科吳球包裕周
鳳隂子淑叅議郭緒張璿王杲
翁迪僉事胡榮曹佺范玶王
懋中龔嵩朱儀則皆秉德率令
punctuated:
中人以下者之所為也。若夫豪傑之士，雖無爵禄榮遇，猶思効忠，况崇階厚給、湛恩渥典，迥出他途萬萬者乎？諸生當有所處矣。
鄉試之錄，凡有事塲屋，如提調、監試、考試，下逮受卷諸執事，例得書，則既見於次簡。如布政梁方、黃璉、閻鉦，按察使陳孜、劉福，叅政黃東山、徐節、陳春，副使王槐、王一言、陳嵩、毛科、吳球、包裕、周鳳、隂子淑，叅議郭緒、張璿、王杲、翁迪，僉事胡榮、曹佺、范玶、王懋中、龔嵩、朱儀，則皆秉德率令
translation_en:
…is what men of middling ability or below would do. As for men of outstanding ability, even without rank, emoluments, or honorable treatment, they still aspire to serve loyally. How much more should they do so when granted lofty rank and generous stipends, profound favor and lavish privileges, exceeding by far those available through other avenues! You candidates should know what stance to take.
In the record of the Provincial Examination, all who served in the examination compound—from the Proctors, examination monitors, and Examiners down to the script receivers and other functionaries—are customarily entitled to have their names recorded; they already appear on the following leaves. As for Provincial Administration Commissioners Liang Fang, Huang Lian, and Yan Zheng; Surveillance Commissioners Chen Zi and Liu Fu; Administration Vice Commissioners Huang Dongshan, Xu Jie, and Chen Chun; Surveillance Vice Commissioners Wang Huai, Wang Yiyan, Chen Song, Mao Ke, Wu Qiu, Bao Yu, Zhou Feng, and Yin Zishu; Administration Assistant Commissioners Guo Xu, Zhang Xuan, Wang Gao, and Weng Di; and Surveillance Assistant Commissioners Hu Rong, Cao Quan, Fan Ping, Wang Maozhong, Gong Song, and Zhu Yi—all uphold virtue and follow good precepts…

title: 弘治十四年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
以造就人才於平日者法得
附見也因及之
湖廣德安府應城縣儒學教
諭歐陽誥謹序
punctuated:
以造就人才於平日者，法得附見也，因及之。
湖廣德安府應城縣儒學教諭歐陽誥謹序。
translation_en:
…and who foster talent in their everyday work. By the prescribed rules, they may be listed additionally; hence they are mentioned here.
Preface respectfully composed by Ouyang Gao, Instructor of the Confucian School of Yingcheng County, De’an Prefecture, Huguang.

title: 弘治十四年雲貴鄉試錄
text:

巡按雲南監察御史何琛〔廷獻四川成都後衛軍籍福建莆田縣人甲辰進士〕

punctuated:
弘治十四年雲貴鄉試。

監臨官：
巡按雲南監察御史何琛〔廷獻，四川成都後衛軍籍，福建莆田縣人，甲辰進士〕。

雲南等處承宣布政使司左布政使李韶〔克諧，四川富順縣人，戊戌進士〕。
雲南等處承宣布政使司右參政張朝用〔惟賢，四川瀘州人，甲辰進士〕。

監試官：
雲南等處提刑按察司副使曹玉〔德潤，應天府江寧縣人，戊戌進士〕。
雲南等處提刑按察司僉事郁容〔弘德，直隸常熟縣人，甲辰進士〕。

湖廣德安府應城縣儒學教諭歐陽誥〔賜之，江西泰和縣人，己酉貢士〕。
湖廣長沙府湘陰縣儒學教諭高巖〔維瞻，四川瀘州衛人，壬子貢士〕。

直隸鳳陽府臨淮縣儒學教諭泰煜〔德輝，浙江慈谿縣人，己酉貢士〕。
湖廣荆州府松滋縣儒學教諭王世雍〔仲和，廣西柳城縣人，戊午貢士〕。

translation_en:
Yunnan–Guizhou Provincial Examination, the fourteenth year of Hongzhi (1501).

Supervising Official:
He Chen, Investigating Censor on inspection duty in Yunnan. His courtesy name was Tingxian; he held military registration in the Chengdu Rear Guard, Sichuan, and was a native of Putian County, Fujian. He became a metropolitan graduate (jinshi) in the jiachen year.

Proctors:
Li Shao, Left Provincial Administration Commissioner of Yunnan. His courtesy name was Kexie; he was a native of Fushun County, Sichuan, and became a metropolitan graduate in the wuxu year.
Zhang Chaoyong, Right Administration Vice Commissioner of Yunnan. His courtesy name was Weixian; he was a native of Luzhou, Sichuan, and became a metropolitan graduate in the jiachen year.

Cao Yu, Surveillance Vice Commissioner of Yunnan. His courtesy name was Derun; he was a native of Jiangning County, Yingtian Prefecture, and became a metropolitan graduate in the wuxu year.

Ouyang Gao, Instructor at the Confucian school of Yingcheng County, De’an Prefecture, Huguang. His courtesy name was Cizhi; he was a native of Taihe County, Jiangxi, and became a tribute scholar (gongshi) in the jiyou year.

Wang Bao, School Director at the Confucian school of Guang’an Subprefecture, Shunqing Prefecture, Sichuan. His courtesy name was Shiyong; he was a native of Macheng County, Huguang, and became a tribute scholar in the renzi year.
Tai Yu, Instructor at the Confucian school of Linhuai County, Fengyang Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. His courtesy name was Dehui; he was a native of Cixi County, Zhejiang, and became a tribute scholar in the jiyou year.
Wang Shiyong, Instructor at the Confucian school of Songzi County, Jingzhou Prefecture, Huguang. His courtesy name was Zhonghe; he was a native of Liucheng County, Guangxi, and became a tribute scholar in the wuwu year.
Zhang Qiu, Assistant Instructor at the Confucian school of Jinxian County, Nanchang Prefecture, Jiangxi. His courtesy name was Zongshao; he was a native of Nanhai County, Guangdong, and became a tribute scholar in the gengzi year.
Pan Xiang, Assistant Instructor at the Confucian school of Guangze County, Shaowu Prefecture, Fujian. His courtesy name was Botu; he was a native of Nanhai County, Guangdong, and became a tribute scholar in the renzi year.

title: 弘治十四年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
印卷官
雲南等處承宣布政使司照磨所照磨杜培〔本齋浙江平陽縣人由吏員〕
雲南等處提刑按察司經歷司知事程樂〔正聲江西餘干縣人由監生〕

===

punctuated:

雲南等處承宣布政使司照磨所照磨杜培〔本齋，浙江平陽縣人，由吏員〕。
雲南等處提刑按察司經歷司知事程樂〔正聲，江西餘干縣人，由監生〕。

安寧州知州陳亮〔志明，直隸廣德州人，戊戌進士〕。

彌封官
雲南府晉寧州知州喻敬〔脩巳，四川內江縣人，癸卯貢士〕。
雲南府昆陽州知州林昕〔以耀，廣東揭陽縣人，庚子貢士〕。

浪穹縣縣丞王雄〔世傑，順天府永清縣人，癸丑進士〕。
translation_en:

title: 弘治十四年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
第壹場
四書
事其大夫之賢者友其士之仁者
故君子不動而敬不言而信
其為氣也至大至剛以直養而無害則塞
于天地之間其為氣也配義與道無是
餒也是集義所生者非義襲而取之也
行有不慊於心則餒矣我故曰告子未
嘗知義以其外之也必有事焉而勿正
===
心勿忘勿助長也
易
比輔也下順從也原筮元永貞无咎以剛
中也
象曰風自火出家人君子以言有物而行
有恒初九閑有家悔亡
易知則有親
君子藏器於身待時而動何不利之有
書
punctuated:
第壹場

四書

事其大夫之賢者，友其士之仁者。

故君子不動而敬，不言而信。

其為氣也，至大至剛，以直養而無害，則塞于天地之間。其為氣也，配義與道；無是，餒也。是集義所生者，非義襲而取之也。行有不慊於心，則餒矣。我故曰：「告子未嘗知義，以其外之也。」必有事焉，而勿正；心勿忘，勿助長也。

易

比，輔也，下順從也。原筮，元永貞，无咎，以剛中也。

象曰：「風自火出，家人。君子以言有物而行有恒。」初九，閑有家，悔亡。

易知則有親。

君子藏器於身，待時而動，何不利之有？

書
translation_en:
First Session

Four Books

Serve the worthy among their great officers, and befriend the humane among their scholars.

Thus the gentleman commands respect without acting and inspires trust without speaking.

As vital energy, it is supremely great and supremely firm. If nourished with uprightness and left unharmed, it fills the space between Heaven and Earth. As vital energy, it accords with righteousness and the Way; without these, it starves. It is produced by the accumulation of righteous deeds, rather than acquired through an isolated act of righteousness. If one's conduct leaves the heart dissatisfied, it starves. Thus I say: “Gaozi has never understood righteousness, because he regards it as external.” One must constantly attend to its cultivation without anticipating the result; the heart must neither forget it nor help it grow by force.

Book of Changes

Bi (Holding Together) means support: those below comply and follow. “Examine through divination whether there is fundamental goodness, constancy, and correctness; there will be no blame”—because the firm line occupies the central position.

The Image says: “Wind issues from fire: Jiaren (The Family). The gentleman accordingly gives substance to his words and constancy to his conduct.” Nine in the first place: Establish restraints within the household; regret disappears.

Being easy to understand brings affection.

The gentleman stores his capacities within himself and waits for the proper time to act. What could fail to be advantageous?

Book of Documents

title: 弘治十四年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
敷奏以言明試以功
王懋乃德視乃烈祖無時豫怠奉先思孝
接下思恭視遠惟明聽德惟聰
弘敷五典式和民則爾身克正罔敢弗正
民心罔中惟爾之中夏暑雨小民惟曰
怨咨冬祁寒小民亦惟曰怨咨厥惟艱
哉思其艱以圖其易民乃寧嗚呼丕顯
哉文王謨丕承哉武王烈啓佑我後人
咸以正罔缺
===
出入起居罔有不欽發號施令罔有不臧
詩
升彼虛矣以望楚矣望楚與堂景山與京
降觀于桑卜云其吉終焉允臧靈雨既
零命彼倌人星言夙駕說于桑田匪直
也人秉心塞淵騋牝三千
伐鼓淵淵振旅闐闐
申伯番番既入于謝徒御啴啴周邦咸喜
戎有良翰不顯申伯王之元舅文武是
punctuated:
敷奏以言，明試以功。

王懋乃德，視乃烈祖，無時豫怠。奉先思孝，接下思恭。視遠惟明，聽德惟聰。

弘敷五典，式和民則。爾身克正，罔敢弗正。民心罔中，惟爾之中。

夏暑雨，小民惟曰怨咨；冬祁寒，小民亦惟曰怨咨。厥惟艱哉！思其艱，以圖其易，民乃寧。

嗚呼！丕顯哉，文王謨！丕承哉，武王烈！啓佑我後人，咸以正罔缺。

出入起居，罔有不欽；發號施令，罔有不臧。

詩

升彼虛矣，以望楚矣。望楚與堂，景山與京。降觀于桑，卜云其吉，終焉允臧。靈雨既零，命彼倌人，星言夙駕，說于桑田。匪直也人，秉心塞淵，騋牝三千。

伐鼓淵淵，振旅闐闐。

申伯番番，既入于謝，徒御啴啴，周邦咸喜。戎有良翰，不顯申伯，王之元舅，文武是
translation_en:
Have them present their proposals in words, and clearly test them through their accomplishments.

O king, cultivate your virtue and look to your illustrious ancestors; never give yourself to ease or indolence. In serving your ancestors, think of filial devotion; in dealing with those below, think of respect. Clear sight consists in seeing far; keen hearing consists in listening to virtue.

Widely promulgate the five teachings, thereby harmonizing the people's standards of conduct. If you yourself can be upright, none will dare to be otherwise. The people's hearts have no fixed mean; they take your mean as their own.

In summer's heat and rain, the common people voice only complaints and sighs; in winter's severe cold, the common people likewise voice only complaints and sighs. How difficult their circumstances are! Consider their hardships and devise ways to ease them; then the people will be at peace.

Ah! How greatly illustrious were King Wen's plans! How magnificently King Wu carried them forward in his achievements! They opened the way for and aided us, their descendants, always through what was right, without deficiency.

In going out and coming in, in rising and resting, let there be nothing lacking in reverence; in issuing proclamations and commands, let there be nothing that is not good.

Book of Odes

He ascended that height to look toward Chu. He surveyed Chu and Tang, measured the hills and heights. Descending, he examined the mulberry trees. The divination declared the site auspicious; in the end it proved truly good. When the timely rain had fallen, he ordered the carriage attendant to harness the horses early, beneath the stars, and halted among the mulberry fields. Nor was this all: this man held a sincere and profound purpose in his heart; his tall horses and mares numbered three thousand.

They beat the drums with deep resounding rolls; they marshalled the troops with thunderous clamour.

The Earl of Shen, vigorous and imposing, had entered Xie. His foot soldiers and charioteers were numerous; all the realm of Zhou rejoiced. You have a worthy pillar of support! How illustrious is the Earl of Shen, the king's eldest maternal uncle! Wen and Wu are those whom he …

憲。

禮記

translation_en:
