title: 弘治十四年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
紀綱既正天下大定
凡人之所以為人者禮義也禮義之始在
於正容體齊顏色順辭令容體正顏色
齊辭令順而后禮義備以正君臣親父
子和長幼君臣正父子親長幼和而后
禮義立故冠而后服備服備而后容體
正顏色齊辭令順故曰冠者禮之始也
是故古者聖王重冠
第貳場
===
論
孟子以道自任
詔誥表〔內科一道〕
擬漢令禮官勸學興禮詔〔元朔五年〕
擬唐以户部侍郎裴垍為中書侍郎同平
章事誥〔元和三年〕
擬宋龍圖閣直學士趙汝愚進名臣奏議
表〔淳熙十三年〕
判語〔五條〕
punctuated:
紀綱既正，天下大定。
凡人之所以為人者，禮義也。禮義之始，在於正容體、齊顏色、順辭令。容體正，顏色齊，辭令順，而后禮義備，以正君臣、親父子、和長幼。君臣正，父子親，長幼和，而后禮義立。故冠而后服備，服備而后容體正、顏色齊、辭令順。故曰：「冠者，禮之始也。」是故古者聖王重冠。
第貳場
論
孟子以道自任。
詔誥表〔內科一道〕
擬漢令禮官勸學興禮詔〔元朔五年〕。
擬唐以户部侍郎裴垍為中書侍郎同平章事誥〔元和三年〕。
擬宋龍圖閣直學士趙汝愚進名臣奏議表〔淳熙十三年〕。
判語〔五條〕
translation_en:
…Once the governing order is set right, all under Heaven is firmly settled.

What makes human beings human is ritual propriety and righteousness. These begin with making one’s bearing correct, one’s expression composed, and one’s speech appropriate. Once bearing is correct, expression composed, and speech appropriate, ritual propriety and righteousness are complete, serving to make relations between ruler and minister correct, those between father and son affectionate, and those between elders and juniors harmonious. Once these relations are correct, affectionate, and harmonious, ritual propriety and righteousness are established. Thus, only after the capping ceremony is one’s attire complete; only when one’s attire is complete are one’s bearing correct, expression composed, and speech appropriate. Hence the saying: “Capping is the beginning of ritual.” For this reason, the sage kings of antiquity attached great importance to capping.

Second Session

Discourse
Mencius took responsibility for the Way upon himself.

Imperial Edicts, Proclamations, and Memorials 〔One question within this category [?].〕
Compose, in the voice of a Han emperor, an edict ordering the ritual officials to encourage learning and promote ritual observance. 〔Fifth year of Yuanshuo.〕

Compose, in the voice of a Tang emperor, a proclamation appointing Pei Ji, Vice Minister of Revenue, as Vice Director of the Secretariat and Chief Minister. 〔Third year of Yuanhe.〕

Compose, in the voice of Zhao Ruyu, Auxiliary Academician of the Longtu Pavilion under the Song, a memorial submitting Memorials and Deliberations of Eminent Ministers. 〔Thirteenth year of Chunxi.〕

Legal Judgments 〔Five items.〕

title: 弘治十四年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
官員赴任過限
丁夫差遣不平
禁止師巫邪術
縱放軍人歇役
子孫違犯教令
第叄塲
策五道
問我
太祖髙皇帝以神武定天下其除亂之功比迹
===
湯武而時勢之難為有甚焉者及其治
定之後又有
大誥三編頒示天下蓋與湯誥之誕告萬方酒
誥之明大命于妹邦同一與民更始之
意也蓋嘗伏而讀之竊有疑焉湯武之
誥纔數十言而止而
三誥之為言乃至二百四條一不已而至于再
再不已而至于三其化導之難易不同
如此者何也抑不知其化之之大意導
punctuated:
官員赴任過限。
丁夫差遣不平。
禁止師巫邪術。
縱放軍人歇役。
子孫違犯教令。

第叄塲
策五道

問：我太祖髙皇帝以神武定天下，其除亂之功比迹湯武，而時勢之難為有甚焉者。及其治定之後，又有《大誥》三編頒示天下，蓋與《湯誥》之誕告萬方、《酒誥》之明大命于妹邦，同一與民更始之意也。蓋嘗伏而讀之，竊有疑焉：湯武之誥纔數十言而止，而三誥之為言乃至二百四條，一不已而至于再，再不已而至于三，其化導之難易不同如此者，何也？抑不知其化之之大意、導
translation_en:
Officials exceeding the time limit for reporting to their posts.
Inequitable assignment of adult male laborers to service.
Prohibiting the heterodox arts of ritual masters and spirit mediums.
Allowing soldiers to cease performing their service.
Sons and grandsons violating instructions and commands.

Third Session
Five Policy Questions

Question: Our Emperor Taizu Gao used his divine martial prowess to bring peace to All under Heaven. His achievement in eliminating disorder matched those of Tang and Wu, yet the circumstances of his time posed even greater difficulties. After he had established orderly government, he also promulgated throughout the realm the three compilations of the Grand Pronouncements (Da Gao). These shared the intention of making a fresh beginning with the people expressed in the Announcement of Tang, which proclaimed broadly to the myriad regions, and in the Announcement on Alcohol, which made the great command clear in the state of Mei.

Having humbly read these texts, we venture to express a doubt. The announcements of Tang and Wu amounted to no more than a few dozen words, whereas the Three Pronouncements extend to as many as 204 articles. One compilation did not suffice, so a second followed; the second did not suffice, so a third followed. Why was there such a difference in the difficulty or ease of transforming and guiding the people? Yet we wonder whether the broad intent behind transforming them, and the guiding …

title: 弘治十四年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
之之大法亦有同焉者否也夫巍巍成
功振耀千古洋洋
聖謨流布天下雖在凡民亦與知之況豪傑之
士乎此有司策士所以首舉為問之意
也
問虞舜以五臣興周文以四友隆古之帝
王未有不得賢人而共理者也然載籍
所記博乎難以議矣姑舉漢世言之則
在高帝有所謂三傑者有所謂四皓者
===
在武帝有所謂三儒者其人品之優劣
可悉得而言歟抑西京之賢尚有出於
三傑四皓三儒之外者歟而當時致治
之盛果皆出於此乎否也考論古人賢
否蓋欲因以觀諸士子尚友之志幸毋
以不暇畧之
問地陰也法當安靜邇者雲南宜良諸郡
縣地震壞民廬舍壓損人物者凡若干
上聞
punctuated:
之之大法，亦有同焉者否也？夫巍巍成功，振耀千古；洋洋聖謨，流布天下。雖在凡民，亦與知之，況豪傑之士乎？此有司策士所以首舉為問之意也。
問：虞舜以五臣興，周文以四友隆。古之帝王，未有不得賢人而共理者也。然載籍所記，博乎難以議矣。姑舉漢世言之，則在高帝，有所謂三傑者，有所謂四皓者；在武帝，有所謂三儒者。其人品之優劣，可悉得而言歟？抑西京之賢，尚有出於三傑、四皓、三儒之外者歟？而當時致治之盛，果皆出於此乎否也？考論古人賢否，蓋欲因以觀諸士子尚友之志，幸毋以不暇畧之。
問：地，陰也，法當安靜。邇者雲南宜良諸郡縣地震，壞民廬舍，壓損人物者凡若干，上聞
translation_en:
…whether the great methods by which they guided the people also had anything in common? Lofty indeed are the achievements, shining through the ages; abundant are the sagely counsels, disseminated throughout the realm. Even ordinary people have a share in knowing them; how much more, then, men of outstanding talent? This is why the responsible officials have made this the first question in examining candidates through policy essays.
Question: Shun of Yu rose with the aid of five ministers, and King Wen of Zhou flourished with the aid of four friends. Among the emperors and kings of antiquity, none failed to obtain worthy men with whom to govern. Yet the accounts in historical writings are so extensive that they are difficult to discuss comprehensively. Let us take the Han dynasty alone: under Emperor Gao there were the so-called Three Heroes and the so-called Four Hoary Elders; under Emperor Wu there were the so-called Three Confucian Scholars. Can you fully explain the relative merits of their personal character? Were there, moreover, worthy men of the Western Han beyond these Three Heroes, Four Hoary Elders, and Three Confucian Scholars? And was the flourishing government achieved at that time indeed entirely due to these men, or not? In examining and discussing whether men of antiquity were worthy, we seek to discern your aspirations, as candidates, to take the ancients as friends. Please do not omit this on the grounds of insufficient time.
Question: Earth is yin and should, by its proper pattern, remain peaceful and still. Recently, earthquakes struck Yiliang and other prefectures and counties in Yunnan, destroying the people's dwellings and crushing and injuring people and other living things in considerable numbers. The matter was reported upward …

title: 弘治十四年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
九重
天子軫念遠遣禮官祭告厥咎何由夫變不虛
生必有感召載之前史固不可誣即今
論之
天子致中和於上大臣脩職業於下宜其海岳
效靈罔有變異而乃如此豈天心仁愛
欲以戒懼吾
君俾益保治於無窮歟抑滇南一方政事亦有
所缺失也夫六事自責者大旱而雨脩
===
正厥事者雉雊不妖則人事之脩豈獨
在於君當然耶抑為之臣者固可漠然
不加意也茲欲考求其故而消弭之以
應上天示戒之意以少紓
九重懼災之心何為而可諸生志懷經綸之業
目擊閭閻之事當亦籌畫於中久矣願
悉言之以助有司之不及
問考課之法虞周所不廢自漢以來其品
式之疎密事權之分合甲乙之等批書
punctuated:
九重。天子軫念，遠遣禮官祭告。厥咎何由？夫變不虛生，必有感召，載之前史，固不可誣。即今論之，天子致中和於上，大臣脩職業於下，宜其海岳效靈，罔有變異，而乃如此，豈天心仁愛，欲以戒懼吾君，俾益保治於無窮歟？抑滇南一方政事亦有所缺失也？夫六事自責者，大旱而雨；脩正厥事者，雉雊不妖。則人事之脩，豈獨在於君當然耶？抑為之臣者，固可漠然不加意也？茲欲考求其故而消弭之，以應上天示戒之意，以少紓九重懼災之心，何為而可？諸生志懷經綸之業，目擊閭閻之事，當亦籌畫於中久矣。願悉言之，以助有司之不及。

問：考課之法，虞周所不廢。自漢以來，其品式之疎密、事權之分合、甲乙之等、批書
translation_en:
…the imperial court. Deeply concerned, the Son of Heaven dispatched ritual officials to that distant region to offer sacrifices and report to the spirits. What has occasioned this calamity? Anomalies do not arise without cause; something must call them forth. The records of earlier histories certainly cannot be dismissed as false. Considering the present, the Son of Heaven brings about equilibrium and harmony above, while the great ministers discharge their duties below. Surely the seas and mountains should manifest their beneficent powers, and no anomalies should occur. Yet things have come to this. Is Heaven, in its benevolence, seeking to admonish and alarm our ruler, so that he may further preserve good government forever? Or are there shortcomings in the administration of the Diannan region?

When a ruler reproached himself on six counts, rain fell during a great drought; when another corrected his conduct of affairs, the crowing of a pheasant ceased to portend evil. Is the duty of setting human affairs in order incumbent upon the ruler alone? May his ministers remain indifferent and pay no heed? We now wish to investigate the causes and eliminate the calamity, responding to Heaven’s intention in issuing its warning and somewhat relieving His Majesty’s anxiety over the disaster. What measures would accomplish this? You students aspire to the work of ordering the realm and have witnessed the affairs of ordinary households. Surely you have long been considering plans in your minds. Please state them fully, to supply what the responsible authorities have failed to achieve.

Question: The system of assessing officials’ performance was maintained under both Yu and Zhou. Since the Han, the varying strictness of its grading procedures, the division or concentration of authority, the grades of A and B, and the written assessments…

title: 弘治十四年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
之辭往往可見至于任事之臣其志尚
亦人人殊有掩過揚善而無所按驗者
有不鞫臧罪而猾惡自禁者其存心何
其恕也有條奏貪殘五十餘人而天下
肅然者有奏舉貪汙十餘人而海內翕
然者其用法何其嚴也內外考績入中
上者纔五十人此則疑于刻督運失米
改判註者至一再變此則疑于專選人
匿喪廢之終身將以振風義也顧亦有
===
===
官吏小過不忍捃拾者矣監司不才付
之一筆將以利生民也顧亦有下位小
節不欲摘發者矣是皆一時任事之臣
有聲績可稱者也而或寬或嚴人自為
治如此不知于法亦有戾乎否也
國朝考課之法一以虞周為準邇年以來法
外之意時有損益盖
九重之上主于愛惜人才而百僚之間皆能將
順
punctuated:
之辭，往往可見。至于任事之臣，其志尚亦人人殊。有掩過揚善而無所按驗者，有不鞫臧罪而猾惡自禁者，其存心何其恕也！有條奏貪殘五十餘人而天下肅然者，有奏舉貪汙十餘人而海內翕然者，其用法何其嚴也！內外考績，入中上者纔五十人，此則疑于刻；督運失米，改判註者至一再變，此則疑于專。選人匿喪，廢之終身，將以振風義也，顧亦有官吏小過不忍捃拾者矣；監司不才，付之一筆，將以利生民也，顧亦有下位小節不欲摘發者矣。是皆一時任事之臣，有聲績可稱者也，而或寬或嚴，人自為治如此，不知于法亦有戾乎否也？
國朝考課之法，一以虞周為準。邇年以來，法外之意，時有損益。盖九重之上，主于愛惜人才，而百僚之間，皆能將順
translation_en:
…the wording of the written assessments can frequently be found. As for the ministers charged with these duties, their aspirations and preferences also differed from person to person. Some concealed faults and commended good qualities without conducting investigations; some did not interrogate those accused of corruption, yet the cunning and wicked restrained themselves. How forgiving their intentions were! Some submitted itemized accusations against more than fifty greedy and oppressive officials, and all under Heaven stood in awe; some impeached more than ten corrupt officials, and the whole realm united in approval. How strict their application of the law was! In evaluations of officials serving within and outside the capital, only fifty attained the middle or upper grades: this seems excessively harsh. In a case involving grain lost under transport supervision, the recorded judgment was revised once and then again: this seems arbitrary [?]. A candidate for appointment concealed a bereavement and was barred from office for life, with the intention of upholding moral conduct and duty; yet there were also those who could not bear to ferret out officials’ minor faults. An incompetent surveillance official was dismissed with a stroke of the brush, with the intention of benefiting the people; yet there were also those who did not wish to expose minor failings among their subordinates. These were all ministers entrusted with responsibilities in their day, whose reputations and achievements deserved praise. Yet some were lenient and others strict, each administering affairs in his own way. We wonder whether this also contravened the law.
Our dynasty’s system of evaluating officials takes the practices of Yu and Zhou as its sole standard. In recent years, considerations beyond the letter of the law have at times led to adjustments. For His Majesty’s overriding concern is to cherish talented men, and all the officials are able to support and carry forward…

title: 弘治十四年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
德意故綜核雖嚴而不流于刻文法雖密而
不過于察此皆諸生耳目之所親見者
也請具陳之或別有所見可裨時政者
幸亦以相告庶執事者聞之或有取焉
問夷狄自古為中國患而禦之未嘗無人
如居鴈門而匈奴不敢犯邊守雲中而
匈奴深畏其畧或誘鮮卑擊弱匈奴而
邊無寇警或於學行禮陳說道義而單
于懷服有并州都督賢於長城者有隴
===
州刺史威振北方者有請城方渠以遏
吐蕃歸路者有總十一軍以築三城於
要路者定兵精勁齊一而聲動虜中其
謀猶何克壯也詔書犒賞而諸羌始為
漢用其人心何遽服也之數人之功烈
可詳言歟洪惟我
國家之於戎狄其綏之之道馭之之法無容
議矣比者醜虜大舉入寇致厪
宵旰之慮遣將出師逐之則潜跡而遁緩之
punctuated:
德意，故綜核雖嚴而不流于刻，文法雖密而不過于察。此皆諸生耳目之所親見者也，請具陳之。或別有所見可裨時政者，幸亦以相告，庶執事者聞之，或有取焉。

問：夷狄自古為中國患，而禦之未嘗無人。如居鴈門而匈奴不敢犯邊，守雲中而匈奴深畏其畧；或誘鮮卑擊弱匈奴而邊無寇警，或於學行禮、陳說道義而單于懷服。有并州都督賢於長城者，有隴州刺史威振北方者，有請城方渠以遏吐蕃歸路者，有總十一軍以築三城於要路者。定兵精勁齊一而聲動虜中，其謀猶何克壯也？詔書犒賞而諸羌始為漢用，其人心何遽服也？之數人之功烈，可詳言歟？洪惟我國家之於戎狄，其綏之之道、馭之之法，無容議矣。比者醜虜大舉入寇，致厪宵旰之慮。遣將出師逐之，則潜跡而遁；緩之
translation_en:
…the imperial benevolent intentions. Thus, although scrutiny of performance is strict, it does not lapse into harshness; although administrative regulations are detailed, their enforcement is not excessively intrusive. These are all things that you candidates have personally witnessed or heard. Please set them out fully. If you have other insights that might benefit current governance, kindly communicate those as well, so that the officials responsible may hear them and perhaps adopt something from them.

Question: From antiquity, the Yi and Di peoples have troubled the Central Kingdom, yet there have always been men capable of resisting them. One was stationed at Yanmen, and the Xiongnu dared not violate the frontier; another defended Yunzhong, and the Xiongnu deeply feared his strategy. One induced the Xianbei to attack and weaken the Xiongnu, leaving the frontier free of alarms about incursions; another performed rites at a school and expounded the Way and righteousness, winning the chanyu’s allegiance. There was a Commander-in-Chief of Bingzhou who was worth more than the Great Wall, and a Regional Inspector of Longzhou whose might awed the north. One requested that Fangqu be fortified to block the Tibetans’ route of return; another commanded eleven armies to build three fortified towns along strategic routes. Troops were made elite, strong, and united [?], and their reputation shook the enemy: how did his strategic plans achieve such strength? An imperial edict bestowed rewards, and the various Qiang peoples began to serve the Han: why did their hearts submit so readily? Can you explain in detail the achievements of these men?

Now, considering our great dynasty’s dealings with the Rong and Di peoples, its methods of pacifying and controlling them admit of no criticism. Recently, the vile enemy invaded in great force, causing His Majesty anxiety from before dawn until late at night. When generals are dispatched with troops to pursue them, they conceal their tracks and flee; when pressure on them is relaxed…

title: 弘治十四年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
則乗間而來兹欲挫其鋒使彼逺遁而
不敢復來散其黨使彼孤立而不能為
患其術將何為而可請著于篇行將為
子
獻焉
punctuated: 則乗間而來。兹欲挫其鋒，使彼逺遁而不敢復來；散其黨，使彼孤立而不能為患，其術將何為而可？請著于篇，行將為子獻焉。
translation_en: …then they seize an opening and return. Now, if we wish to blunt their offensive so that they flee far away and dare not return, and disperse their confederates so that they stand isolated and cannot cause trouble, what methods would accomplish this? Please set forth your answer in writing; I shall then submit it to the throne on your behalf.

title: 弘治十四年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
第壹場
四書
事其大夫之賢者友其士之仁者
王仲仁
同考試官教諭王批揭書出題示公也塲中
作者類多浮詞惟此篇純正簡潔如渾金美玉自然
令人把玩不厭也錄之以為求仁者式
考試官教諭高批簡明可取
考試官教諭歐陽批當時聖人教子貢意
===
摹寫殆盡
聖人告賢者為仁惟隨所與而得其人焉蓋為
仁貴乎慎所與也今於大夫之賢而事之士之
仁而友之則得其人矣為仁之道豈外是哉宜
吾夫子以是為子貢告也今夫為仁之道固由
於已亦資乎人是故一邦之中有大夫焉大夫
不賢不事可也彼德足以尊主庇民仁足以敦
化善俗非大夫之賢者乎不有以事之則此心
無所依歸如為仁何必也傾心奉承無傲惰也
punctuated:
第壹場
四書
「事其大夫之賢者，友其士之仁者。」
王仲仁

同考試官教諭王批：揭書出題，示公也。塲中作者類多浮詞，惟此篇純正簡潔，如渾金美玉，自然令人把玩不厭也。錄之以為求仁者式。
考試官教諭高批：簡明可取。
考試官教諭歐陽批：當時聖人教子貢意，摹寫殆盡。

聖人告賢者為仁，惟隨所與而得其人焉。蓋為仁貴乎慎所與也。今於大夫之賢而事之，士之仁而友之，則得其人矣。為仁之道豈外是哉？宜吾夫子以是為子貢告也。今夫為仁之道，固由於已，亦資乎人。是故一邦之中有大夫焉，大夫不賢，不事可也。彼德足以尊主庇民，仁足以敦化善俗，非大夫之賢者乎？不有以事之，則此心無所依歸，如為仁何？必也傾心奉承，無傲惰也，
translation_en:
First Session
Four Books
“Serve the worthy among its grandees, and befriend the benevolent among its gentlemen.”
Wang Zhongren

Comment by Associate Examiner Wang, Instructor: Opening the book and selecting the topic demonstrates impartiality. Most candidates in the examination hall resorted to empty verbiage. This essay alone is pure, sound, concise, and clear, like unrefined gold or fine jade: one naturally delights in examining it without tiring. It is recorded here as a model for those seeking benevolence.

Comment by Examiner Gao, Instructor: Concise and clear; worthy of acceptance.

Comment by Examiner Ouyang, Instructor: It conveys almost completely what the Sage intended when he instructed Zigong on that occasion.

When the Sage instructed a worthy man in practicing benevolence, he taught him simply to find the right people among those with whom he associated. For in practicing benevolence, one must above all take care in choosing one’s associates. If one serves the worthy among the grandees and befriends the benevolent among the gentlemen, one has found the right people. Could the way of practicing benevolence lie beyond this? It was fitting that our Master should give Zigong this instruction.

Now, the way of practicing benevolence certainly depends on oneself, yet it also draws support from others. Thus, within a state there are grandees. If a grandee is not worthy, one may refrain from serving him. But one whose virtue suffices to honor his ruler and protect the people, and whose benevolence suffices to strengthen moral transformation and improve customs—is he not a worthy grandee? Unless one finds a way to serve him, the heart has nowhere to turn for support: how, then, can one practice benevolence? One must therefore serve him wholeheartedly, without arrogance or indolence, …

title: 弘治十四年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
虛己聽順無敢慢也所謂用下敬上者在是豈
曰禮貌云乎哉一國之內有士焉士而未仁不
友可也彼窮居而脩身以道側陋而脩道以仁
非士之仁者乎不有以友之則此心無所嚮慕
如為仁何必也合志同方而契結金蘭也營道
同術而情投膠漆也所謂久要不忘者在是豈
徒面交而已哉夫事大夫之賢者則彼賢而我
不賢有以興其嚴憚之心友士之仁者則彼仁
而我不仁有以賴其切磋之力為仁有所資矣
===
尚何德之不成哉抑考聖門之徒問仁者眾而
聖人告之各異姑舉其槩若顏子問仁則告以
克己復禮仲弓問仁則告以主敬行恕司馬牛
問仁則曰其言也訒樊遲問仁則曰先難後獲
至此子貢問仁則又以是告之蓋子貢為人病
在悅不若己者無非因人而成就之也厥後子
貢性與天道之悟天階日月之喻不有得於今
日之力歟
故君子不動而敬不言而信
punctuated:
虛己聽順，無敢慢也。所謂用下敬上者在是，豈曰禮貌云乎哉？一國之內有士焉，士而未仁，不友可也。彼窮居而脩身以道，側陋而脩道以仁，非士之仁者乎？不有以友之，則此心無所嚮慕，如為仁何？必也合志同方，而契結金蘭也；營道同術，而情投膠漆也。所謂久要不忘者在是，豈徒面交而已哉？夫事大夫之賢者，則彼賢而我不賢，有以興其嚴憚之心；友士之仁者，則彼仁而我不仁，有以賴其切磋之力。為仁有所資矣，尚何德之不成哉？抑考聖門之徒，問仁者眾，而聖人告之各異。姑舉其槩：若顏子問仁，則告以克己復禮；仲弓問仁，則告以主敬行恕；司馬牛問仁，則曰其言也訒；樊遲問仁，則曰先難後獲。至此子貢問仁，則又以是告之。蓋子貢為人，病在悅不若己者，無非因人而成就之也。厥後子貢性與天道之悟，天階日月之喻，不有得於今日之力歟？

故君子不動而敬，不言而信。
translation_en:
…Humbly listen and comply, never daring to be negligent. This is what it means to show respect to superiors from a subordinate position. Could it refer merely to outward courtesy? Within a state there are scholars. If a scholar is not yet humane, one may refrain from befriending him. But those who, dwelling in straitened circumstances, cultivate themselves through the Way, and who, living in obscurity, cultivate the Way through humaneness—are these not humane scholars? Unless one befriends them, the heart has no one to admire and aspire to emulate. How, then, can one practice humaneness? One must share their aspirations and follow the same course, forming a bond firm as metal and fragrant as orchids; pursue the Way through the same methods, with affections adhering like glue and lacquer. This is what it means never to forget an old pledge. Could it amount merely to a superficial acquaintance? When one serves a worthy grand master, his worthiness and one’s own lack of it awaken a sense of reverent awe. When one befriends a humane scholar, his humaneness and one’s own lack of it allow one to benefit from the refining power of mutual instruction. With such support for practicing humaneness, what virtue could fail to be perfected?

Moreover, if we examine the disciples in the Sage’s school, many asked about humaneness, yet the Sage answered each differently. To give only the broad outlines: when Master Yan asked about humaneness, he was told to overcome the self and return to ritual propriety; when Zhonggong asked, he was told to make reverence his guiding principle and practice reciprocity; when Sima Niu asked, the reply was to be restrained in speech; when Fan Chi asked, the reply was to put difficult tasks first and rewards afterward. Here, when Zigong asked about humaneness, he was given this further instruction. For Zigong’s failing lay in delighting in those inferior to himself; the Sage’s instruction was entirely intended to perfect him according to his particular character. Later, Zigong attained an understanding of human nature and the Way of Heaven, and offered the analogies of a stairway to Heaven and of the sun and moon. Did these achievements not owe something to the effort begun on this occasion?

Thus the gentleman commands respect without acting and inspires trust without speaking.

title: 弘治十四年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
楊士雲
同考試官訓導張批題主存養之功說而不
動不言難於措辭此作會理成章其有得於心學者
同考試官教諭秦批此篇於敬信上用心事
講最為得旨
考試官教諭高批上達事最難於言吾
於子有取矣
考試官教諭歐陽批存養事非體認真切
者不能道此作得之
===
君子於未然之時而存本然之天其為己之功
密矣蓋敬信本然之天也君子不待言動而此
心存焉則為己之功孰有加於是哉中庸三十
三章自下學立心之始推而言之及此謂夫君
子為己之學當何如其用功耶是故人不能以
無動也然當萬念未萌一物未接之時則不動
矣斯時也或可少忽而君子之心則不敢忽兢
兢焉儼乎大賓之是見業業焉凛乎大祭之是
承盖於未動而已有此敬矣奚待動而後敬乎
punctuated:
楊士雲

同考試官訓導張批：題主存養之功說，而「不動不言」難於措辭。此作會理成章，其有得於心學者。

同考試官教諭秦批：此篇於敬信上用心事講，最為得旨。

考試官教諭高批：上達事最難於言，吾於子有取矣。

考試官教諭歐陽批：存養事，非體認真切者不能道，此作得之。

君子於未然之時而存本然之天，其為己之功密矣。蓋敬信，本然之天也。君子不待言動而此心存焉，則為己之功孰有加於是哉？《中庸》三十三章，自下學立心之始推而言之，及此謂夫君子為己之學，當何如其用功耶？是故人不能以無動也，然當萬念未萌、一物未接之時，則不動矣。斯時也，或可少忽，而君子之心則不敢忽，兢兢焉，儼乎大賓之是見；業業焉，凛乎大祭之是承。盖於未動而已有此敬矣，奚待動而後敬乎？
translation_en:
Yang Shiyun

Comment by Associate Examiner Zhang, Assistant Instructor: The topic chiefly concerns the work of preserving and nurturing the mind, but “neither moving nor speaking” is difficult to express. This composition grasps the principle and gives it coherent expression; its author has attained some understanding of the learning of the mind.

Comment by Associate Examiner Qin, Instructor: This essay devotes careful attention to reverence and trustworthiness in its exposition [?], and captures the purport exceptionally well.

Comment by Examiner Gao, Instructor: Matters of higher understanding are the hardest to express. I find much to approve in your work.

Comment by Examiner Ouyang, Instructor: The work of preserving and nurturing the mind cannot be articulated by someone without a genuine and penetrating personal understanding. This composition captures it.

The gentleman preserves his original, Heaven-endowed nature before anything has occurred: how meticulous is his work of cultivating himself! Reverence and trustworthiness are indeed his original, Heaven-endowed nature. If the gentleman preserves this mind without waiting to speak or act, what work of self-cultivation could surpass this? Chapter thirty-three of the Doctrine of the Mean develops its discussion from the initial stages of elementary learning and establishing the mind’s purpose. On reaching this point, it asks: how should the gentleman apply himself to learning for his own cultivation? Thus, people cannot remain without action. Yet when the myriad thoughts have not yet stirred and not a single thing has been encountered, there is no movement. At such a time, one might permit oneself a little inattention, but the gentleman’s mind dares not be inattentive. Vigilant and cautious, he is solemn as though receiving an honored guest; watchful and apprehensive, he is awed as though conducting a great sacrifice. Before he has moved, this reverence is already present. Why should he wait until he moves before being reverent?

title: 弘治十四年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
人不能以無言也然當萬境俱寂一事未應之
際則不言矣斯際也或可少怠而君子之心則
不敢怠確然真實無纖芥偽妄也渾然純一無
毫髮虚假也盖於未言而已有此信矣豈待言
而後信乎噫敬於不動則動無往而不敬信於
不言則言無往而不信君子為己之功可謂益
加密矣中庸示人為學之要何其切哉考之中
庸前章言聖人之德極其盛矣此復自下學之
事推言其入德之要在省察存養而已盖動而
===
敬以省察靜而敬以存養則動靜交謹内外一
致而君子為己之功無復加矣故下文馴致篤
恭而天下平之盛以及無聲無臭之妙曷嘗不
自此動靜功夫中來耶學者不可不知
其為氣也至大至剛以直養而無害則塞
于天地之間其為氣也配義與道無是
餒也是集義所生者非義襲而取之也
行有不慊於心則餒矣我故曰告子未
嘗知義以其外之也必有事焉而勿正
punctuated:
人不能以無言也，然當萬境俱寂、一事未應之際，則不言矣。斯際也，或可少怠，而君子之心則不敢怠。確然真實，無纖芥偽妄也；渾然純一，無毫髮虚假也。盖於未言而已有此信矣，豈待言而後信乎？噫！敬於不動，則動無往而不敬；信於不言，則言無往而不信。君子為己之功，可謂益加密矣。《中庸》示人為學之要，何其切哉！考之《中庸》，前章言聖人之德，極其盛矣。此復自下學之事，推言其入德之要，在省察存養而已。盖動而敬以省察，靜而敬以存養，則動靜交謹，内外一致，而君子為己之功無復加矣。故下文馴致篤恭而天下平之盛，以及無聲無臭之妙，曷嘗不自此動靜功夫中來耶？學者不可不知。

其為氣也，至大至剛，以直養而無害，則塞于天地之間。其為氣也，配義與道；無是，餒也。是集義所生者，非義襲而取之也。行有不慊於心，則餒矣。我故曰告子未嘗知義，以其外之也。必有事焉，而勿正
translation_en:
People cannot be without speech. Yet when all surrounding things are silent and no matter has yet called for a response, they do not speak. At such a moment, one might allow oneself a little slackness, but the gentleman’s heart dares not slacken. It is firmly genuine, without the slightest falsehood or deception; wholly pure and undivided, without a hair’s breadth of pretence. Thus, even before speaking, he already possesses this trustworthiness. How could he wait until he speaks before becoming trustworthy? Ah! If he is reverent when not acting, then whenever he acts he will be reverent; if he is trustworthy when not speaking, then whenever he speaks he will be trustworthy. The gentleman’s work of cultivating himself for his own sake may indeed be called ever more painstaking. How closely the Doctrine of the Mean addresses the essentials of learning!

If we examine the Doctrine of the Mean, the preceding chapter describes the virtue of the sage in its utmost fullness. Here it returns to the elementary tasks of learning and explains that the essentials for entering into virtue lie simply in self-examination and in preserving and nourishing the mind. For through reverence in activity one examines oneself, and through reverence in stillness one preserves and nourishes the mind. Then both activity and stillness are attended with care, the inward and outward are at one, and nothing further can be added to the gentleman’s work of cultivating himself for his own sake. Thus the ensuing text gradually reaches the consummate state in which profound reverence brings peace to all under Heaven, and then the subtlety of what has neither sound nor scent. How could these ever arise from anything other than this work in activity and stillness? Students must understand this.

As qi, it is supremely great and supremely firm. If nourished with uprightness and left unharmed, it fills the space between Heaven and Earth. As qi, it accords with righteousness and the Way; without these, it starves. It is born of the accumulation of righteous deeds; it cannot be seized through an isolated act of righteousness. If one’s conduct leaves the heart dissatisfied, it starves. Thus I said that Gaozi never understood righteousness, because he regarded it as external. One must keep working at it, but must not anticipate the result…

title: 弘治十四年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
心勿忘勿助長也
于經
同考試官訓導潘批此題頭緒雖多而理則
貫串似易實難是作詞不費而理自足盖嘗知
養浩然者
考試官教諭高批曲盡養氣始終事可録
考試官教諭歐陽批約繁就簡孟義之
獨優老取之
大賢論氣由養而充必詳所以養而只其節度
焉盖養氣固在集義亦不可無節度也不然何
以塞天地而配道義也扒孟子因公孫丑之問
而告之以此盖謂浩然之為氣乃天地之正氣
至大初無其限量至剛不可以屈撓其體段本
如是也誠能自反而縮則得其養而又無作為
以害之則其本體不虧充塞天地而無間矣然
能養成此氣則有以合乎人心之裁制有以配
乎天理之自然使其行之勇决無所疑憚也若
無此氣則其一時所為雖未必不出於道義而
punctuated:
心勿忘，勿助長也。
于經。
同考試官訓導潘批：此題頭緒雖多，而理則貫串，似易實難。是作詞不費而理自足，盖嘗知養浩然者。
考試官教諭高批：曲盡養氣始終事，可録。
考試官教諭歐陽批：約繁就簡，孟義之獨優老取之。
大賢論氣，由養而充，必詳所以養而只其節度焉。盖養氣固在集義，亦不可無節度也。不然，何以塞天地而配道義也？扒孟子因公孫丑之問而告之以此，盖謂浩然之為氣，乃天地之正氣。至大，初無其限量；至剛，不可以屈撓。其體段本如是也。誠能自反而縮，則得其養，而又無作為以害之，則其本體不虧，充塞天地而無間矣。然能養成此氣，則有以合乎人心之裁制，有以配乎天理之自然，使其行之勇决，無所疑憚也。若無此氣，則其一時所為，雖未必不出於道義，而
translation_en:
…do not forget it in your heart, and do not help it grow.

Yu Jing 于經.

Associate Examiner Pan, Assistant Instructor, comments: Although this topic has many strands, its underlying principle runs through them all. It seems easy but is actually difficult. This composition expounds the principle fully without expending excessive words. Its author appears to understand the cultivation of the vast, flowing qi.

Examiner Gao, Instructor, comments: It thoroughly explores the cultivation of qi from beginning to end. It merits inclusion.

Examiner Ouyang, Instructor, comments: It reduces complexity to simplicity. Its treatment of Mencius’s meaning is especially outstanding [?]; I select it. [The latter part of the comment is garbled.]

When the great worthy discusses qi, which becomes full through cultivation, he must explain in detail how to cultivate it and its proper limits [?]. For cultivating qi certainly lies in accumulating righteousness, but it also requires proper limits. Otherwise, how could it fill Heaven and Earth and accord with the Way and righteousness? [An unclear character, 扒, precedes the following sentence.] Mencius gave this explanation in response to Gongsun Chou’s question. His meaning was that the vast, flowing qi is the upright qi of Heaven and Earth. It is supremely great, originally without limit or measure; it is supremely firm and cannot be bent or weakened. Such is its fundamental constitution. If, upon examining oneself, one truly finds oneself upright, then this qi receives nourishment. If, moreover, one refrains from contrived actions that injure it, its original substance remains unimpaired, filling Heaven and Earth without a gap. Once one has cultivated this qi to maturity, one can accord with the discerning judgments of the human heart and match the spontaneity of Heaven’s principle, acting courageously and decisively, without doubt or fear. Without this qi, although what one does on a particular occasion may indeed proceed from the Way and righteousness, yet…

title: 弘治十四年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
其體有不充則亦不免於疑懼而不足以有為
矣氣之由養而充者如此而其養之之始乃由
事皆合義而自反常直是以無所愧怍而此氣
自然發生於中豈由只行一事偶合於義可以
掩襲於外而得之乎若所行一有不合於義則
不足於心而體豈能充之乎故我謂告子未嘗
知義者以為外而不復以集義為事也然則集
義者必當致力於所有事也豈可預期其效耶
其或未充則但當勿忘其所有事也豈可作為
===
以助其長耶氣由集義而生者又如此是則集
義勿忘即直養矣勿正勿助即無害矣此其所
以塞天地而配道義者有由然哉嗟夫孟子之
不動心其原盖出於此乃若告子者以仁內義
外而不復以義為事則不能集義以生浩然之
氣而欲彊制其心則又不免於正助之病付身
心於冥然悍然之地所謂不動心亦異於孟子
矣孟子以是為公孫丑告則告子所言之非豈
俟攻而後破哉
punctuated: 其體有不充，則亦不免於疑懼而不足以有為矣。氣之由養而充者如此，而其養之之始，乃由事皆合義而自反常直，是以無所愧怍，而此氣自然發生於中。豈由只行一事，偶合於義，可以掩襲於外而得之乎？若所行一有不合於義，則不足於心，而體豈能充之乎？故我謂告子未嘗知義者，以為外而不復以集義為事也。然則集義者必當致力於所有事也，豈可預期其效耶？其或未充，則但當勿忘其所有事也，豈可作為以助其長耶？氣由集義而生者又如此。是則集義勿忘，即直養矣；勿正勿助，即無害矣。此其所以塞天地而配道義者，有由然哉！嗟夫！孟子之不動心，其原盖出於此。乃若告子者，以仁內義外，而不復以義為事，則不能集義以生浩然之氣，而欲彊制其心，則又不免於正助之病。付身心於冥然悍然之地，所謂不動心亦異於孟子矣。孟子以是為公孫丑告，則告子所言之非，豈俟攻而後破哉？
translation_en: …if this vital force is not full in its substance, one still cannot escape doubt and fear and is incapable of effective action. Such is the way vital force becomes full through cultivation. The beginning of its cultivation lies in ensuring that every deed accords with righteousness and that, upon self-examination, one is always upright. Thus one has nothing to be ashamed of, and this vital force arises naturally within. How could it be obtained through an external assault, merely by performing a single deed that happens to accord with righteousness? If anything one does fails to accord with righteousness, one feels dissatisfied at heart; how, then, could this vital force attain fullness in its substance? Thus, when I say that Gaozi has never understood righteousness, it is because he regards it as external and no longer makes accumulating righteous deeds his task. Those who accumulate righteous deeds must therefore devote their efforts to the work incumbent upon them. How could they anticipate its results? If their vital force is not yet full, they should simply not forget the work incumbent upon them. How could they contrive to assist its growth? Such, in turn, is the way vital force arises from accumulating righteous deeds. Accumulating righteous deeds and not forgetting this task are precisely what it means to nourish it through uprightness; neither anticipating results nor assisting its growth is precisely what it means to do it no harm. There is indeed a reason why it can thereby fill Heaven and Earth and accord with the Way and righteousness! Ah! Mengzi’s unperturbed heart had its source in this. As for Gaozi, he regarded benevolence as internal and righteousness as external, and no longer made righteousness his task. He therefore could not accumulate righteous deeds to generate the vast, flowing vital force. Yet, in seeking forcibly to control his heart, he could not escape the faults of anticipating results and assisting growth. He consigned body and heart to a state of benighted obstinacy; what he called an unperturbed heart was thus different from Mengzi’s. When Mengzi explained this to Gongsun Chou, did the errors in Gaozi’s words need to await an attack before they were demolished?

title: 弘治十四年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
易
比輔也下順從也原筮元永貞无咎以剛
中也
于經
同考試官訓導潘批此題兩言卦體作者
罕能分别多以九五於下順從一句講重而於
剛中一句又重複支離見理親切講說明白
無如此篇取之以冠本房
考試官教諭高批發明比道得三聖之意
===
考試官教諭歐陽批比道甚大此作形容
盡之矣
彖傳釋卦名以見下比上之義釋卦辭以見上
比下之德盖下之所比在上而上之所以為比
在德也彖傳釋名辭而各本諸卦體者如此其
闡比道之旨精矣昔伏羲畫比之卦文王繫比
之辭吾夫子傳彖從而釋之以為卦之所以為
比者盖本人心仰戴衆志協從有親輔於上之
義而非暌乖渙散之謂也然以卦體言之下體
punctuated:
易

比，輔也，下順從也。原筮元永貞，无咎，以剛中也。

于經

同考試官訓導潘批：此題兩言卦體，作者罕能分别，多以九五於「下順從」一句講重，而於「剛中」一句又重複支離。見理親切，講說明白，無如此篇，取之以冠本房。

考試官教諭高批：發明比道，得三聖之意。

考試官教諭歐陽批：比道甚大，此作形容盡之矣。

彖傳釋卦名，以見下比上之義；釋卦辭，以見上比下之德。盖下之所比在上，而上之所以為比在德也。彖傳釋名辭，而各本諸卦體者如此，其闡比道之旨精矣。昔伏羲畫比之卦，文王繫比之辭，吾夫子傳彖，從而釋之，以為卦之所以為比者，盖本人心仰戴、衆志協從，有親輔於上之義，而非暌乖渙散之謂也。然以卦體言之，下體
translation_en:
Book of Changes

“Bi (Holding Together) means aiding; those below yield and follow. In consulting the stalks anew, there is no blame if there is primordial goodness, constancy, and correctness, because the firm line occupies the central position.”

Yu Jing

Comment by Associate Examiner Pan, Assistant Instructor: This topic speaks twice of the hexagram’s structure, but writers seldom distinguish the two references. Most place excessive emphasis on the nine in the fifth position when explaining “those below yield and follow,” and then become repetitive and disjointed when discussing “the firm line occupies the central position.” No other essay equals this one in its close grasp of principle and clarity of exposition. I have selected it to rank first in this examining room.

Comment by Examiner Gao, Instructor: In elucidating the Way of holding together, it captures the intent of the three sages.

Comment by Examiner Ouyang, Instructor: The Way of holding together is exceedingly vast; this composition describes it exhaustively.

The Commentary on the Judgments explains the hexagram’s name to reveal the meaning of those below holding to those above; it explains the hexagram statement to reveal the virtue through which those above hold together with those below. For those below direct their allegiance toward those above, while what enables those above to bring about this union lies in their virtue. Thus, in explaining both the name and the statement, the Commentary on the Judgments grounds each explanation in the hexagram’s structure. How finely it elucidates the purport of the Way of holding together!

Long ago, Fuxi drew the hexagram Bi, and King Wen attached its statement. Our Master then composed the Commentary on the Judgments and explained it. He held that the hexagram is called Bi because it is founded upon people looking upward in loyal support and their wills joining in harmonious obedience. It signifies drawing close to and aiding those above, rather than estrangement, discord, and dispersal. Yet, speaking in terms of the hexagram’s structure, the lower trigram…

title: 弘治十四年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
之陰有初二三也莫不翕然順服惟五之是輔
上體之柔有四與上也罔不靡然歸向惟五之
是附四方攸同王后其維翰矣八表景從皇王
其維辟矣卦之得名非以此歟夫下之所以比
者固在乎上上之所以為比者尤在乎德故卦
辭所謂人之所以為比者必再筮以自審原筮
以自察果有元永貞之德而无虧斯可當眾之
歸而无咎者蓋以卦體言之九五居至尊之位
為顯比之主以陽居陽是之謂剛以九居五是
===
之謂中剛則不雜於陰柔一乾剛之正健也中
則不失於偏倚一皇極之建中也所以為元永
貞者在是矣所以為无咎者在是矣辭之所繫
非以是歟是知下有心以比乎上上有德以比
乎下上下交而比道成矣彖傳本卦體以釋名
辭者如此可謂曲盡其旨歟雖然人君不患天
下之未比而患吾德之未脩吾德既脩則天下
之比蓋有不期然而然者矣故温恭允塞者舜
也南河之避終不能沮謳歌朝覲之歸祇台德
punctuated: 之陰有初二三也，莫不翕然順服，惟五之是輔；上體之柔有四與上也，罔不靡然歸向，惟五之是附。四方攸同，王后其維翰矣；八表景從，皇王其維辟矣。卦之得名，非以此歟？夫下之所以比者，固在乎上；上之所以為比者，尤在乎德。故卦辭所謂人之所以為比者，必再筮以自審，原筮以自察，果有元永貞之德而无虧，斯可當眾之歸而无咎者。蓋以卦體言之，九五居至尊之位，為顯比之主，以陽居陽，是之謂剛；以九居五，是之謂中。剛則不雜於陰柔，一乾剛之正健也；中則不失於偏倚，一皇極之建中也。所以為元永貞者在是矣，所以為无咎者在是矣。辭之所繫，非以是歟？是知下有心以比乎上，上有德以比乎下，上下交而比道成矣。《彖傳》本卦體以釋名辭者如此，可謂曲盡其旨歟？雖然，人君不患天下之未比，而患吾德之未脩。吾德既脩，則天下之比，蓋有不期然而然者矣。故温恭允塞者，舜也；南河之避，終不能沮謳歌朝覲之歸。祇台德
translation_en:
…the yin lines of the lower trigram are the first, second, and third. All submit together in obedience, supporting only the fifth. The yielding lines of the upper trigram are the fourth and the topmost. All turn toward it in allegiance, attaching themselves only to the fifth. The four quarters unite, with the king as their mainstay; the eight outer regions follow as a shadow follows its form, with the sovereign as their ruler. Is this not how the hexagram derives its name, Bi, “Holding Together”?

Those below hold together by looking to those above; but those above become the focus of their allegiance above all through virtue. Thus, when the hexagram statement speaks of how a person becomes the focus of allegiance, he must divine again with milfoil to examine himself, probing the divination to scrutinize himself. Only if he truly possesses unimpaired virtue that is fundamental, enduring, and steadfast can he receive the allegiance of the multitude without blame. For, in terms of the hexagram’s structure, the nine in the fifth place occupies the supremely honored position and is the ruler who makes holding together manifest. A yang line occupying a yang position is what is called firmness; a nine occupying the fifth position is what is called centrality. Firmness is unmixed with yin yieldingness: it is wholly the upright vigor of Qian’s strength. Centrality does not lapse into partiality or imbalance: it is wholly the establishment of the mean through the sovereign’s ultimate standard. Herein lies what makes it fundamental, enduring, and steadfast; herein lies what makes it free from blame. Is this not why these words were attached to the hexagram?

We thus know that those below have the will to hold together with those above, while those above possess the virtue to hold together with those below. Above and below enter into mutual relations, and the Way of holding together is fulfilled. Such is the Commentary on the Judgments’ use of the hexagram’s structure to explain its name and statement. May we not say that it fully elucidates their meaning in every detail?

Nevertheless, a ruler should be concerned not that All under Heaven has yet to unite around him, but that his own virtue has yet to be cultivated. Once his virtue is cultivated, the allegiance of All under Heaven will come of itself, without being sought. Thus it was Shun who was “gentle, reverent, and truly sincere.” His withdrawal to Nanhe could not ultimately prevent those who sang his praises and those who came to pay court from turning to him. “Reverently, my virtue…”

title: 弘治十四年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
先者禹也陽城之逃終不能卻萬國玉帛之獻
卒之中國踐天子位而成虞夏之盛者未有不
本於德也然則欲求君德備民心歸而有合於
是卦之義者吾於虞夏有徵焉
易知則有親
董資元
同考試官訓導潘批融會本義意思詞語
整潔豈嘗究心於易者歟
考試官教諭高批說出體記意可觀
===
考試官教諭歐陽批題難言而辭足以達
之非深於易者不能
善體乾道者不難於人之知自得乎人之比夫
體道在己亦當驗之於人也吾之心既為人所
易知矣則同是心者烏有不親之者乎昔大傳
論乾坤之理分見於天地此則言法乾道之易
者謂夫乾之功雖至溥而无際乾之德實至易
而無難人之所為果能如乾之易也吾知其本
心瑩然明白而无傾險中扃湛若洞達而無迂
punctuated:
先者，禹也。陽城之逃，終不能卻萬國玉帛之獻。卒之中國踐天子位而成虞夏之盛者，未有不本於德也。然則欲求君德備、民心歸而有合於是卦之義者，吾於虞夏有徵焉。
易知則有親。
董資元
同考試官訓導潘批：融會本義意思，詞語整潔，豈嘗究心於易者歟？
考試官教諭高批：說出體記意，可觀。
考試官教諭歐陽批：題難言，而辭足以達之，非深於易者不能。
善體乾道者，不難於人之知，自得乎人之比。夫體道在己，亦當驗之於人也。吾之心既為人所易知矣，則同是心者，烏有不親之者乎？昔《大傳》論乾坤之理，分見於天地，此則言法乾道之易者。謂夫乾之功雖至溥而无際，乾之德實至易而無難。人之所為果能如乾之易也，吾知其本心瑩然明白而无傾險，中扃湛若洞達而無迂
translation_en:
…gave precedence to reverence for his own virtue: this was Yu. His withdrawal to Yangcheng ultimately could not turn back the offerings of jade and silk from the myriad states. That they eventually occupied the position of Son of Heaven in the central realm and brought about the flourishing of Yu and Xia was invariably founded upon virtue. Thus, if we seek instances in which a ruler’s virtue was complete and the people’s hearts turned toward him, in accordance with the meaning of this hexagram, I find corroboration in Yu and Xia.
“When One Is Easy to Know, One Gains Affection”
Dong Ziyuan
Comment by Associate Examiner Pan, Assistant Instructor: He has thoroughly assimilated the ideas of the Original Meaning. His wording is orderly and polished. Might he be someone who has devoted himself to studying the Book of Changes?
Comment by Examiner Gao, Instructor: He brings out the meaning of “tiji” [?]; it merits attention.
Comment by Examiner Ouyang, Instructor: The topic is difficult to express, yet his language adequately conveys it. Only someone deeply versed in the Book of Changes could accomplish this.
One who skillfully embodies the Way of Qian is readily understood by others and naturally gains their allegiance. Embodying the Way lies with oneself, yet it should also be tested in one’s dealings with others. Once my heart is easy for others to understand, how could those who share this same heart fail to feel affection for me? Formerly, the Great Commentary discussed the principles of Qian and Kun as manifested respectively in Heaven and Earth. Here, however, it speaks of emulating the ease of the Way of Qian. Though Qian’s accomplishment is all-embracing and boundless, its virtue is supremely easy and free of difficulty. If a person’s actions can indeed resemble the ease of Qian, I know that his original heart will be luminous and clear, without deviousness or treachery, and his innermost mind serene and thoroughly lucid, without tortuosity…

title: 弘治十四年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
曰昭昭乎暴白於人接其外即可以知其内彰
彰乎昭示於衆因其語即可以得其心不假推
測之勞而日章之實人皆可得而見之也奚難
焉無事探索之力而存主之妙人皆可得而知
之也奚難焉夫易知如此則是一人之心有以
通衆人之心將見知其心者然其心勃然鶴鳴
子和之機動知其易者慕其易翕然斷金如蘭
之願興盍簪以聚不戒而自孚也舉於我乎是
比拔茅以征不約而自同也舉於我乎是附人
===
雖間於衆寡聲應氣求者則無間焉勢雖殊於
遠近響應影隨者則不殊焉是則易知則所以
驗其易者已至有親則所以資其易者益深必
如是而後可久也此其所以為賢人之德歟雖
然此特體乾道之易者耳人能體坤之道則亦
可為賢人之業矣然猶未也體之而至於聖則
可以與天地參矣夫聖人之所以聖者盡此易
簡也賢人之所以賢者體此易簡也衆人之所以
愚者又非昧此易簡乎噫均是人也而有聖
punctuated: 曰，昭昭乎暴白於人，接其外即可以知其内；彰彰乎昭示於衆，因其語即可以得其心。不假推測之勞，而日章之實，人皆可得而見之也，奚難焉？無事探索之力，而存主之妙，人皆可得而知之也，奚難焉？夫易知如此，則是一人之心有以通衆人之心。將見知其心者然其心，勃然鶴鳴子和之機動；知其易者慕其易，翕然斷金如蘭之願興。盍簪以聚，不戒而自孚也，舉於我乎是比；拔茅以征，不約而自同也，舉於我乎是附。人雖間於衆寡，聲應氣求者則無間焉；勢雖殊於遠近，響應影隨者則不殊焉。是則易知，則所以驗其易者已至；有親，則所以資其易者益深。必如是而後可久也，此其所以為賢人之德歟？雖然，此特體乾道之易者耳。人能體坤之道，則亦可為賢人之業矣。然猶未也，體之而至於聖，則可以與天地參矣。夫聖人之所以聖者，盡此易簡也；賢人之所以賢者，體此易簡也；衆人之所以愚者，又非昧此易簡乎？噫！均是人也，而有聖
translation_en:
…[?] Plainly manifest to others, his inward character can be known simply by encountering his outward bearing; clearly revealed to all, his heart can be understood simply from his words. Without the labor of conjecture, everyone can see the reality of his virtue becoming more manifest each day: what difficulty is there? Without the effort of searching, everyone can understand the subtle workings of what he preserves within and takes as his governing principle: what difficulty is there? When he is thus easy to know, the heart of one person can communicate with the hearts of all. We shall see those who know his heart approve of it, spontaneously stirred to respond like the young crane answering its parent's call; those who know his ease admire it, united in their desire for a fellowship that can cut through metal and whose words are fragrant as orchids. Gathering together like hair held by a clasp, they trust him of themselves without being admonished, and all draw close to him. Advancing together like clumps of thatch pulled up by their intertwined roots, they unite of themselves without prior agreement, and all attach themselves to him. Though people differ in being many or few, there is no division among those whose voices answer one another and whose vital energies seek one another out. Though their circumstances differ in distance and proximity, there is no difference among those who respond like echoes and follow like shadows. Thus, in being easy to know, the evidence of his ease is complete; in having others draw close to him, the support for his ease grows ever deeper. Only then can he endure. Is this not what constitutes the virtue of a worthy person?

Yet this is merely to embody the ease of the Way of Qian. If one can embody the Way of Kun, one can also achieve the accomplishments of a worthy person. Even this, however, is not the ultimate attainment: by embodying these principles and reaching sagehood, one can stand alongside Heaven and Earth as a third power. What makes sages sagely is their complete realization of this ease and simplicity; what makes worthy people worthy is their embodiment of this ease and simplicity. Is it not likewise ignorance of this ease and simplicity that makes ordinary people foolish? Alas! All are equally human, yet there are sages…

title: 弘治十四年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
賢愚之異非此理之異所造之不同也有志於
易簡者烏可以不勉
書
敷奏以言明試以功
王仲仁
同考試官教諭王批題本平易場中作者
於敷言試功處殊欠體貼此篇寫出有虞御
群后之氣象宛然在目宜寘高選
考試官教諭高批辭不牽強而意自
===
足可以為文矣
考試官教諭歐陽批壁經中求似此亦少
行述職之典嚴考績之法聖世統御諸侯之道
也蓋述職行則政無所隱考績嚴則人不敢欺
有虞待諸侯之來朝可謂得其道矣史臣紀帝
舜之時當五載之內天子一巡乎方岳諸侯各
朝於京師然其來朝也豈無事而空行哉想其
有來雍雍至止肅肅凡施設於一國者必使於
是而敷奏區畫於四境者必使於是而對揚如
punctuated:
賢愚之異，非此理之異，所造之不同也。有志於易簡者，烏可以不勉？

書
敷奏以言，明試以功。
王仲仁

同考試官教諭王批：題本平易，場中作者於敷言試功處殊欠體貼。此篇寫出有虞御群后之氣象，宛然在目，宜寘高選。

考試官教諭高批：辭不牽強，而意自足，可以為文矣。

考試官教諭歐陽批：壁經中求似此亦少。

行述職之典，嚴考績之法，聖世統御諸侯之道也。蓋述職行，則政無所隱；考績嚴，則人不敢欺。有虞待諸侯之來朝，可謂得其道矣。史臣紀帝舜之時，當五載之內，天子一巡乎方岳，諸侯各朝於京師。然其來朝也，豈無事而空行哉？想其有來雍雍，至止肅肅，凡施設於一國者，必使於是而敷奏；區畫於四境者，必使於是而對揚。如
translation_en:
…the distinctions between sages, worthies, and fools arise not from differences in this principle, but from differences in their attainment. How could those who aspire to ease and simplicity fail to exert themselves?

Book of Documents
“They presented their reports in words and were clearly tested through their achievements.”
Wang Zhongren

Comment by Associate Examiner Wang, Instructor: The topic is straightforward, yet candidates in the examination hall have shown a marked lack of close understanding of the presentation of reports and the testing of achievements. This essay depicts the manner in which the ruler of Yu governed the assembled lords, bringing it vividly before our eyes. It deserves a high placing.

Comment by Examiner Gao, Instructor: The language is unforced, and the meaning is complete in itself. This qualifies as accomplished writing.

Comment by Examiner Ouyang, Instructor: Even among essays on the “Classic from the wall” [?], few comparable examples can be found.

To conduct the prescribed reporting of duties and rigorously apply the rules for evaluating achievements: this is how the feudal lords were governed in an age of sage rule. When duties are reported, nothing in government remains concealed; when achievements are rigorously evaluated, no one dares deceive. The ruler of Yu may indeed be said to have found the proper way to receive the feudal lords when they came to court. The historians record that, in Emperor Shun’s time, within each five-year period the Son of Heaven made one tour of the sacred mountains of the regions, and the feudal lords each attended court in the capital. Yet could their visits to court have been empty journeys with no business to transact? Imagine them approaching in harmony and arriving with solemn reverence. Whatever measures they had implemented within their states, he required them to report fully on this occasion; whatever arrangements they had made throughout their territories, he required them to explain in acknowledgment of his commands. For example …

title: 弘治十四年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
正朔制度若何而一之同之五禮五器若何而
脩之如之明目張膽於黻扆之前歴歴乎可聽
也輸忱露悃於冕旒之下昭昭乎無隱也述職
之公盖如此其言不善固有以告飭之矣其言
之善也豈可以遽信哉必聴言而觀行狥名而
責實如鑑斯空試其所施設者有益於生民否
乎如水斯止驗其所區畫者有關於治體否乎
正朔制度果同歟一歟五禮五器果脩歟如歟
或勤或怠舉莫逃於洞察一至公而無私也若
===
===
殿若最悉不出於藻鑑一至明而無蔽也考績
之嚴又如此是則述職公考績嚴庸錫之典斯
無愧矣有虞法制之善所以不可及歟抑論之
天不能自治而付之天子天子不能獨治而分
之諸侯諸侯各守一國所以宣上徳而達下情
也使五載之間不行敷言試功之典則無以作
其勤而起其怠上下之情何由而通欲民盡被
其澤難矣後千餘年成周有六年五服一朝又
六年王乃時巡考制度於四岳諸侯各朝于方
punctuated:
正朔制度若何而一之同之，五禮五器若何而脩之如之，明目張膽於黻扆之前，歴歴乎可聽也；輸忱露悃於冕旒之下，昭昭乎無隱也。述職之公盖如此。其言不善，固有以告飭之矣；其言之善也，豈可以遽信哉？必聴言而觀行，狥名而責實。如鑑斯空，試其所施設者有益於生民否乎；如水斯止，驗其所區畫者有關於治體否乎。正朔制度果同歟、一歟？五禮五器果脩歟、如歟？或勤或怠，舉莫逃於洞察，一至公而無私也；若殿若最，悉不出於藻鑑，一至明而無蔽也。考績之嚴又如此。是則述職公，考績嚴，庸錫之典斯無愧矣。有虞法制之善，所以不可及歟！

抑論之，天不能自治而付之天子，天子不能獨治而分之諸侯。諸侯各守一國，所以宣上徳而達下情也。使五載之間不行敷言試功之典，則無以作其勤而起其怠，上下之情何由而通？欲民盡被其澤，難矣。後千餘年，成周有六年五服一朝，又六年王乃時巡，考制度於四岳，諸侯各朝于方
translation_en:
…how the calendar and institutions were unified and brought into conformity, and how the five rites and five ritual tokens were put in order and made to accord with prescribed forms: with eyes open and courage firm before the embroidered screen of the throne, they presented reports that could be heard in every detail. Offering their sincerity and laying bare their hearts beneath the sovereign’s tasseled crown, they made everything plain and concealed nothing. Such was the impartiality of the reporting of duties. If their statements revealed shortcomings, there were certainly means to admonish and instruct them; but if their statements were favorable, could they immediately be believed? Their words had to be heard and their conduct observed; their reputations had to be followed up and actual results demanded. Like a mirror empty of preconceptions, the ruler tested whether what they had implemented benefited the people; like still water, he examined whether their plans had a bearing on sound government. Had the calendar and institutions indeed been brought into conformity and unified? Had the five rites and five ritual tokens indeed been put in order and made to accord with prescribed forms? Whether diligent or negligent, none escaped his penetrating scrutiny: he was wholly impartial and without selfishness. Whether ranked lowest or highest in performance, all came within his discerning appraisal: he was wholly clear-sighted and free of obscurity. Such, moreover, was the rigor of performance evaluation. With duties reported impartially and performance evaluated rigorously, the practice of rewarding merit could thus be carried out without reproach. Was this not why the excellence of the laws and institutions of the Yu dynasty could not be surpassed?

To consider the matter further: Heaven cannot itself govern, and so entrusts government to the Son of Heaven; the Son of Heaven cannot govern alone, and so divides responsibility among the feudal lords. Each lord guards a state, thereby extending the virtue of those above and communicating the circumstances of those below. If, within each five-year period, the practice of presenting reports and testing achievements were not carried out, there would be no means to encourage their diligence and rouse them from negligence. How, then, could the circumstances of those above and below be communicated? It would be difficult to ensure that all the people received the benefits of government. More than a thousand years later, under the established Zhou dynasty, those of the five service zones attended court once in six years; after another six years, the king made his tours of inspection, examining institutions at the Four Sacred Peaks, while the feudal lords each attended court at the regional…

title: 弘治十四年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
岳大明黜陟雖疏數異時繁簡異制然後世稱
治化之盛必曰虞周良有以夫
出入起居罔有不欽發號施令罔有不臧
劉永
同考試官教諭王批題本文武德上說明
白易見作者往往以發號施令為政殊失
本旨此篇得之矣蓋嘗用心於經學者歟
考試官教諭高批理明詞暢
考試官教諭歐陽批得旨可取
===
動無不敬言無不善前王得近臣之助然也甚
矣近臣於君德有攸繫也則夫前王動之敬而
言之善者豈非得近臣以為助哉昔穆王命伯
冏為太僕正而告之至此意謂文武之時君聖
於上臣賢於下其侍御僕從之臣又極旦夕承
弼之力則德之脩也夫何如哉是以居上臨下
不能無動也文武之動也或出入焉惟以抑畏
而為心或起居焉惟以祇肅而為念周旋中規
何者非天理之自持折旋中矩何者非天命之
punctuated:
岳，大明黜陟。雖疏數異時，繁簡異制，然後世稱治化之盛，必曰虞周，良有以夫！

「出入起居，罔有不欽；發號施令，罔有不臧。」
劉永

同考試官教諭王批：題本文武德上說，明白易見。作者往往以發號施令為政，殊失本旨。此篇得之矣，蓋嘗用心於經學者歟！

考試官教諭高批：理明詞暢。

考試官教諭歐陽批：得旨可取。

動無不敬，言無不善，前王得近臣之助然也。甚矣，近臣於君德有攸繫也！則夫前王動之敬而言之善者，豈非得近臣以為助哉？昔穆王命伯冏為太僕正，而告之至此，意謂文武之時，君聖於上，臣賢於下，其侍御僕從之臣又極旦夕承弼之力，則德之脩也夫何如哉？是以居上臨下，不能無動也。文武之動也，或出入焉，惟以抑畏而為心；或起居焉，惟以祇肅而為念。周旋中規，何者非天理之自持？折旋中矩，何者非天命之
translation_en:
…peak, and demotions and promotions were clearly determined. Although the intervals differed in length and the institutions differed in complexity, whenever later generations spoke of flourishing government and moral transformation, they invariably named the ages of Shun and Zhou. Surely there was good reason for this!

“In going out and coming in, rising and resting, they were never without reverence; in issuing proclamations and promulgating commands, they were never without goodness.”
By Liu Yong.

Comment by Associate Examiner Wang, Instructor: The topic concerns the virtue of Kings Wen and Wu; its meaning is clear and readily apparent. Writers often treat issuing proclamations and promulgating commands as a matter of administration, thoroughly missing the original purport. This essay has grasped it. Surely its author has devoted careful attention to the study of the Classics!

Comment by Examiner Gao, Instructor: The reasoning is clear and the language fluent.

Comment by Examiner Ouyang, Instructor: It grasps the purport and merits acceptance.

That the former kings were reverent in every action and good in every utterance resulted from the assistance of their close attendants. How profoundly the ruler’s virtue depends upon his close attendants! Was it not through their assistance that the former kings were reverent in action and good in speech? When King Mu appointed Bo Jiong Chief of the Charioteers, he addressed him in these terms. His meaning was that, in the time of Kings Wen and Wu, the rulers above were sages and the ministers below were worthy. Moreover, the ministers who attended them, drove their chariots, and accompanied them exerted themselves to the utmost, supporting and assisting them morning and evening. How fully cultivated, then, must their virtue have been!

Thus, occupying the highest position and presiding over those below, they could not remain without action. In their actions, Kings Wen and Wu, whether going out or coming in, kept only humility and awe in their hearts; whether rising or resting, they kept only reverence and solemnity in their thoughts. Their circling movements accorded with the compass: what movement did not express their own adherence to Heaven’s principle? Their turns accorded with the square: what movement did not express Heaven’s mandate …

title: 弘治十四年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
自度穆穆乎一和敬之旁作也雍雍乎一篤恭
之顯象也深宫如是大廷如是合幽顯而一揆
豈有一毫之不敬乎一日萬幾不能無言也文
武之言也一發號焉莫不盡善而盡美一施令
焉莫不至精而至備王言如絲何者不切於生
民王言如綸何者不關於治體洋洋乎嘉言之
孔彰也秩秩乎德音之濬發也微言如是大政
如是舉小大而一致豈有纖芥之不善乎是則
文武之聖尚有賴於近臣之助今予德不及於
===
文武得不賴伯冏以為助哉大抵僕臣之於人
主服御所由職掌大命所由出入不可不擇人
以任之也苟非其人則朝夕移養而不知漸入
於邪僻欲動之敬言之善亦難也已故穆王於
誥命之際惓惓乎此噫若文武者匪特為穆王
者所當法實萬世有天下者之所當法
詩
申伯番番既入于謝徒御嘽嘽周邦咸喜
戎有良翰不顯申伯王之元舅文武是
punctuated:
自度。穆穆乎，一和敬之旁作也；雍雍乎，一篤恭之顯象也。深宫如是，大廷如是，合幽顯而一揆，豈有一毫之不敬乎？一日萬幾，不能無言也。文武之言也，一發號焉，莫不盡善而盡美；一施令焉，莫不至精而至備。王言如絲，何者不切於生民？王言如綸，何者不關於治體？洋洋乎，嘉言之孔彰也；秩秩乎，德音之濬發也。微言如是，大政如是，舉小大而一致，豈有纖芥之不善乎？是則文武之聖，尚有賴於近臣之助。今予德不及於文武，得不賴伯冏以為助哉？大抵僕臣之於人主，服御所由職掌，大命所由出入，不可不擇人以任之也。苟非其人，則朝夕移養，而不知漸入於邪僻，欲動之敬、言之善，亦難也已。故穆王於誥命之際，惓惓乎此。噫！若文武者，匪特為穆王者所當法，實萬世有天下者之所當法。

詩

申伯番番，既入于謝，徒御嘽嘽，周邦咸喜。戎有良翰，不顯申伯，王之元舅，文武是
translation_en:
…measuring themselves against it. How solemn they were: harmonious reverence manifested on every side! How dignified they were: earnest respect made visibly apparent! Thus they behaved in the secluded palace, and thus in the great court. Their conduct in private and in public followed a single standard: could there have been the slightest irreverence?

With myriad affairs arising each day, they could not remain without speaking. Whenever Wen and Wu issued a proclamation, it was wholly good and wholly admirable; whenever they promulgated an order, it was utterly precise and complete. When the king’s words were like silk thread, which did not bear directly upon the people’s lives? When the king’s words were like a thick cord, which did not concern the essentials of government? How abundant: their excellent words shone forth brightly! How orderly: their virtuous utterances issued from deep within! Thus it was with their slightest words, and thus with their great policies. Small and great alike were consistent: could there have been the tiniest particle of anything not good?

Thus even the sageliness of Wen and Wu still depended upon the assistance of close ministers. Now that my virtue falls short of Wen and Wu’s, how could I fail to rely upon Bo Jiong for assistance?

Generally, servants attending a ruler have charge of his clothing and personal equipment, and through them his great commands pass in and out. One must therefore select suitable men for these appointments. If unsuitable men are chosen, their influence morning and evening will alter his disposition, and without realizing it he will gradually descend into perversity. It will then be difficult indeed for him to act reverently and speak well. Hence King Mu dwelt so earnestly upon this when issuing his charge. Ah! Men such as Wen and Wu were models not only for King Mu; they are truly models for all who possess the realm throughout the ages.

Book of Odes

The Earl of Shen, vigorous and imposing,
Had entered Xie.
His footmen and charioteers were numerous;
All the realm of Zhou rejoiced.
You have a worthy pillar of support!
How illustrious is the Earl of Shen,
The king’s senior maternal uncle,
Taking Wen and Wu as…

title: 弘治十四年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
憲
楊士雲
同考試官訓導張批此題預道申伯就封
之事而戎有良翰文武是憲二句盖體宣王
分封本意作者率多忽此是篇詞暢理明
宜取之以冠多士
同考試官教諭泰批題乃一篇之關楗作者
多於良翰為憲處不知照應保南土式南邦
意此篇體認親切挑剔分明且理致精到
===
而文采不浮盖嘗究心於本領者與
考試官教諭高批大雅義詞約理精者
無踰是篇故錄之
考試官教諭歐陽批四篇經義俱可觀而
惟錄此篇者譬諸嘗鼎一臠旨可知矣
詩人之贈親臣美其就封而有以慰乎人表其
重望而足以法乎人盖慰乎人而法乎人非威
望素著者不能也詩人於親臣之就封得不預
道以美之哉宣王之舅申伯出封于謝而尹吉
punctuated:
憲。
楊士雲
同考試官訓導張批：此題預道申伯就封之事，而「戎有良翰」「文武是憲」二句，盖體宣王分封本意。作者率多忽此，是篇詞暢理明，宜取之以冠多士。
同考試官教諭泰批：題乃一篇之關楗，作者多於「良翰」「為憲」處，不知照應「保南土」「式南邦」意。此篇體認親切，挑剔分明，且理致精到，而文采不浮，盖嘗究心於本領者與！
考試官教諭高批：大雅義，詞約理精者，無踰是篇，故錄之。
考試官教諭歐陽批：四篇經義俱可觀，而惟錄此篇者，譬諸嘗鼎一臠，旨可知矣。
詩人之贈親臣，美其就封而有以慰乎人，表其重望而足以法乎人。盖慰乎人而法乎人，非威望素著者不能也。詩人於親臣之就封，得不預道以美之哉？宣王之舅申伯出封于謝，而尹吉
translation_en:
…takes as models.

Yang Shiyun 楊士雲

Comment by Associate Examiner Zhang, Assistant Instructor: This topic anticipates the Earl of Shen’s departure to take up his fief. The two phrases, “You have a fine supporting pillar” and “He takes Kings Wen and Wu as his models,” embody King Xuan’s original intention in granting the fief. Most writers overlook this. This essay’s language flows freely and its reasoning is clear; it deserves to be selected to head the candidates’ work.

Comment by Associate Examiner Tai, Instructor: The topic is the hinge of the entire poem. In treating “a fine supporting pillar” and “taking as models,” most writers fail to connect these phrases with the ideas of “protecting the southern lands” and “being a model for the southern states.” This essay grasps the meaning intimately and makes its distinctions clearly. Moreover, its reasoning is precise and penetrating, while its literary embellishment is not superficial. Surely its author has devoted serious attention to the fundamentals!

Comment by Examiner Gao, Instructor: Among essays interpreting the Greater Odes, none surpasses this one in concision of language and refinement of reasoning. We therefore include it.

Comment by Examiner Ouyang, Instructor: All four essays on the meaning of the classics are worthy of attention. That only this one is included is like tasting a single morsel from a cooking vessel: from it, the flavor of the whole can be known.

In presenting a poem to a minister related to the king, the poet praises his departure to take up his fief as something that reassures the people, and displays his great prestige as sufficient to make him a model for them. For reassuring the people and serving as their model are beyond anyone whose authority and reputation have not long been established. As this royal kinsman and minister departs to take up his fief, how could the poet fail to anticipate the event and praise him? King Xuan’s maternal uncle, the Earl of Shen, went out to take up his fief at Xie, and Yin Ji…

title: 弘治十四年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
甫作詩以送之及此謂夫申伯以王朝之世臣
膺南土之重寄威武足以讋服乎人心勇畧足
以作新乎士氣觀其就封之時徒焉步行以從
者擁導前後何如此其眾也入謝之際御焉挽
車以行者環衛左右何如彼其盛也周邦之人
得於觀感之間交致喜慶之辭以為是申伯之
武必能鎮定南服所謂之屏之翰者有所賴矣
汝今不有良翰乎斯申伯之勇必能保障南土
所謂于蕃于宣者有所托矣汝今不有良榦乎
===
然是甚顯之申伯以言其親則姻連玉牒而為
王室之懿親其寵之隆也何如榮冠戚里而為
宣王之元舅其望之重也何若是以操觚染翰
南土未必無文士也莫不以其文是法焉披堅
執銳南國未必無武士也靡不以其武是憲焉
是則南土是保式是南邦固宣王分封之本意
戎有良翰文武是憲又申伯就封之能事尹吉
甫預道以贈其行其意不既深乎嗟夫愛人以
德所以贈人以言也吉甫一代文章之伯於申
punctuated: 甫作詩以送之，及此謂夫申伯以王朝之世臣，膺南土之重寄，威武足以讋服乎人心，勇畧足以作新乎士氣。觀其就封之時，徒焉步行以從者，擁導前後，何如此其眾也！入謝之際，御焉挽車以行者，環衛左右，何如彼其盛也！周邦之人，得於觀感之間，交致喜慶之辭，以為是申伯之武，必能鎮定南服，所謂「之屏之翰」者有所賴矣。汝今不有良翰乎？斯申伯之勇，必能保障南土，所謂「于蕃于宣」者有所托矣。汝今不有良榦乎？然是甚顯之申伯，以言其親，則姻連玉牒而為王室之懿親，其寵之隆也何如！榮冠戚里而為宣王之元舅，其望之重也何若！是以操觚染翰，南土未必無文士也，莫不以其文是法焉；披堅執銳，南國未必無武士也，靡不以其武是憲焉。是則「南土是保，式是南邦」，固宣王分封之本意；「戎有良翰，文武是憲」，又申伯就封之能事。尹吉甫預道以贈其行，其意不既深乎？嗟夫！愛人以德，所以贈人以言也。吉甫一代文章之伯，於申
translation_en: …[Yin Ji]fu composed a poem to see him off. At this point, he says that Shen Bo, as a hereditary servant of the royal court, had been entrusted with weighty responsibilities in the southern lands. His martial authority was sufficient to awe people into submission, and his courage and strategic ability sufficient to renew the soldiers’ spirit. Observe him as he proceeded to his fief: how numerous were those who followed on foot, escorting and leading him before and behind! As he entered Xie, how magnificent was the company of those driving and drawing the carriages, surrounding and guarding him on either side! Moved by what they witnessed, the people of Zhou exchanged words of joy and congratulation. They believed that Shen Bo’s martial prowess would surely pacify the southern domains: there was now someone upon whom they could rely to serve as “a screen and a supporting pillar.” Do you not now have a worthy supporting pillar? Shen Bo’s courage would surely safeguard the southern lands: there was now someone to whom they could entrust the task of “serving as a bulwark and spreading royal authority.” Do you not now have a worthy mainstay? Moreover, this illustrious Shen Bo was, in terms of kinship, linked by marriage to the royal genealogy and a close relative of the royal house. How great the favor he enjoyed! His distinction surpassed that of the other royal relatives, and he was King Xuan’s senior maternal uncle. How weighty his prestige! Thus, among those who held writing tablets and dipped their brushes—the southern lands surely had their men of letters—none failed to take his civil virtues as their model. Among those who wore armor and bore sharp weapons—the southern realm surely had its warriors—none failed to take his martial virtues as their standard. Accordingly, “protecting the southern lands and being a model to the southern states” was indeed King Xuan’s original purpose in granting the fief; “you have a worthy supporting pillar, whose civil and martial virtues are the standard” also expressed what Shen Bo could accomplish upon taking up his fief. Yin Jifu spoke of these things in anticipation, offering his words as a parting gift. Was his intention not profound? Ah! To love someone through virtue is precisely why one offers words as a gift. Jifu was the foremost literary master of his age; with regard to Shen…

title: 弘治十四年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
伯封謝則咏崧高於仲山甫城齊則咏烝民其
事實其情親與後世葩詞藻句者大不侔矣然
則二賢固有德行者矣吉甫其亦善於贈行者歟
儀式刑文王之典日靖四方
陳淳
同考試官訓導張批題本平易作者多襲
陳言令人厭觀此篇說出後王格先之由詞
理嚴整筆力老健其工於葩經者與
同考試官教諭秦批題意具於傳註作者
===
多體認不真此篇順題講義坦然明白
且氣充詞贍無片言陳腐使人望之而知
其為竒士矣
考試官教諭高批體貼周王所以格先
享祭之意無餘蘊矣
考試官教諭歐陽批詩正而葩此作得之
法前王之舊章安今日之天下此王者格先之
由也盖前人之所制後人之所法也今後王法
典以安天下其感格先王之神有由然哉此宗
punctuated:
伯封謝則咏《崧高》，於仲山甫城齊則咏《烝民》，其事實，其情親，與後世葩詞藻句者大不侔矣。然則二賢固有德行者矣，吉甫其亦善於贈行者歟？
「儀式刑文王之典，日靖四方。」
陳淳
同考試官訓導張批：題本平易，作者多襲陳言，令人厭觀。此篇說出後王格先之由，詞理嚴整，筆力老健，其工於葩經者與！
同考試官教諭秦批：題意具於傳註，作者多體認不真。此篇順題講義，坦然明白，且氣充詞贍，無片言陳腐，使人望之而知其為竒士矣。
考試官教諭高批：體貼周王所以格先享祭之意，無餘蘊矣。
考試官教諭歐陽批：詩正而葩，此作得之。
法前王之舊章，安今日之天下，此王者格先之由也。盖前人之所制，後人之所法也。今後王法典以安天下，其感格先王之神，有由然哉！此宗
translation_en:
…when [Shen]bo was enfeoffed at Xie, he sang “Lofty Mountains”; when Zhong Shanfu built the walls of Qi, he sang “The Multitude of the People.” The events were real and the feelings intimate: these poems differed greatly from the flowery diction and ornate phrases of later ages. Thus, the two worthies certainly possessed virtuous conduct; was Jifu not also skilled in offering words of farewell?
“Follow and emulate King Wen’s statutes, daily bringing peace to the four quarters.”
Chen Chun
Comment by Associate Examiner Zhang, Assistant Instructor: The topic is straightforward, but writers mostly repeat stale expressions, making their work tedious to read. This essay explains how a succeeding king moves the spirits of his predecessors. Its language and reasoning are rigorous and orderly, and its writing mature and vigorous. Surely its author is accomplished in the Classic of Poetry!
Comment by Associate Examiner Qin, Instructor: The meaning of the topic is fully set out in the commentaries and annotations, but writers mostly fail to grasp it truly. This essay follows the topic in expounding its meaning, plainly and clearly. Moreover, its spirit is full and its language ample, without a single stale phrase. One need only look at it to recognize an exceptional talent.
Comment by Examiner Gao, Instructor: It fully apprehends the meaning of how the Zhou king moves his predecessors’ spirits to partake of the sacrifices, leaving nothing unexplored.
Comment by Examiner Ouyang, Instructor: Poetry is correct and yet florid; this composition captures that quality.
To follow the established statutes of former kings and bring peace to the realm today: this is how a king moves the spirits of his predecessors. What earlier men instituted is what later men take as their model. Now, when a succeeding king follows these statutes to bring peace to the realm, surely there is a reason why he can move and reach the spirits of the former kings! This is the ancestral …

title: 弘治十四年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
祀文王於明堂以配上帝之樂歌也想其登歌
之頃致其冀享之誠謂夫我之奉祭上帝之享
既不敢必文王之享則有可必然所以必我文
王之享豈無自耶誠以文王安民之心寓諸典
籍也今雖沒矣典不與之俱沒我則儀而式之
于以恪遵成憲罔敢有或違文王安民之政布
諸典冊也今雖往矣典不與之俱往我則式而
刑之于以率由舊章罔敢有或懈如懷保小民
典之行於岐者悉舉而行之使行於昔者行於
===
今焉如惠鮮鰥寡政之布於豐者咸遵而布之
俾布於前者布於後焉夫我之法典者豈徒然
哉蓋以文王之典安天下之典今日之天下文
王之天下故自西自東四方何大也舉是典日
以安之使咸蒙至治之澤地雖異而澤之所及
無或異自南自北四方何廣也布斯典日以靖
之俾悉囿咸和之治人雖殊而治之所被無或
殊于以保郊鼎於無虞而鳧鷖既醉之太平千
載猶一日也于以衍姬錄於不墜而棫樸卷阿
punctuated: 祀文王於明堂以配上帝之樂歌也。想其登歌之頃，致其冀享之誠，謂夫我之奉祭，上帝之享既不敢必，文王之享則有可必。然所以必我文王之享，豈無自耶？誠以文王安民之心寓諸典籍也。今雖沒矣，典不與之俱沒，我則儀而式之，于以恪遵成憲，罔敢有或違。文王安民之政布諸典冊也。今雖往矣，典不與之俱往，我則式而刑之，于以率由舊章，罔敢有或懈。如懷保小民，典之行於岐者，悉舉而行之，使行於昔者行於今焉。如惠鮮鰥寡，政之布於豐者，咸遵而布之，俾布於前者布於後焉。夫我之法典者，豈徒然哉？蓋以文王之典，安天下之典；今日之天下，文王之天下。故自西自東，四方何大也！舉是典，日以安之，使咸蒙至治之澤，地雖異而澤之所及無或異。自南自北，四方何廣也！布斯典，日以靖之，俾悉囿咸和之治，人雖殊而治之所被無或殊。于以保郊鼎於無虞，而《鳧鷖》《既醉》之太平，千載猶一日也；于以衍姬錄於不墜，而《棫樸》《卷阿》
translation_en:
…a hymn for sacrificing to King Wen in the Hall of Light, associating him with the Lord on High. Imagine the moment when the hymn was sung in the hall, giving fullest expression to the sincere hope that the offerings would be accepted: “As I present this sacrifice, I dare not presume that the Lord on High will accept it; yet there is reason to be certain that King Wen will accept it. Can my certainty that our King Wen will accept it be without foundation? Truly, King Wen’s intention to bring peace to the people resides in the canonical records. Though he has now passed away, his established precepts have not perished with him. I take them as my pattern and model, thereby reverently observing the established statutes, never daring to depart from them in any respect. King Wen’s measures for bringing peace to the people are set forth in the canonical writings. Though he has now departed, his precepts have not departed with him. I take them as my model and standard, thereby following the old ordinances, never daring to grow lax in any respect. Thus, in cherishing and protecting the common people, I put fully into practice the precepts carried out in Qi, so that what was practiced in the past is practiced today. Likewise, in showing kindness to widowers and widows and relieving their distress, I follow and promulgate all the measures instituted in Feng, so that what was promulgated before is promulgated afterward.

“Is my modeling myself on these precepts without purpose? King Wen’s precepts are precepts for bringing peace to all under Heaven; the realm of today is King Wen’s realm. Thus, from the west and from the east—how vast are the four quarters! I put these precepts into practice, daily bringing peace to them, so that all receive the beneficence of consummate government. Though the lands differ, none differs in receiving that beneficence. From the south and from the north—how extensive are the four quarters! I promulgate these precepts, daily bringing tranquility to them, so that all dwell within a universally harmonious order. Though the people differ, none differs in being embraced by that government. Thereby I safeguard the suburban sacrifices and the dynastic tripods against peril, and the great peace celebrated in Wild Ducks and Gulls and Already Drunk endures for a thousand years as though for a single day. Thereby I perpetuate the dynastic mandate of the Ji house [?], keeping it from falling, and the Clustered Oaks and the Winding Hill…

title: 弘治十四年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
之大化百世猶一朝也噫法典安民則所以感
格之者其有素矣配享之祭文王之神豈不既
右享乎考之明堂之祭周公以義起之也然於
天維庶其饗之不敢加一詞焉於文王則言儀
式其典日靖四方天不待賛法文王所以法天
也卒章惟言畏天之威而不及文王者統於尊
也畏天所以畏文王也天與文王夫何間之有
哉
春秋
===
諸侯遂圍許 曹伯襄復歸于曹遂會諸
侯圍許〔俱僖公二十八年〕
周希謙
同考試官學正王 批 題本胡傳晉討許不
臣曹復國不義人皆知之究其聖人所以予奪
者則難發揮是篇獨能組織傳註鋪叙明
白且有斷制真得屬比之教者况三場俱優
取冠本房公論協矣
考試官教諭高 批 說曹許可責處讀之
punctuated:
之大化，百世猶一朝也。噫！法典安民，則所以感格之者，其有素矣。配享之祭，文王之神豈不既右享乎？考之明堂之祭，周公以義起之也。然於天，維庶其饗之，不敢加一詞焉；於文王，則言儀式其典，日靖四方。天不待賛，法文王所以法天也。卒章惟言畏天之威，而不及文王者，統於尊也。畏天所以畏文王也。天與文王，夫何間之有哉？

春秋

諸侯遂圍許。曹伯襄復歸于曹，遂會諸侯圍許。〔俱僖公二十八年〕

周希謙

同考試官學正王批：題本胡傳，晉討許不臣，曹復國不義，人皆知之。究其聖人所以予奪者，則難發揮。是篇獨能組織傳註，鋪叙明白，且有斷制，真得屬比之教者。况三場俱優，取冠本房，公論協矣。

考試官教諭高批：說曹許可責處，讀之
translation_en:
…the great transforming influence celebrated in “The Luxuriant Oaks” (Yupu) and “The Winding Hill” (Juan’a), such that a hundred generations are as a single morning. Ah! By following the statutes and bringing peace to the people, one has long laid the foundations for moving the spirits to respond. At the sacrifice in which King Wen accompanies Heaven, would his spirit not indeed graciously accept the offering? Examining the sacrifice in the Hall of Light, we find that the Duke of Zhou instituted it according to what was right. Yet concerning Heaven, he merely hoped that it would accept the offering, not daring to add a single word. Concerning King Wen, however, he spoke of taking his statutes as a model and daily bringing peace to the four quarters. Heaven requires no praise: taking King Wen as a model is the means of taking Heaven as a model. That the final stanza speaks only of revering Heaven’s awe-inspiring might, without mentioning King Wen, is because both are subsumed under the more exalted. Revering Heaven is the means of revering King Wen. What distinction, then, could there be between Heaven and King Wen?

Spring and Autumn Annals

“The regional lords thereupon besieged Xu.” “Xiang, Earl of Cao, returned to Cao and thereupon joined the regional lords in besieging Xu.” 〔Both entries are from the twenty-eighth year of Duke Xi.〕

Zhou Xiqian

That Jin punished Xu for failing in its duties as a subject, and that Cao’s restoration was unrighteous, are things everyone knows. But investigating and expounding the Sage’s grounds for praise and blame is difficult. It truly grasps the teaching conveyed through connecting and comparing entries. Moreover, his work in all three sessions was excellent. Selecting him as the highest-ranked candidate in this examining room accords with the general judgment.
