title: 弘治十四年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
凛然
考試官教諭歐陽批得聖人正名分嚴義
利之意
諸侯討罪春秋正君臣之典諸侯復國春秋嚴
義利之别觀諸書法特予諸侯圍許深責曹襄
復國意斯見矣聖筆之精一何至哉昔者晉文
主伯吾聞其一戰勝楚兩朝于王矣迺今因許
不會率會溫之師以討之禁其樵採絶其往來
文之圍許似亦過也經於此乃予晉文其意也
===
何按古者天子巡狩諸侯皆有方岳之朝周法
天子行幸三百里内有起居之問河陽踐土是
許之密邇者使許誠能膏車秣馬以會夫諸侯
端委弁冕以覲夫天子庶得人臣之職則亦無
可討者夫何諸侯再會也許則若罔聞知天子
再臨也許則畧不介意則於禮當討而在文問
罪之師不容緩矣雖曰環城而攻似為過舉然
不朝是討不臣是問以王法律之在貶爵削地
可也烏可執此以重文之咎耶故經於此書曰
punctuated:
凛然。
考試官教諭歐陽批：得聖人正名分、嚴義利之意。
諸侯討罪，《春秋》正君臣之典；諸侯復國，《春秋》嚴義利之别。觀諸書法，特予諸侯圍許，深責曹襄復國，意斯見矣。聖筆之精，一何至哉！昔者晉文主伯，吾聞其一戰勝楚，兩朝于王矣。迺今因許不會，率會溫之師以討之，禁其樵採，絶其往來。文之圍許，似亦過也。經於此乃予晉文，其意也何？按古者天子巡狩，諸侯皆有方岳之朝。周法，天子行幸，三百里内有起居之問。河陽、踐土，是許之密邇者。使許誠能膏車秣馬以會夫諸侯，端委弁冕以覲夫天子，庶得人臣之職，則亦無可討者。夫何諸侯再會也，許則若罔聞知；天子再臨也，許則畧不介意。則於禮當討，而在文問罪之師不容緩矣。雖曰環城而攻，似為過舉，然不朝是討，不臣是問。以王法律之，在貶爵削地可也，烏可執此以重文之咎耶？故經於此書曰：
translation_en:
… makes one shudder.
Examiner Ouyang, Instructor, comments: It grasps the Sage’s intent to rectify names and status and to distinguish strictly between righteousness and profit.
When the feudal lords punish wrongdoing, the Spring and Autumn Annals sets right the norms governing ruler and minister; when feudal lords are restored to their states, it draws a strict distinction between righteousness and profit. Examining its wording, we find that it expressly approves the feudal lords’ siege of Xu and sternly censures Xiang of Cao’s restoration to his state. Its intent is evident here. How consummate is the precision of the Sage’s brush!
Formerly, when Duke Wen of Jin presided as hegemon, I have heard that he defeated Chu in a single battle and twice paid court to the king. Now, because Xu failed to attend the assembly, he led the forces assembled at Wen to punish it, preventing its people from gathering firewood and cutting off passage to and fro. Duke Wen’s siege of Xu would seem excessive. Yet the Classic approves Duke Wen here. What is its intent?
Upon examination, in antiquity, when the Son of Heaven made a tour of inspection, the feudal lords all had an obligation to attend court at the sacred mountain of their region. Under Zhou regulations, when the Son of Heaven traveled, those within three hundred li were obliged to inquire after his well-being. Heyang and Jiantu were very near Xu. Had the ruler of Xu sincerely prepared his carriages and fed his horses to meet the feudal lords, and donned ceremonial robes and headgear to seek audience with the Son of Heaven, he might have fulfilled his duties as a subject, and there would have been nothing to punish. Why, then, when the feudal lords assembled twice, did Xu act as though it had heard and knew nothing? And when the Son of Heaven came twice, why did Xu pay no heed at all? According to ritual propriety, Xu therefore deserved punishment, and Duke Wen could not delay his punitive expedition.
Although surrounding and attacking the city might seem excessive, it was failure to attend court that he punished, and failure to act as a subject that he called to account. Judged by the king’s law, even demotion in rank and forfeiture of territory would have been permissible. How could one seize upon this to heap blame on Duke Wen? Thus, at this point the Classic writes: …

title: 弘治十四年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
遂傳曰其稱遂繼事之辭也其予夫晉文所以
責夫許者何如哉所謂正君臣之典者盖如此
若曹人從楚吾聞其見執於晉以畀於宋矣廼
今因晉見釋遂會諸侯以圍許位其固有國其
宜君曹之復國不亦可乎經於此於曹書名其
貶云何夫義者天理之公正其義必推之天下
國家而可行利者人欲之私放於利必至於奪
攘而後厭正義明道在諸侯所有事者使曹苟
能持詞執禮以請於王仗義執言以復其國庶
===
得歸國之道則亦無可議者奈何始之見執也
既不上告王室以求伸今之復國也又乃下貨
筮史而得釋則於利是行而於晉囚執之刑幸
而免矣借曰貨以藩身何愛之有然臨難苟免
以賂得國以大義律之誠匹夫賤者事也豈可
以此而薄曹之罪耶故經於此書其名曰襄傳
曰其歸之道非所以歸也其深責曹襄而所以
生名之者何若哉所謂嚴義利之別者又如此
雖然許曹不足言矣然晉文合四國能勝强大
punctuated:
「遂」。傳曰：「其稱遂，繼事之辭也。」其予夫晉文，所以責夫許者何如哉？所謂正君臣之典者，盖如此。
若曹人從楚，吾聞其見執於晉，以畀於宋矣。廼今因晉見釋，遂會諸侯以圍許。位其固有，國其宜君，曹之復國不亦可乎？經於此於曹書名，其貶云何？夫義者，天理之公，正其義，必推之天下國家而可行；利者，人欲之私，放於利，必至於奪攘而後厭。正義明道，在諸侯所有事者。使曹苟能持詞執禮以請於王，仗義執言以復其國，庶得歸國之道，則亦無可議者。奈何始之見執也，既不上告王室以求伸；今之復國也，又乃下貨筮史而得釋，則於利是行，而於晉囚執之刑幸而免矣。借曰：「貨以藩身，何愛之有？」然臨難苟免，以賂得國，以大義律之，誠匹夫賤者事也。豈可以此而薄曹之罪耶？故經於此書其名曰「襄」。傳曰：「其歸之道，非所以歸也。」其深責曹襄，而所以生名之者何若哉？所謂嚴義利之別者，又如此。
雖然，許、曹不足言矣。然晉文合四國，能勝强大
translation_en:
…“thereupon.” The Commentary says: “Its use of ‘thereupon’ is an expression marking the continuation of an undertaking.” How does its approval of Duke Wen of Jin serve to censure Xu? Such is what is meant by setting right the established relations between ruler and subject.
As for the ruler of Cao following Chu, I have heard that he was seized by Jin and handed over to Song. Now, having obtained his release through Jin, he thereupon joined the feudal lords in besieging Xu. The position was originally his, and the state was one he ought to rule: was Cao’s restoration to his state not permissible? Yet here the Classic records the ruler of Cao by his personal name. What is the meaning of this censure? Righteousness is the impartiality of Heaven’s principle: when one sets one’s conduct right according to righteousness, it must be practicable when extended throughout the realm, its states, and its ruling houses. Profit is the selfishness of human desires: if one acts for profit, one will not be satisfied until one has resorted to seizure and plunder. Upholding righteousness and making the Way manifest are duties incumbent upon the feudal lords. Had the ruler of Cao been able to present his case and uphold ritual propriety in petitioning the king, and to invoke righteousness and speak on just grounds to recover his state, he might have attained the proper way of returning to his state, and there would have been nothing to criticize. Why, then, when first taken captive, did he fail to appeal upward to the royal house to seek redress? And why, when recovering his state, did he instead stoop to bribing the divination scribe to obtain his release? He thus acted for profit and only luckily escaped the punishment of imprisonment at Jin’s hands. Suppose one says, “If wealth can shield one’s person, why begrudge it?” Yet to seek escape at any cost when faced with trouble, and to obtain a state through bribery, is, when judged by the great principles of righteousness, truly the conduct of a base common fellow. How could this serve to diminish Cao’s guilt? Thus the Classic here records his personal name, “Xiang.” The Commentary says: “The means by which he returned were not the proper means of returning.” How profound is its censure of Xiang of Cao, and what does its naming him while still alive imply? Such, again, is what is meant by strictly distinguishing righteousness from profit.
Even so, Xu and Cao scarcely merit discussion. Yet Duke Wen of Jin, uniting four states, was able to defeat the powerful…

title: 弘治十四年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
之楚合十一國之師不能服蕞爾之許何哉盖
踐土之盟血未乾又帥諸侯以會溫城濮之大
勞甫息又帥諸侯以圍許禮煩威黷諸侯亦罷
於奔命矣况討許以不朝為名假公義以濟私
忿乎故曰晉文公譎而不正
冬十月壬午公子遂會晉趙盾盟于衡雍
乙酉公子遂會雒戎盟于暴俱文公八年
楊敷頤
同考試官學正王批內夏外夷作者類能
===
言之於盟會上講雒邑戎不當居處畧弗
之及此作詞不煩而理獨到必造詣之深
者取之
考試官教諭高批得謹嚴意
考試官教諭歐陽批春秋謹華夷之辨意
正如此
即春秋深别華夷之盟見春秋深謹華夷之辨
夫明族類別内外春秋法也得不於公子遂之
盟趙盾雒戎以深致意哉何則中國之有戎狄
punctuated:
之楚，合十一國之師，不能服蕞爾之許，何哉？盖踐土之盟血未乾，又帥諸侯以會溫；城濮之大勞甫息，又帥諸侯以圍許。禮煩威黷，諸侯亦罷於奔命矣。况討許以不朝為名，假公義以濟私忿乎？故曰：「晉文公譎而不正。」
冬十月壬午，公子遂會晉趙盾，盟于衡雍。乙酉，公子遂會雒戎，盟于暴。俱文公八年。
楊敷頤
同考試官學正王批：內夏外夷，作者類能言之；於盟會上講雒邑戎不當居處，畧弗之及。此作詞不煩而理獨到，必造詣之深者，取之。
考試官教諭高批：得謹嚴意。
考試官教諭歐陽批：《春秋》謹華夷之辨，意正如此。
即《春秋》深别華夷之盟，見《春秋》深謹華夷之辨。
夫明族類，別内外，《春秋》法也。得不於公子遂之盟趙盾、雒戎，以深致意哉？何則？中國之有戎狄
translation_en:
…Chu, so powerful, yet when he assembled the armies of eleven states, he could not subdue tiny Xu. Why was this? The blood of the covenant at Jiantu had scarcely dried before he again led the regional lords to assemble at Wen; the great exertions at Chengpu had scarcely ended before he again led them to besiege Xu. Ceremonies became burdensome and military might was deployed to excess; the regional lords, too, were exhausted by rushing to obey his commands. Moreover, he attacked Xu on the pretext that it had failed to attend court, using public righteousness to satisfy private anger. Thus it is said: “Duke Wen of Jin was deceitful and not upright.”
“In winter, in the tenth month, on renwu, Prince Sui met Zhao Dun of Jin and made a covenant at Hengyong.” “On yiyou, Prince Sui met the Luo Rong and made a covenant at Bao.” Both entries are from the eighth year of Duke Wen.
Yang Fuyi.
Comment by Associate Examiner Wang, School Instructor: “Writers generally know how to discuss treating the Xia as insiders and the Yi as outsiders. Yet in discussing these covenant meetings, they scarcely address the point that the Rong of Luoyi ought not to have been dwelling there. This composition is economical in wording and distinctive in its grasp of principle. Its author must possess profound attainments. Accept it.”
Comment by Examiner Gao, Instructor: “It captures the sense of vigilance and strictness.”
Comment by Examiner Ouyang, Instructor: “Precisely such is the intent of the Spring and Autumn Annals in carefully maintaining the distinction between Hua and Yi.”
From the Spring and Autumn Annals’ sharp differentiation between covenants with Hua and with Yi, we see how carefully it maintains the distinction between Hua and Yi.
To clarify ethnic affiliations and distinguish insiders from outsiders is the rule of the Spring and Autumn Annals. Could it fail to attach profound significance to Prince Sui’s making covenants with Zhao Dun and the Luo Rong? Why is this? The presence of Rong and Di in the Central States…

title: 弘治十四年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
猶君子之有小人在周公有膺懲之舉在大易
有否泰之分戎狄者豈可雜處於中國而中國
者安可混同於戎狄耶廼今魯文中葉仲遂執
政內焉欲免晉討外焉欲結戎援十月壬午既
偕趙盾而講盟衡雍是月乙酉復偕雒戎而結
盟于暴衡雍盟也以大夫而專諸侯之禮猶以
中國而交中國于暴盟也以戎醜而干中國之
事是以中國而交夷狄度彼叅此固無足取矣
夫春秋記約而志詳者也於是二盟而深別之
===
何詞之贅而不憚煩乎蓋以雒邑天地之中王
畿之內四時陰陽之所和萬國衣冠之所萃斯
何地歟以戎醜而可居耶彼戎以西方之夷僻
在荒服之外氈毳其服侏㒀其語戎何人斯於
雒邑而可居耶以聲明文物之區雜被髮野祭
之俗華夷之族類泯然矣內外之藩籬蕩然矣
苟於此而不深別之謹嚴之法安在哉經於是
一則曰公子遂二則曰公子遂不使雒戎同於
趙盾一則曰壬午二則曰乙酉不使戎盟混於
punctuated: 猶君子之有小人。在周公有膺懲之舉，在大易有否泰之分。戎狄者豈可雜處於中國，而中國者安可混同於戎狄耶？廼今魯文中葉，仲遂執政，內焉欲免晉討，外焉欲結戎援。十月壬午，既偕趙盾而講盟衡雍；是月乙酉，復偕雒戎而結盟于暴。衡雍盟也，以大夫而專諸侯之禮，猶以中國而交中國；于暴盟也，以戎醜而干中國之事，是以中國而交夷狄。度彼叅此，固無足取矣。夫春秋記約而志詳者也，於是二盟而深別之，何詞之贅而不憚煩乎？蓋以雒邑，天地之中，王畿之內，四時陰陽之所和，萬國衣冠之所萃。斯何地歟，以戎醜而可居耶？彼戎，以西方之夷，僻在荒服之外，氈毳其服，侏㒀其語。戎何人斯，於雒邑而可居耶？以聲明文物之區，雜被髮野祭之俗，華夷之族類泯然矣，內外之藩籬蕩然矣。苟於此而不深別之，謹嚴之法安在哉？經於是一則曰公子遂，二則曰公子遂，不使雒戎同於趙盾；一則曰壬午，二則曰乙酉，不使戎盟混於
translation_en:
…is like the presence of petty men among gentlemen. The Duke of Zhou undertook punitive campaigns against them, and the great Book of Changes distinguishes between Obstruction and Peace. How could the Rong and Di be allowed to dwell intermingled with the Central States, and how could the Central States be confounded with the Rong and Di? Yet midway through the reign of Duke Wen of Lu, Zhong Sui held power. In domestic affairs he sought to avert punishment by Jin; in external affairs he sought to secure Rong support. On the renwu day of the tenth month, he joined Zhao Dun in concluding a covenant at Hengyong; on the yiyou day of that same month, he again concluded a covenant, this time with the Luo Rong at Bao. In the covenant at Hengyong, a grand master arrogated to himself the ceremonial prerogatives of the feudal lords, but it was still one Central State dealing with another. In the covenant at Bao, the Rong rabble intruded into the affairs of the Central States: this was a Central State entering into relations with the barbarians. Weighing the former against the latter, neither was worthy of approval. The Spring and Autumn Annals is concise in its records yet precise in what it conveys. Why, then, does it distinguish these two covenants so emphatically, apparently adding redundant words without shrinking from repetition?

Luoyi lies at the center of Heaven and Earth, within the royal domain. It is where the four seasons and yin and yang are harmonized, and where the capped and robed dignitaries of the myriad states assemble. What sort of place is this, that the Rong rabble should be allowed to inhabit it? Those Rong are barbarians of the west, dwelling remotely beyond even the outermost zone of submission. Their clothing is felt and animal hair; their speech is unintelligible [?]. Who are these Rong, that they should be allowed to dwell in Luoyi? To mingle the customs of loose hair and sacrifices in the wild with a region of illustrious institutions and cultural refinement would obliterate the distinction between Chinese and barbarian peoples and sweep away the barriers between the inner and outer realms. If no rigorous distinction were made here, where would the Annals’ exacting standards be? Thus the Classic says “Prince Sui” in the first entry and “Prince Sui” again in the second, refusing to place the Luo Rong on the same footing as Zhao Dun. In the first entry it says “renwu,” and in the second “yiyou,” refusing to let the covenant with the Rong be conflated with…

title: 弘治十四年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
晉盟而又正其名與地以深別之者使人知華
夏之中雒邑之內此為華彼為夷猶薰蕕之不
可以同器涇渭之不可以同流則族類以明內
外以別名分截然確乎其不可雜矣立法之精
且嚴何如哉不特此也中國而夷狄則狄之夷
狄猾夏則膺之謹魯隐于唐之盟志楚子陸渾
之伐皆此意也觀於夾谷之會所謂裔不謀夏
夷不亂華之言則知春秋之旨矣噫以為經世
之典撥亂反正之書百王不易之大法信夫
===
禮記
故祭帝於郊所以定天位也
陳傑
考試官教諭高批作此義者類襲陳
言可厭而於定天位處亦欠明白詞理兩
得是篇其空群矣
考試官教諭歐陽批說出先王達禮教之意
先王行尊天之禮所以立尊君之禮盖莫尊於
天而君儗之也因尊天而尊君之禮立焉則禮
punctuated:
晉盟，而又正其名與地以深別之者，使人知華夏之中、雒邑之內，此為華，彼為夷，猶薰蕕之不可以同器、涇渭之不可以同流，則族類以明，內外以別，名分截然，確乎其不可雜矣。立法之精且嚴何如哉！不特此也，中國而夷狄則狄之，夷狄猾夏則膺之。謹魯隐于唐之盟，志楚子陸渾之伐，皆此意也。觀於夾谷之會，所謂「裔不謀夏，夷不亂華」之言，則知《春秋》之旨矣。噫！以為經世之典、撥亂反正之書、百王不易之大法，信夫！

禮記
故祭帝於郊，所以定天位也。
陳傑

考試官教諭高批：作此義者類襲陳言，可厭，而於定天位處亦欠明白。詞理兩得，是篇其空群矣。

考試官教諭歐陽批：說出先王達禮教之意。

先王行尊天之禮，所以立尊君之禮，盖莫尊於天而君儗之也。因尊天而尊君之禮立焉，則禮
translation_en:
…the covenant with Jin. Furthermore, by correctly recording the names and places to distinguish them sharply, it makes people understand that within the central lands of Huaxia, within Luoyi itself, these are Hua and those are Yi. Just as fragrant and foul-smelling plants cannot share a vessel, and the Jing and Wei rivers cannot share a stream, so the distinctions between peoples are made clear, and those within are distinguished from those outside. Names and statuses are sharply delimited, firmly precluding any confusion. How precise and strict is its establishment of rules! Nor is this all: when the central states behave as barbarians, it treats them as barbarians; when barbarians disturb the Xia, it chastises them. Its scrupulous treatment of Duke Yin of Lu’s covenant at Tang and its recording of the Viscount of Chu’s attack on Luhun both express this intent. Consider the meeting at Jiagu and the words, “Those of the distant borderlands must not plot against the Xia; the Yi must not bring disorder to the Hua.” Then one understands the purport of the Spring and Autumn Annals. Ah! Truly it is a canon for ordering the world, a book for dispelling disorder and restoring what is right, and a great law that a hundred kings cannot alter!

Record of Rites
“Thus, sacrificing to the Supreme Sovereign in the suburbs serves to establish the position conferred by Heaven.”
Chen Jie

Comment by Examiner Gao, Instructor: Those who compose essays on this passage generally repeat stale expressions, which is tiresome; they also fail to clarify the point about establishing the position conferred by Heaven. This essay succeeds in both expression and reasoning and surely surpasses all the others.

Comment by Examiner Ouyang, Instructor: It brings out the former kings’ intention to extend the teaching of ritual.

The former kings performed rites honoring Heaven in order to establish rites honoring the ruler, for nothing is more exalted than Heaven, and the ruler is its counterpart. When rites honoring the ruler are established through honoring Heaven, then ritual …

title: 弘治十四年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
教何患其不達哉記禮運者謂夫帝乃天之所
主天乃帝之所寓萬物資之以始功莫尚也先
王則儀物具陳駕鑾輿而有事於吉土之郊嵗
功資之以成德莫加也先王則精誠懇到被龍
衮而大饗於泰壇之上攄報本之心於燔燎之
餘惴惴然恐帝之逺而難格也伸反始之念於
對越之頃勿勿乎冀天之聽而來饗也所以然
者盖以民之於君猶君之於天君而不知所以
尊天民而安知所以尊君哉今郊祭而尊天之
===
禮以行則天下之民莫不曰代天理物吾君之
功無間於帝知帝之至尊則知君之同尊也又
莫不曰繼天立極吾君之德配合於天知天之
當事則知君之當事也巍巍九重四海傾心而
仰之如帝位於是而定矣穆穆一人萬方拱極
而戴之如天分於是而正矣吁禮行而天道顯
位定而君分尊先王達禮教之意何其至哉抑
不特此耳祀社於國所以列地利也祖廟所以
本仁也償禮鬼神而祀山川本諸事為而祭五
punctuated: 教何患其不達哉？記《禮運》者謂夫帝乃天之所主，天乃帝之所寓。萬物資之以始，功莫尚也，先王則儀物具陳，駕鑾輿而有事於吉土之郊；嵗功資之以成，德莫加也，先王則精誠懇到，被龍衮而大饗於泰壇之上。攄報本之心於燔燎之餘，惴惴然恐帝之逺而難格也；伸反始之念於對越之頃，勿勿乎冀天之聽而來饗也。所以然者，盖以民之於君，猶君之於天。君而不知所以尊天，民而安知所以尊君哉？今郊祭而尊天之禮以行，則天下之民莫不曰：「代天理物，吾君之功無間於帝。」知帝之至尊，則知君之同尊也。又莫不曰：「繼天立極，吾君之德配合於天。」知天之當事，則知君之當事也。巍巍九重，四海傾心而仰之如帝，位於是而定矣；穆穆一人，萬方拱極而戴之如天，分於是而正矣。吁！禮行而天道顯，位定而君分尊，先王達禮教之意何其至哉！抑不特此耳，祀社於國，所以列地利也；祖廟，所以本仁也；償禮鬼神而祀山川，本諸事為而祭五
translation_en:
…how could there be any concern that such teaching would not reach everywhere? The author of the “Evolution of Ritual” (Liyun) says that the Lord on High is Heaven in its aspect as sovereign, while Heaven is that in which the Lord on High resides. All things depend upon him for their beginnings, and no achievement surpasses his. Thus the former kings arrayed all the ceremonial objects, mounted their bell-adorned carriages, and performed sacrifice in the suburbs on auspicious ground [?]. The labors of the year depend upon him for their completion, and no virtue exceeds his. Thus the former kings brought utmost sincerity and earnestness, donned dragon robes, and offered the great sacrifice upon the Grand Altar. Amid the sacrificial burning, they expressed their desire to repay the source of all things, anxiously fearing that the Lord on High was distant and difficult to summon. While reverently facing him, they expressed their wish to return to the beginning, urgently [?] hoping that Heaven would hear and come to enjoy the offerings.

The reason for this is that the people stand in relation to their ruler as the ruler stands in relation to Heaven. If the ruler does not know how to honor Heaven, how can the people know how to honor their ruler? Now, when the suburban sacrifice is offered and the rites honoring Heaven are performed, all the people under Heaven say: “Our ruler orders all things on Heaven’s behalf; his achievements are indistinguishable from those of the Lord on High.” Knowing that the Lord on High is supremely honored, they know that their ruler is likewise honored. They also all say: “Our ruler carries on Heaven’s work and establishes the supreme standard; his virtue accords with Heaven.” Knowing that Heaven ought to be served, they know that their ruler ought to be served.

Lofty within the ninefold palace, he receives the wholehearted reverence of all within the four seas, who look up to him as to the Lord on High: his position is thereby established. August as the One Man, he receives the allegiance of all regions, which converge upon him as upon the pole star and uphold him as Heaven: the distinctions of rank are thereby set right. Ah! When ritual is performed, Heaven’s Way becomes manifest; when his position is established, the ruler’s status is honored. How consummate was the former kings’ intention to extend ritual teaching everywhere!

Yet this is not all. Sacrificing to the soil altar in the capital serves to set forth the benefits of the earth; ancestral temples serve to root benevolence in its source. In requiting [?] the spirits with rites, they sacrificed to mountains and rivers; taking practical affairs as their basis, they sacrificed to the five…

title: 弘治十四年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
祀皆是使禮教之四達廟有宗祝朝有三公學
有三老五更皆明禮教以淑天下至於君之一
身乃居巫史瞽侑之中而守至正焉則又以禮
自防示教於天下也先王以禮示教而以身為
率如此所以幽感神明感人而臻類應之效也
夫豈不宜
紀綱既正天下大定
趙儀
考試官教諭高批本傳註先序之以
禮為說有發揮有照應經義如此可錄矣
考試官教諭歐陽批得子夏告文侯意
惟禮得其序斯世極其治盖禮乃世之大閑也
孰謂禮得其序而世有不治者哉子夏答魏文
侯推言古樂之所由作如此謂夫昔者聖王因
天下大當以興制作立父子君臣以為紀綱紀
則有六所謂諸父諸舅有善而有義族人昆弟
有叙而有親以至師長朋友有尊而有舊也紀
之所在禮莫大焉綱則有三所謂相臨而有君
punctuated:
祀，皆是使禮教之四達。廟有宗祝，朝有三公，學有三老五更，皆明禮教以淑天下。至於君之一身，乃居巫史瞽侑之中而守至正焉，則又以禮自防，示教於天下也。先王以禮示教，而以身為率如此，所以幽感神、明感人，而臻類應之效也。夫豈不宜？
紀綱既正，天下大定。
趙儀
考試官教諭高批：本傳註，先序之，以禮為說，有發揮，有照應。經義如此，可錄矣。
考試官教諭歐陽批：得子夏告文侯意。
惟禮得其序，斯世極其治。盖禮乃世之大閑也，孰謂禮得其序而世有不治者哉？子夏答魏文侯，推言古樂之所由作如此。謂夫昔者聖王因天下大當以興制作，立父子君臣以為紀綱。紀則有六，所謂諸父諸舅有善而有義，族人昆弟有叙而有親，以至師長朋友有尊而有舊也。紀之所在，禮莫大焉。綱則有三，所謂相臨而有君
translation_en:
…the Five Sacrifices: all these serve to spread ritual teaching in every direction. In the ancestral temple there are ancestral and invocational officials; at court, the Three Dukes; and in the schools, the Three Elders and Five Experienced Men, honored representatives of the aged. All elucidate ritual teaching to improve the world. As for the ruler himself, he dwells among spirit mediums, scribes, blind musicians, and their assistants, maintaining the utmost rectitude. Thus he also uses ritual to guard his own conduct and instruct the world by example. Such was the way the former kings taught through ritual and made themselves exemplars. Hence, in the unseen realm they moved the spirits, and in the visible realm they moved people, achieving the effect of like responding to like. Was this not fitting?
“Once the guiding bonds and cardinal relationships are rectified, all under Heaven is firmly settled.”
Zhao Yi.
Comment by Examiner Gao, Instructor: Grounding the discussion in the transmitted commentary and annotations, the author first sets out the subject and explains it through ritual. There is elaboration, and the parts correspond with one another. An exposition of the Classics such as this merits inclusion.
Comment by Examiner Ouyang, Instructor: This captures the meaning of Zixia’s words to Marquis Wen.
Only when ritual attains its proper order does the world attain the highest degree of good government. Ritual is indeed the great restraint upon the world. Who could say that, when ritual has attained its proper order, the world could remain ungoverned? Such was Zixia’s explanation, in answering Marquis Wen of Wei, of the origins of ancient music. His meaning was that the sage kings of old, taking advantage of a time when all under Heaven was in great accord [?], established institutions and set up the relationships of father and son, ruler and minister, as guiding bonds and cardinal relationships. There are six guiding bonds: toward paternal uncles and maternal uncles, goodness and righteousness; among fellow clansmen and brothers, proper precedence and affection; and toward teachers and elders, and toward friends, respect and enduring attachment. Wherever these guiding bonds obtain, nothing is greater than ritual. There are three cardinal relationships: in the relationship of governing there is the ruler…

title: 弘治十四年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
臣君則為臣之綱相生而有父子父則為子之
綱以至相聚而有夫婦夫則為妻之綱也綱之
所在禮莫踰焉紀焉既正其必行之族黨鄉里
無反無側井然而有條矣綱焉既正其必施之
朝廷閨門無偏無黨秩然而有序矣夫禮所以
定民志也今紀綱正矣則自東以西天下雖大
孰不在於範圍之中自南以北疆域雖廣孰有
出於維持之外遠近乂安無復有乖爭凌犯之
風而世臻於極治矣不謂之天下大定可乎內
===
外寧謐無復有搶攘摇杌之勢而時底於太平
矣不謂之天下大定得乎夫禮序於上而化成
於下如此古樂之所由以作也不在是歟大抵
樂不可苟作也必禮序而後可作禮不可徒制
也必治定而後可制此古之帝王始之以飾治
功而終之以賛化育其所由來者不易而所以
致用者匪輕也否則區區文具而已嗚呼後之
人主有比湯武而幾成康者猶謂治之隆替不
在禮樂而莫之究彼文侯何人斯而足以與此
punctuated: 臣，君則為臣之綱；相生而有父子，父則為子之綱；以至相聚而有夫婦，夫則為妻之綱也。綱之所在，禮莫踰焉。紀焉既正，其必行之族黨鄉里，無反無側，井然而有條矣；綱焉既正，其必施之朝廷閨門，無偏無黨，秩然而有序矣。夫禮所以定民志也。今紀綱正矣，則自東以西，天下雖大，孰不在於範圍之中？自南以北，疆域雖廣，孰有出於維持之外？遠近乂安，無復有乖爭凌犯之風，而世臻於極治矣，不謂之天下大定可乎？內外寧謐，無復有搶攘摇杌之勢，而時底於太平矣，不謂之天下大定得乎？夫禮序於上而化成於下如此，古樂之所由以作也，不在是歟？大抵樂不可苟作也，必禮序而後可作；禮不可徒制也，必治定而後可制。此古之帝王始之以飾治功，而終之以賛化育，其所由來者不易，而所以致用者匪輕也。否則區區文具而已。嗚呼！後之人主有比湯武而幾成康者，猶謂治之隆替不在禮樂，而莫之究。彼文侯何人斯，而足以與此
translation_en:
…and minister: the ruler serves as the guiding bond for the minister. Through generation there are father and son: the father serves as the guiding bond for the son. Through union there are husband and wife: the husband serves as the guiding bond for the wife. Where these guiding bonds apply, ritual permits no transgression. Once the six relationships are rectified, they must be practiced among clans, neighborhoods, and villages, with neither opposition nor deviation, each duly ordered. Once the three guiding bonds are rectified, they must be applied at court and within the household, without partiality or faction, each in its proper order. Ritual serves to settle the people’s intentions. Now that these relationships and guiding bonds are rectified, from east to west, vast though the world is, who does not fall within their bounds? From south to north, broad though the realm is, who stands beyond their sustaining reach? Near and far are well governed and secure; habits of discord, contention, oppression, and encroachment no longer exist, and the world attains the highest degree of order. Could one fail to call this the great settlement of all under Heaven? Within and without all is tranquil; turmoil and instability no longer prevail, and the age attains supreme peace. Could one fail to call this the great settlement of all under Heaven? When ritual is duly ordered above and moral transformation is accomplished below in this way, is this not precisely the basis upon which ancient music was created?

In general, music cannot be created heedlessly: only after ritual is duly ordered may it be created. Ritual cannot be instituted as mere form: only after order is established may it be instituted. Thus the emperors and kings of antiquity began by embellishing the achievements of their rule and ended by assisting the transforming and nurturing work of Heaven and Earth. What brought ritual and music into being was no easy matter, and the purposes they served were far from trivial. Otherwise, they would amount to nothing more than paltry formalities. Alas! Among later rulers there were those who rivaled Tang and Wu and approached Cheng and Kang, yet they still maintained that the flourishing or decline of good government did not depend upon ritual and music, and failed to investigate the matter fully. What sort of man, then, was that Marquis Wen, that he should be capable of participating in this…

title: 弘治十四年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
子夏之言祗見其托迹於簡冊之間也噫
第貳場
論
孟子以道自任
楊士雲
同考試官訓導張批論題本以道字為重
而於時字亦不可輕過作者類多忽畧此篇
有發揚有歸宿筆力高古自是一家議論
得士如此可以為秋闈慶矣
===
同考試官教諭秦批寫出孟子以道自任之
意有挽萬鈞筆力于其善於論者
考試官教諭高批以時與力二字推孟子
心事曲盡無餘而議論滾滾無一句一字
不切當者可以為論矣
考試官教諭歐陽批是作議論淵源筆
力蒼健反覆曲折發盡程子道孟子
之意末復發出程子自任之意其亦
學焉而有得者歟
punctuated:
子夏之言，祗見其托迹於簡冊之間也。噫！

第貳場
論
孟子以道自任
楊士雲

同考試官訓導張批：論題本以道字為重，而於時字亦不可輕過。作者類多忽畧，此篇有發揚，有歸宿，筆力高古，自是一家議論。得士如此，可以為秋闈慶矣。

同考試官教諭秦批：寫出孟子以道自任之意，有挽萬鈞筆力，于其善於論者。

考試官教諭高批：以時與力二字推孟子心事，曲盡無餘，而議論滾滾，無一句一字不切當者，可以為論矣。

考試官教諭歐陽批：是作議論淵源，筆力蒼健，反覆曲折，發盡程子道孟子之意。末復發出程子自任之意，其亦學焉而有得者歟？
translation_en:
…As for Zixia’s words, we see only that they have found a resting place among written records. Alas!

Second Session
Discourse
“Mencius Took Responsibility for the Way upon Himself”
By Yang Shiyun

Comment by Associate Examiner Zhang, Assistant Instructor: The discourse topic places primary weight on the word “Way,” but the word “timeliness” must not be passed over lightly either. Writers generally overlook this. This essay develops its argument fully and brings it to a definite conclusion. Its writing is lofty and antique in style, and its argument has a distinctive voice. Finding a scholar like this is cause for rejoicing at the autumn Provincial Examination.

Comment by Associate Examiner Qin, Instructor: It brings out the meaning of Mencius’s taking responsibility for the Way upon himself. Its writing has the strength to pull a weight of ten thousand jun; he is among those skilled in discourse [?].

Comment by Examiner Gao, Instructor: Through the two terms “timeliness” and “capacity,” it explores Mencius’s innermost concerns, exhausting every nuance and leaving nothing unexplained. Its argument flows abundantly, yet not a single sentence or word is inappropriate. This deserves to be called a discourse.

Comment by Examiner Ouyang, Instructor: This work’s argument has deep foundations, and its writing is vigorous and mature. Through repeated turns and subtle developments, it fully brings out Master Cheng’s meaning in speaking of Mencius. At the end, it further brings out Master Cheng’s own sense of responsibility. Surely its author, too, has gained understanding through study?

title: 弘治十四年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
理有出於衆人之所同而聖賢獨任之此
必有不得已者矣道之在天下非一人之
所得私也衆人與聖賢之所同也衆人與
聖賢同有之則固宜衆人之分任之也然
不可以徒任也力能任則任之時可任則
任之力不足而任者愚非其時而任者妄
有其力遭其時而諉於不任者畫三者聖
賢不由也然則以衆人之所同而聖賢獨
任之其心豈得已哉程子曰孟子以道自
===
任予於是有以知孟子之不得已者矣請
終言之斯道也何道也原於天而具於人
天下古今所共由之道也韓子所謂堯傳
之舜舜傳之禹禹傳之湯湯傳之文武周
公文武周公傳之孔子皆是物也孔子之
道顏子盖得之矣簞瓢陋巷自樂其樂恝
然若無與於斯道者何也當是時任之者
有孔子故也若時無孔子則顏子亦必將
駕其說於天下舍陋巷之安而授室於列
punctuated:
理有出於衆人之所同而聖賢獨任之，此必有不得已者矣。道之在天下，非一人之所得私也，衆人與聖賢之所同也。衆人與聖賢同有之，則固宜衆人之分任之也。然不可以徒任也：力能任則任之，時可任則任之。力不足而任者愚，非其時而任者妄，有其力、遭其時而諉於不任者畫。三者，聖賢不由也。然則以衆人之所同而聖賢獨任之，其心豈得已哉？程子曰：「孟子以道自任。」予於是有以知孟子之不得已者矣。請終言之。

斯道也，何道也？原於天而具於人，天下古今所共由之道也。韓子所謂「堯傳之舜，舜傳之禹，禹傳之湯，湯傳之文武周公，文武周公傳之孔子」，皆是物也。孔子之道，顏子盖得之矣。簞瓢陋巷，自樂其樂，恝然若無與於斯道者，何也？當是時，任之者有孔子故也。若時無孔子，則顏子亦必將駕其說於天下，舍陋巷之安而授室於列
translation_en:
There are principles shared by all people for which sages and worthies alone assume responsibility. There must be something that compels them to do so. The Way in the world is not something any one person may possess exclusively; it is shared by ordinary people and sages and worthies alike. Since they all possess it, ordinary people should certainly bear a share of responsibility for it. Yet one cannot assume this responsibility without due grounds: one should undertake it when one has the strength to do so, and when the times permit it. To undertake it without sufficient strength is foolish; to undertake it at the wrong time is rash; to have the strength and encounter the right time, yet evade responsibility, is to set limits upon oneself. Sages and worthies follow none of these three courses. If, then, they alone assume responsibility for what all people share, how could they feel free to do otherwise? Master Cheng said, “Mengzi took responsibility for the Way upon himself.” From this I understand why Mengzi could not do otherwise. Allow me to explain fully.

What is this Way? It originates in Heaven and is fully present in human beings; it is the Way that all under Heaven, past and present, follow together. What Master Han described—“Yao transmitted it to Shun, Shun to Yu, Yu to Tang, Tang to Wen, Wu, and the Duke of Zhou, and Wen, Wu, and the Duke of Zhou to Kongzi”—was in every case this very thing. Master Yan surely attained Kongzi’s Way. Why, then, with his basket of food and gourd of drink in a humble lane, did he take delight in his own joy, seemingly unconcerned, as though he had no part in this Way? It was because Kongzi was there at that time to bear responsibility for it. Had there been no Kongzi then, Master Yan too would surely have carried his teachings throughout the world, relinquishing the peace of his humble lane to establish his household among the various …

title: 弘治十四年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
國去簞瓢之樂而傳食於諸侯至欲退焉
若愚以終其身不可得已孟子之得孔子
之道猶顏子也而其時則非顏子之時也
不遭顏子之時而欲樂顏子之樂是固無
賢者也何足以為孟子孟子之在當時蓋
有以好辯譏之者矣其曉之之言曰予豈
好辯哉予不得已也夫孟子之好辯將以
明道也非苟以求勝於人而已也即求勝
於人亦求孔子之道勝也非求勝其私說
===
也故曰不直則道不見我且直之此孟子
之所為以道自任者也且孟子之時何時
也邪說橫流之時也邪說橫流壞人心術
其禍蓋有不可勝言者孟子以命世亞聖
之才生當其時目擊其禍力足以任之而
不為之圖則安在其為聖賢也夫聖賢之
於衆人其性同也其性同則其道無不同
者然天之生聖賢非如衆人之泛泛然而
已也生一聖賢者將以衆人付之也天以
punctuated:
國，去簞瓢之樂而傳食於諸侯，至欲退焉，若愚以終其身，不可得已。孟子之得孔子之道，猶顏子也，而其時則非顏子之時也。不遭顏子之時，而欲樂顏子之樂，是固無賢者也，何足以為孟子？孟子之在當時，蓋有以好辯譏之者矣。其曉之之言曰：「予豈好辯哉？予不得已也。」夫孟子之好辯，將以明道也，非苟以求勝於人而已也。即求勝於人，亦求孔子之道勝也，非求勝其私說也。故曰：「不直則道不見，我且直之。」此孟子之所為以道自任者也。
且孟子之時何時也？邪說橫流之時也。邪說橫流，壞人心術，其禍蓋有不可勝言者。孟子以命世亞聖之才，生當其時，目擊其禍，力足以任之，而不為之圖，則安在其為聖賢也？夫聖賢之於衆人，其性同也；其性同，則其道無不同者。然天之生聖賢，非如衆人之泛泛然而已也。生一聖賢者，將以衆人付之也。天以
translation_en:
…states, abandon the pleasures of his rice basket and drinking gourd, and receive sustenance in succession from the feudal lords. Even if he wished to withdraw and spend the rest of his life seeming foolish, he could not have done so. Mengzi’s grasp of Kongzi’s Way was like Yanzi’s, but his times were not Yanzi’s times. To wish to enjoy Yanzi’s joys without living in Yanzi’s times would surely be to lack worthiness; how could that suffice for being Mengzi? In Mengzi’s day, there were indeed those who mocked him for his fondness for disputation. In explaining himself to them, he said: “Do I delight in disputation? I have no choice.” Mengzi’s disputation was intended to illuminate the Way, not merely to prevail over others. Even when he sought to prevail over others, he sought the victory of Kongzi’s Way, not the victory of his own private doctrines. Thus he said: “Unless these are set right, the Way will not be manifest. I shall set them right.” This is how Mengzi took responsibility for the Way.
Moreover, what sort of age was Mengzi’s? It was an age when pernicious doctrines ran rampant. Such doctrines corrupted people’s hearts and their moral dispositions, producing calamities beyond description. Mengzi possessed the talents of an epoch-making figure and Second Sage. Born into that age, he witnessed its calamities firsthand. If, though fully capable of shouldering this responsibility, he had made no effort to address them, wherein would his claim to sagehood or worthiness have lain? Sages and worthies share the same nature as ordinary people; since their nature is the same, their Way is likewise the same. Yet Heaven does not bring forth sages and worthies merely to live undistinguished lives like ordinary people. When it brings forth a sage or worthy, it intends to entrust the multitude to him. Heaven takes…

title: 弘治十四年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
眾人付之聖賢則聖賢視之猶一體也而
顧為獨善之計可乎今夫道路之間有遺
物焉其重百鈞問之路之人皆曰是烏獲
之物也過者日千百人力不能舉皆委而
去之不顧也烏獲過之而認得為己物將
委而去之乎抑亦舉而歸之其家乎孟子
之於道其認之也何以異此吾道之重不
啻百鈞而亦非孟子之所得私者然孔子
之嫡傳在孟子由孟子認之固若己物然
===
今而害於邪說之橫流則其為道路之遺
也久矣其私以為己任者政以舉其故物
耳而況其力又足以任之者乎其所以任
之者何也距楊墨也息邪說也當孟子時
邪說之害道者不止楊墨而楊墨為甚故
其距之最嚴其意以為人之所以為人者
以其有君父也孔子之道所以為正者以
其有仁義也楊氏為我是無君也墨氏兼
愛是無父也無父則不仁無君則不義不
punctuated:
眾人付之聖賢，則聖賢視之猶一體也，而顧為獨善之計，可乎？今夫道路之間有遺物焉，其重百鈞，問之路之人，皆曰：「是烏獲之物也。」過者日千百人，力不能舉，皆委而去之，不顧也。烏獲過之而認得為己物，將委而去之乎？抑亦舉而歸之其家乎？孟子之於道，其認之也何以異此？吾道之重，不啻百鈞，而亦非孟子之所得私者。然孔子之嫡傳在孟子，由孟子認之，固若己物然。
今而害於邪說之橫流，則其為道路之遺也久矣。其私以為己任者，政以舉其故物耳，而況其力又足以任之者乎？其所以任之者何也？距楊墨也，息邪說也。當孟子時，邪說之害道者不止楊墨，而楊墨為甚，故其距之最嚴。其意以為，人之所以為人者，以其有君父也；孔子之道所以為正者，以其有仁義也。楊氏為我，是無君也；墨氏兼愛，是無父也。無父則不仁，無君則不義。不
translation_en:
…the multitude is entrusted to the sages and worthies, who therefore regard them as forming one body with themselves. Could they nevertheless plan merely to perfect themselves alone? Suppose an object lies abandoned on a road, weighing a hundred jun. When people on the road are asked about it, they all say, “This belongs to Wu Huo.” Hundreds and thousands pass it each day, but, lacking the strength to lift it, all leave it behind without a backward glance. If Wu Huo passes and recognizes it as his own, will he leave it behind? Or will he lift it and carry it home? How does Mengzi’s recognition of the Way differ from this? Our Way weighs more than a hundred jun, yet it is not something Mengzi could possess exclusively. Nevertheless, the direct transmission from Kongzi rested with Mengzi; in recognizing it, he naturally regarded it as something of his own.
Now, harmed by the unchecked spread of heterodox teachings, the Way had long lain like an abandoned object on the road. In personally taking it as his responsibility, he was simply lifting up what had always been his own. How much more should he do so when his strength was sufficient for the task! How did he discharge this responsibility? By opposing Yang Zhu and Mo Di and putting an end to heterodox teachings. In Mengzi’s time, the heterodox teachings that harmed the Way were not limited to those of Yang and Mo, but theirs were the most harmful; hence he opposed them most sternly. His reasoning was that what makes people human is their recognition of ruler and father, and what makes Kongzi’s Way correct is its benevolence and righteousness. Yang’s doctrine of acting for oneself amounts to recognizing no ruler; Mo’s doctrine of impartial love amounts to recognizing no father. To recognize no father is to lack benevolence; to recognize no ruler is to lack righteousness. Without…

title: 弘治十四年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
仁不義則其去禽獸不遠矣使楊墨而非
人也則可楊墨亦人耳顧乃陷於禽獸而
不自知又以引吾同道之人使我坐視其
禍而不之救是縱之也助之也其去楊墨
幾何故昌言極論必使天下之人曉然知
楊墨之害而後已楊墨之道息則孔子之
道著矣其他異端曲說私智小數凡可以
病吾正道者一一辭而闢之以塞其源若
為並耕之說者闢之為義外之說者闢之
===
為善戰之說者闢之為連諸侯之說者闢
之闢乎彼所以衛乎此也其惡之也切故
其闢之也嚴其任之也重故其衛之也力
於乎孟子之有功於斯道也大矣夫孟子
之功固大矣而其不得已之故則非知道
之君子有不能真知之者盖其所遭之時
與其所賦之才力皆有不容不任焉者故
也使其幸而得為孔子之徒則陋巷之樂
當與顏子同之此任固無與也又不然□
punctuated:
仁不義，則其去禽獸不遠矣。使楊墨而非人也，則可；楊墨亦人耳，顧乃陷於禽獸而不自知，又以引吾同道之人。使我坐視其禍而不之救，是縱之也，助之也，其去楊墨幾何？故昌言極論，必使天下之人曉然知楊墨之害而後已。楊墨之道息，則孔子之道著矣。其他異端曲說、私智小數，凡可以病吾正道者，一一辭而闢之，以塞其源。若為並耕之說者，闢之；為義外之說者，闢之；為善戰之說者，闢之；為連諸侯之說者，闢之。闢乎彼，所以衛乎此也。其惡之也切，故其闢之也嚴；其任之也重，故其衛之也力。於乎！孟子之有功於斯道也大矣！

夫孟子之功固大矣，而其不得已之故，則非知道之君子，有不能真知之者。盖其所遭之時與其所賦之才力，皆有不容不任焉者故也。使其幸而得為孔子之徒，則陋巷之樂，當與顏子同之，此任固無與也。又不然，□
translation_en:
…without benevolence or righteousness, they are not far removed from birds and beasts. If Yang Zhu and Mo Di were not human, that might be acceptable; yet Yang and Mo are human too. Nevertheless, they sink to the level of birds and beasts without knowing it, and draw others who share our Way along with them. If I were to sit by and watch this calamity without coming to their rescue, I would be indulging them and assisting them. How far would that place me from Yang and Mo? Thus Mengzi spoke openly and argued to the utmost, refusing to stop until everyone under Heaven clearly understood the harm caused by Yang and Mo. Once their teachings ceased, the Way of Kongzi would become manifest. As for other heterodox doctrines, distorted arguments, self-serving cleverness, and petty stratagems—anything that could injure our orthodox Way—he refuted and rejected each in turn, blocking them at their source. Those who advocated that rulers till the fields alongside the people, he refuted; those who claimed that righteousness is external, he refuted; those who advocated skill in warfare, he refuted; and those who advocated alliances among the feudal lords, he refuted. Refuting those teachings was his means of defending this Way. Because his abhorrence was profound, his refutations were stern; because his responsibility was weighty, his defense was vigorous. Ah! Great indeed was Mengzi’s service to this Way!

Mengzi’s achievement was certainly great. Yet unless one is a gentleman who understands the Way, one may fail truly to understand why he had no choice but to act. This was because both the age in which he lived and the abilities with which he was endowed made it impossible for him not to shoulder this responsibility. Had he been fortunate enough to become a disciple of Kongzi, he would have shared Master Yan’s joy in his humble alley, and this responsibility would have been no concern of his. Or, failing that, [illegible character] …

title: 弘治十四年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
使顏子與之並生於戰國則孟子猶有可
諉者亦將退焉若愚以終其身而已耳今
孔顏既不可作而旁觀一世之人其才力
又皆無足與於斯者然則孟子不以身任
之而欲諉之誰哉故程子之言不徒曰任
道而必曰自任而又曰以道自任任者如
有所負而不釋之辭自者獨致其力而不
容人參之之辭以者如物在手而左右之
之辭非孟子之識時以察其幾量力以致
===
其决其孰能與於此哉程子生於千四百
年之後而推尊之如此其可謂深知孟子
之心者矣雖然斯言也程子非獨為孟子
發也盖亦有自狀之意存焉程子之道上
接孟子之傳者也自孟子後以道自任者
非斯人吾誰與歸
表
擬宋龍圖閣直學士趙汝愚進名臣奏議
表〔淳熙十三年〕
punctuated:
使顏子與之並生於戰國，則孟子猶有可諉者，亦將退焉，若愚以終其身而已耳。今孔顏既不可作，而旁觀一世之人，其才力又皆無足與於斯者，然則孟子不以身任之，而欲諉之誰哉？故程子之言，不徒曰任道，而必曰自任，而又曰以道自任。任者，如有所負而不釋之辭；自者，獨致其力而不容人參之之辭；以者，如物在手而左右之之辭。非孟子之識時以察其幾，量力以致其决，其孰能與於此哉？程子生於千四百年之後，而推尊之如此，其可謂深知孟子之心者矣。雖然，斯言也，程子非獨為孟子發也，盖亦有自狀之意存焉。程子之道，上接孟子之傳者也。自孟子後，以道自任者，非斯人，吾誰與歸？

表

擬宋龍圖閣直學士趙汝愚進名臣奏議表〔淳熙十三年〕
translation_en:
…Had Master Yan lived alongside him in the Warring States period, Mengzi would still have had someone to whom he could entrust this responsibility. He too would then have withdrawn, appearing foolish, and simply lived out his days. But Confucius and Master Yan could no longer be brought back to life; and when Mengzi surveyed the people of his age, none possessed the talent and strength sufficient to share in this undertaking. If Mengzi did not shoulder it himself, to whom could he entrust it? Thus Master Cheng did not merely say that he “undertook responsibility for the Way”; he insisted on saying that he “personally undertook responsibility,” and further that he “took the Way as his own responsibility.” “Undertaking responsibility” (ren) expresses bearing a burden without laying it down. “Personally” (zi) expresses exerting one’s strength alone, without allowing another to share in the task. “Taking” (yi) expresses holding something in one’s hands and directing it. Without Mengzi’s understanding of his times, through which he discerned their incipient tendencies, and his assessment of his own strength, through which he reached his resolve, who could have attained this? Master Cheng lived fourteen hundred years later, yet esteemed him so highly: he may indeed be said to have understood Mengzi’s heart profoundly. Nevertheless, Master Cheng spoke these words not solely about Mengzi; they also contained an intention to describe himself. Master Cheng’s Way directly continued the transmission from Mengzi. Among those who, since Mengzi, have taken the Way as their own responsibility, if not this man, whom should I follow?

Memorial

A memorial composed in the person of Zhao Ruyu of the Song, Auxiliary Academician of the Longtu Pavilion, submitting the Collected Memorials of Eminent Ministers (Mingchen zouyi)〔Thirteenth year of Chunxi [1186]〕

title: 弘治十四年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
王仲仁
同考試官教諭王批造語精而用事核
表製佳矣
考試官教諭高批得宋臣忠愛意
考試官教諭歐陽批詞語醇正得四六
之體可嘉
伏以
責難陳善懋昭建極之休納諫聽言丕闡
用中之懿義雖出於往古文則述於
===
先朝竊惟治道之盛衰寔關言路之通塞堯設
諫鼓聿臻於變之風武置戒鼗爰致永清
之化自時厥後理亂相尋循之則興違之
則壞粤稽
祖宗之立法固於諫諍而留心增置諫員大振
敢言之氣崇獎直節深懷不諱之朝許給
舍以封還責侍從以獻納故當時之士咸
思學古通經而投匭之章皆欲惠民保國
顧往事之可為法戒即今日之在所依歸
punctuated:
王仲仁

同考試官教諭王批：造語精而用事核，表製佳矣。
考試官教諭高批：得宋臣忠愛意。
考試官教諭歐陽批：詞語醇正，得四六之體，可嘉。

伏以：責難陳善，懋昭建極之休；納諫聽言，丕闡用中之懿。義雖出於往古，文則述於先朝。竊惟治道之盛衰，寔關言路之通塞。堯設諫鼓，聿臻於變之風；武置戒鼗，爰致永清之化。自時厥後，理亂相尋，循之則興，違之則壞。粤稽祖宗之立法，固於諫諍而留心。增置諫員，大振敢言之氣；崇獎直節，深懷不諱之朝。許給舍以封還，責侍從以獻納。故當時之士，咸思學古通經，而投匭之章，皆欲惠民保國。顧往事之可為法戒，即今日之在所依歸。
translation_en:
Wang Zhongren

Comment by Associate Examiner Wang, an Instructor: “The phrasing is refined and the historical allusions exact. This is an excellent memorial.”
Comment by Examiner Gao, an Instructor: “It captures the loyal devotion of a Song minister.”
Comment by Examiner Ouyang, an Instructor: “The language is pure and correct, and it conforms to the form of four-and-six parallel prose. Commendable.”

I humbly submit: By holding the ruler to demanding standards and setting forth what is good, ministers splendidly display the excellence of establishing the supreme standard; by accepting remonstrance and heeding counsel, the ruler amply manifests the virtue of applying the mean. Though these principles derive from distant antiquity, the writings recount them from preceding reigns.

I venture to reflect that the flourishing or decline of good government truly depends upon whether the channels for counsel are open or blocked. Yao set up a drum for remonstrance, thereby achieving a transforming moral influence; King Wu installed a hand drum for admonition, thereby bringing about enduring peace through his transforming rule. Thereafter, order and disorder followed one another: those who followed this practice flourished; those who departed from it fell into ruin.

Considering the institutions established by our imperial ancestors, they certainly gave careful attention to remonstrance. They increased the number of remonstrance officials, greatly encouraging the spirit of speaking boldly; they honored and rewarded steadfast integrity, deeply cherishing the ideal of a court where nothing was barred from discussion. They permitted Supervising Secretaries and Secretariat Drafters to return imperial directives under seal and charged attendant officials with presenting counsel. Thus the scholars of those days all aspired to study antiquity and master the Classics, and the memorials they deposited in the petition boxes all aimed to benefit the people and safeguard the state. Considering that past events can furnish both models and warnings, they are precisely what we should take as our guide today…

title: 弘治十四年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
因稡成百餘卷之書亦既閱二十年之乆
分門列類則自君道而訖邊防據事繫時
則由
欽宗而泝
藝祖豈但易求政事得失之跡盖亦可推
國家隆替之由顧効力於涓埃曷叨塵於
進御恭惟
〇〇〇〇孝隆
德壽澤洽黔黎圖作敬天恐起居之或懈禮嚴
===
敵國猶恢復之靡忘肆寤寐以思賢恒優
容而受諫惟哲后多求古訓而聖人不棄
邇言彼充棟之藏萬幾諒未暇及若連屏
之繪一目則已無遺妄意此書殊切人主
臣身違
象魏心係
龍墀才不如徵莫紀帝王之政忠惟慕相敢
陳晁董之文伏願
鑒此辛勤
punctuated: 因稡成百餘卷之書，亦既閱二十年之乆。分門列類，則自君道而訖邊防；據事繫時，則由欽宗而泝藝祖。豈但易求政事得失之跡，盖亦可推國家隆替之由。顧効力於涓埃，曷叨塵於進御？恭惟〇〇〇〇孝隆德壽，澤洽黔黎；圖作敬天，恐起居之或懈；禮嚴敵國，猶恢復之靡忘。肆寤寐以思賢，恒優容而受諫。惟哲后多求古訓，而聖人不棄邇言。彼充棟之藏，萬幾諒未暇及；若連屏之繪，一目則已無遺。妄意此書殊切人主。臣身違象魏，心係龍墀。才不如徵，莫紀帝王之政；忠惟慕相，敢陳晁董之文。伏願鑒此辛勤
translation_en:
…Accordingly, I compiled a work of more than a hundred juan, a task that has now taken twenty years. Arranged by subject and category, it extends from the way of the ruler to frontier defense; linking events to their dates, it traces backward from Qinzong to Yizu, the dynastic founder. It not only makes the evidence of successes and failures in government readily accessible, but also allows one to infer the causes of the state's rise and decline. Yet my contribution is as slight as a drop of water or a speck of dust: how dare I presume to present it for imperial perusal?
I reverently reflect that Your Majesty [four circles in the transcription] has shown exalted filial devotion toward Deshou [?], and that your beneficence reaches the common people. You have had a picture made concerning reverence for Heaven [?], fearing any lapse in your daily conduct; although observing strict ceremonial relations with the rival state, you have never forgotten the recovery of lost territory. Thus, waking and sleeping, you think of worthy men, and constantly receive remonstrance with generous forbearance. The enlightened sovereign seeks instruction abundantly from antiquity, and the sage does not disregard ordinary people's words. Amid your myriad affairs, you surely have little leisure to consult collections that fill whole buildings; but a depiction spread across adjoining screens can be taken in completely at a glance. I venture to think that this book is especially pertinent to a ruler.
Your servant is far from the palace gate-towers, yet my heart remains bound to the imperial steps. My ability falls short of Zheng's, and I cannot record the government of emperors and kings; in loyalty I aspire only to emulate Xiang [?], and dare to submit writings in the manner of Chao and Dong. I humbly pray that you will recognize this painstaking labor…

title: 弘治十四年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
留神乙覽不必泛求而寡要但常致力以精
思對
列聖於遺編當有因往知來之益屈群策而决
事不效尋章摘句之為用躋世道於昇平
以復
祖宗之隆盛臣無任瞻
天仰
聖激切屏營之至謹以所撰皇朝名臣奏議一
百五十卷奉
===
表隨
進以
聞
第叁塲
策
第一問
楊士雲
同考試官訓導張批寫出
聖祖創治之艱頌
punctuated:
留神乙覽，不必泛求而寡要，但常致力以精思。對列聖於遺編，當有因往知來之益；屈群策而决事，不效尋章摘句之為用。躋世道於昇平，以復祖宗之隆盛。臣無任瞻天仰聖、激切屏營之至，謹以所撰《皇朝名臣奏議》一百五十卷，奉表隨進以聞。
第叁塲
策
第一問
楊士雲
同考試官訓導張批：寫出聖祖創治之艱，頌
translation_en:
…give it your attention in your imperial reading. You need not range widely while grasping little of the essentials, but should continually apply yourself to careful reflection. Encountering the successive sage emperors in the writings they left behind, you will gain the benefit of understanding what is to come through what has gone before. Drawing upon the counsels of many to decide affairs, you will not follow the practice of merely searching out passages and plucking out phrases. Bring the realm to peace and prosperity, thereby restoring the flourishing achievements of your imperial ancestors. Your servant, gazing toward Heaven and looking up to Your Sagely Majesty, is overcome with fervent emotion and trembling awe. I respectfully submit, together with this memorial, the 150 juan of Memorials of Eminent Ministers of Our Imperial Dynasty (Huangchao mingchen zouyi) that I have compiled, for Your Majesty’s attention.

Policy Essays
First Question
Yang Shiyun
