title: 弘治十四年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
誥之意粲然有章足見所學
同考試官教諭泰批
聖製一策敷荅詳盡斷制明白真策手也
考試官教諭高批
皇祖與湯武時勢之難易化導之異同士子間知其畧然未有如
此卷敷陳具盡者況他策俱稱魁多士知
無愧矣
考試官教諭歐陽批
聖祖創造之難垂訓之意揄揚殆盡其服膺而有得者歟
===
知我
聖祖定天下之難當知我
聖祖致太平之難蓋武功以定天下文教以致
太平此湯武與我
聖祖之所同也時異勢殊道有升降取之既難
化之亦不易此我
聖祖與湯武之所以異也知乎此則
聖神功德之盛庶可窺其萬一矣請因明問而
敬對之自古大亂之後必有聖人起而掃
punctuated:
誥之意，粲然有章，足見所學。

同考試官教諭泰批：聖製一策，敷荅詳盡，斷制明白，真策手也。

考試官教諭高批：皇祖與湯武時勢之難易、化導之異同，士子間知其畧，然未有如此卷敷陳具盡者。況他策俱稱，魁多士知無愧矣。

考試官教諭歐陽批：聖祖創造之難、垂訓之意，揄揚殆盡，其服膺而有得者歟？

知我聖祖定天下之難，當知我聖祖致太平之難。蓋武功以定天下，文教以致太平，此湯武與我聖祖之所同也。時異勢殊，道有升降，取之既難，化之亦不易，此我聖祖與湯武之所以異也。知乎此，則聖神功德之盛，庶可窺其萬一矣。請因明問而敬對之。自古大亂之後，必有聖人起而掃
translation_en:
…the meaning of the proclamations is brilliantly and coherently expressed, amply demonstrating his learning.

Comment by Associate Examiner Tai, Instructor: His policy essay on the imperial composition develops its response fully and thoroughly, and its judgments are clear. He is truly an accomplished writer of policy essays.

Comment by Examiner Gao, Instructor: Candidates sometimes understand in outline the relative difficulties of the circumstances faced by our imperial ancestor and by Tang and Wu, and the similarities and differences in their moral transformation and guidance of the people. Yet none has expounded these matters as fully as this script. Moreover, his other policy essays are all commensurate in quality; he can deservedly rank foremost among the candidates [?].

Comment by Examiner Ouyang, Instructor: He has expounded and praised almost exhaustively the difficulties our sagely ancestor faced in founding the dynasty and the intent of the instructions he left to posterity. Surely he has taken them to heart and gained understanding from them?

To understand the difficulty with which our sagely ancestor pacified All-under-Heaven, one must understand the difficulty with which he brought about Great Peace. Military achievements serve to pacify All-under-Heaven, while civil instruction serves to bring about Great Peace: this is what Tang and Wu shared with our sagely ancestor. But their times and circumstances differed, and the Way had its ascendancy and decline. Since winning the realm was difficult, transforming its people was no easy matter either: this is how our sagely ancestor differed from Tang and Wu. Understanding this, we may perhaps glimpse one ten-thousandth of the grandeur of his sagely and divine achievements and virtue. Allow me respectfully to reply in accordance with your illuminating question. Since antiquity, after great disorder, a sage has invariably arisen to sweep away…

title: 弘治十四年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
除其禍若湯之放桀武王之伐紂皆神武
不殺一怒而安天下之民者然其為功則
未有若我
太祖之難者也是故夏之德衰于桀成湯于是
乎有鳴條之役罪人既黜則兆民允殖矣
未聞放桀之後復别有所攻伐也商之德
衰于紂武王于是乎有牧野之師凶殘既
取則四海永清矣未聞伐紂之後復别有
所戡定也元政不綱群雄訌亂驅烏合之
衆逞鴟張之威淫名僭號相望于天下甲
僨而乙起東討而西叛恣為荼毒賊我良
民時勢之難為未有甚于此時者也我
太祖以江淮聖人應運而起恭天成命伐暴救
民一征而顛賊亮再征而揜偽吳三征而
披閩粵四征而卷齊魯遂擣元都掇秦晋
掀巴蜀復中國帝王所自立之地况不階
寸土一民呼吸響應以成大業簡冊所載
未之前聞較之資亳衆以興師藉西師而
punctuated: 除其禍。若湯之放桀、武王之伐紂，皆神武不殺，一怒而安天下之民者。然其為功，則未有若我太祖之難者也。是故夏之德衰于桀，成湯于是乎有鳴條之役，罪人既黜，則兆民允殖矣。未聞放桀之後，復别有所攻伐也。商之德衰于紂，武王于是乎有牧野之師，凶殘既取，則四海永清矣。未聞伐紂之後，復别有所戡定也。元政不綱，群雄訌亂，驅烏合之衆，逞鴟張之威，淫名僭號，相望于天下。甲僨而乙起，東討而西叛，恣為荼毒，賊我良民。時勢之難為，未有甚于此時者也。我太祖以江淮聖人應運而起，恭天成命，伐暴救民。一征而顛賊亮，再征而揜偽吳，三征而披閩粵，四征而卷齊魯，遂擣元都，掇秦晋，掀巴蜀，復中國帝王所自立之地。况不階寸土一民，呼吸響應，以成大業，簡冊所載，未之前聞。較之資亳衆以興師、藉西師而
translation_en:
…sweep away its calamities. Tang’s banishment of Jie and King Wu’s campaign against Zhou both displayed divine martial prowess without slaughter: with a single outburst of anger, they brought peace to the people of the realm. Yet neither accomplished his task amid difficulties comparable to those faced by our Taizu. When the virtue of Xia declined under Jie, Cheng Tang fought the battle of Mingtiao. Once the guilty ruler had been deposed, the multitudes could truly flourish. We have not heard that, after banishing Jie, he had further campaigns to wage elsewhere. When the virtue of Shang declined under Zhou, King Wu launched the campaign at Muye. Once the cruel tyrant had been captured, all within the Four Seas enjoyed lasting peace. We have not heard that, after attacking Zhou, he had further territories to subdue.

Yuan government lost its order, and rival strongmen plunged the realm into strife. Driving motley hordes before them and flaunting their predatory might, they assumed extravagant designations and usurped titles, appearing everywhere throughout the realm. One fell and another arose; when a campaign was launched in the east, rebellion broke out in the west. They inflicted suffering without restraint and harmed our good people. Never had circumstances been harder to manage than at this time.

Our Taizu, the sage of the Jiang and Huai region, arose in response to the destined turn of events. Reverently obeying Heaven’s settled mandate, he attacked the violent and rescued the people. In his first campaign he overthrew the rebel Liang; in his second he overwhelmed the spurious Wu regime; in his third he broke through Min and Yue; in his fourth he swept through Qi and Lu. He then struck the Yuan capital, seized Qin and Jin, overturned resistance in Ba and Shu, and recovered the lands in which the emperors and kings of the Central Realm had established themselves. Moreover, he began without so much as an inch of territory or a single subject to build upon; at his call, people responded like an echo, enabling him to accomplish his great undertaking. Nothing like it had previously been heard of in the historical records. Compared with one who drew upon the people of Bo to raise an army, or one who relied upon the army of the west to…

title: 弘治十四年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
舉事者其難易又何如也嗚呼盛矣
祖訓有曰羣雄之強盛至難服也而朕以服之
觀于此豈不益信矣乎自古帝王之興必
有施命以告天下若成湯之誕告萬方武
王之明大命于妹邦皆渙其大號風動而
教化之者然其為教亦未有若我
太祖之難者也是故當桀之時同惡相濟者雖
有其人然止于簡賢附勢者耳其餘則皆
良民也故成湯之誥無費詞商之餘民染
===
紂之惡者亦不過妹土之人耳其他故家
遺俗尚多有之故武王之誥專妹土元以
夷狄入主中國變我綱常汙我衣冠盡天
下之民耳濡目染日改月化相率而為鳥
獸之羣者幾百年教化之難行未有甚于
此時者也我
太祖用夏變夷駸駸至于十八九年之後其風
猶未盡革于是有
三編之誥頒示天下一不已而至于再再不已
punctuated: 舉事者，其難易又何如也？嗚呼，盛矣！《祖訓》有曰：「羣雄之強盛，至難服也，而朕以服之。」觀于此，豈不益信矣乎？自古帝王之興，必有施命以告天下，若成湯之誕告萬方、武王之明大命于妹邦，皆渙其大號，風動而教化之者。然其為教，亦未有若我太祖之難者也。是故當桀之時，同惡相濟者雖有其人，然止于簡賢附勢者耳，其餘則皆良民也，故成湯之誥無費詞。商之餘民，染紂之惡者亦不過妹土之人耳，其他故家遺俗尚多有之，故武王之誥專妹土。元以夷狄入主中國，變我綱常，汙我衣冠，盡天下之民耳濡目染，日改月化，相率而為鳥獸之羣者幾百年，教化之難行，未有甚于此時者也。我太祖用夏變夷，駸駸至于十八九年之後，其風猶未盡革。于是有三編之誥，頒示天下，一不已而至于再，再不已……
translation_en:
…in undertaking their enterprise, how did the difficulty or ease of their task compare with his? Ah, how magnificent! The Ancestral Instructions states: “The rival leaders were powerful and flourishing, exceedingly difficult to subdue; yet I subdued them.” Considering this, can we fail to believe it all the more firmly? Whenever emperors and kings arose in antiquity, they invariably issued commands to proclaim their intentions to all under Heaven. Thus Cheng Tang made his great announcement to the myriad regions, and King Wu made the great mandate clear to the domain of Mei. All broadcast their great proclamations, transforming and instructing the people as wind moves things. Yet none faced difficulties in giving instruction such as those faced by our Taizu.

Thus, in Jie’s time, although there were men who aided one another in wrongdoing, these were limited to those who slighted the worthy [?] and attached themselves to the powerful. The rest were all good people, so Cheng Tang’s announcement required no expenditure of words. Among the surviving people of Shang, those tainted by Zhou’s wickedness were likewise no more than the people of Mei. Elsewhere, many old families and inherited customs still remained, so King Wu’s announcement addressed Mei alone.

The Yuan, as barbarians, entered and ruled the Central Kingdom, altering our cardinal relationships and constant moral principles and defiling our caps and robes. All the people under Heaven were steeped in these influences through what they heard and saw, changing day by day and month by month, leading one another into becoming flocks of birds and beasts for nearly a hundred years. Never had moral instruction been harder to put into effect than at this time. Our Taizu used the civilization of the Chinese to transform the barbarians, but even as time advanced past eighteen or nineteen years, their customs had still not been entirely reformed. Thereupon the Admonitions in Three Compilations were promulgated throughout the realm. He did not stop at the first, but proceeded to a second; nor did he stop at the second…

title: 弘治十四年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
而至于三如父母臨之師保誨之必欲與
斯世同躋于皇極之五福而後已其曰申
明五常即克綏厥猷之旨也其曰為民造
福即輯寧邦家之心也其曰誥如擒惡受
賞即群飲勿佚盡執拘以歸于周之說也
其曰輕生易死復出
三誥以示之即勿庸殺之姑惟教之之意也勝
殘去殺已見於創業之時禮樂可興不待
於繼世之後於乎盛矣
===
祖訓又曰民經世亂務習奸猾至難齊也而朕
已齊之觀于此又豈不益信矣乎夫湯武
皆古聖人也其功德之盛復何間然顧其
所遇之時視我
聖祖則有不同焉者此我
聖祖之所以為難也百三十餘年來至于今日
天下之民皆得以安養于大順大化之域
優游于遵道遵義之天者果誰之力歟用
之而不知習之而不察者此凡民也非豪
punctuated:
而至于三，如父母臨之，師保誨之，必欲與斯世同躋于皇極之五福而後已。其曰「申明五常」，即「克綏厥猷」之旨也。其曰「為民造福」，即「輯寧邦家」之心也。其曰「誥如擒惡受賞」，即「群飲勿佚，盡執拘以歸于周」之說也。其曰「輕生易死，復出三誥以示之」，即「勿庸殺之，姑惟教之」之意也。勝殘去殺，已見於創業之時；禮樂可興，不待於繼世之後。於乎盛矣！

《祖訓》又曰：「民經世亂，務習奸猾，至難齊也，而朕已齊之。」觀于此，又豈不益信矣乎？夫湯武皆古聖人也，其功德之盛，復何間然？顧其所遇之時，視我聖祖，則有不同焉者，此我聖祖之所以為難也。百三十餘年來，至于今日，天下之民皆得以安養于大順大化之域，優游于遵道遵義之天者，果誰之力歟？用之而不知，習之而不察者，此凡民也，非豪
translation_en:
…and went on to a third, watching over them like parents and instructing them like tutors and guardians, determined not to rest until he had brought the people of this age together into the five blessings of the August Standard. His words, “Explain and make clear the Five Constant Virtues,” convey the purpose of “enabling them to settle into the proper way.” His words, “Create blessings for the people,” express the resolve to “bring peace to the state and its households.” His words, “The proclamation: apprehend evildoers and receive rewards” [?], convey the teaching, “Do not let those who drink in groups escape; arrest them all and bring them to Zhou.” His words, “They hold life cheap and readily face death; issue the Three Proclamations again to instruct them,” express the intention, “There is no need to kill them; for the present, simply teach them.” Overcoming brutality and dispensing with killing were already evident during the founding of the dynasty; rites and music could flourish without awaiting the reigns of his successors. Ah, how magnificent!

The Ancestral Injunctions further states: “The people have lived through an age of disorder and have devoted themselves to deceit and cunning. They are exceedingly difficult to bring into order, yet I have brought them into order.” In light of this, how could one fail to believe these words all the more firmly? Tang and Wu were both sages of antiquity: what fault could possibly be found with their abundant achievements and virtue? Yet the times they encountered differed from those faced by our Sagely Ancestor. This is what made our Sagely Ancestor’s task so difficult. For more than a hundred and thirty years, down to the present day, the people throughout the realm have all been able to live in peace and security within a domain of perfect harmony and moral transformation, dwelling at ease beneath a heaven where the Way and righteousness are followed. Whose efforts, indeed, have made this possible? Those who benefit from it without knowing, and grow accustomed to it without examining it, are ordinary people, not men of outstanding…

title: 弘治十四年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
傑之士也愚也何敢自擬于豪傑執事倘
與其進尚能歌猗那之詩誦下武之章以
揚厲
神功聖德于商周之世
第二問
楊敷順
同考試官學正王批具事核立詞正讀之
令人起敬其亦兩省之傑者
考試官教諭高批西京人才枚數幾盡
===
而評品亦當是真尚友者乎可敬
考試官教諭歐陽批古帝王用賢圖治子能
一一品第言之亦可以覘子之所養矣
帝王之治世必資乎賢而賢才之行誼當
究其實盖君以臣興臣以君出名以實著
實以名求也然欲評品其高下不於行誼
之實其何以哉執事發策下詢承學請勉
對其萬一粤稽諸古虞舜之帝也雖曰以
玄德之升聞而其所以致風動之休則有
punctuated:
傑之士也。愚也何敢自擬于豪傑？執事倘與其進，尚能歌《猗那》之詩，誦《下武》之章，以揚厲神功聖德于商周之世。
第二問
楊敷順
同考試官學正王批：具事核，立詞正，讀之令人起敬，其亦兩省之傑者。
考試官教諭高批：西京人才，枚數幾盡，而評品亦當，是真尚友者乎！可敬。
考試官教諭歐陽批：古帝王用賢圖治，子能一一品第言之，亦可以覘子之所養矣。
帝王之治世，必資乎賢，而賢才之行誼，當究其實。盖君以臣興，臣以君出，名以實著，實以名求也。然欲評品其高下，不於行誼之實，其何以哉？執事發策下詢，承學請勉對其萬一。粤稽諸古，虞舜之帝也，雖曰以玄德之升聞，而其所以致風動之休，則有
translation_en:
…men of outstanding ability. How could I, in my ignorance, dare compare myself to such men? If you, honored examiners, should approve my advancement, I may yet sing the poem “Yi Na” and recite the ode “Continuing the Martial Achievement” (Xia Wu), thereby extolling our founder’s divine achievements and sagely virtue alongside those of the Shang and Zhou ages.
Second Policy Question
Yang Fushun
Comment by Associate Examiner Wang, Instructor: “The facts presented are sound, and the wording is correct. Reading this inspires respect. He too is an outstanding man of the two provinces.”
Comment by Examiner Gao, Instructor: “He enumerates almost all the talented men of the Western Han, and his assessments are also appropriate. Is he indeed one who takes the ancients as his friends? Worthy of respect.”
Comment by Examiner Ouyang, Instructor: “You can discuss and rank, one by one, the worthy men whom ancient emperors and kings employed in seeking good government. This also offers a glimpse of your own cultivation.”
For emperors and kings to govern the world, they must rely upon worthy men; yet the conduct and integrity of those men must be examined for their substance. For rulers flourish through their ministers, and ministers come forth through their rulers; reputation becomes manifest through substance, and substance is sought through reputation. But if one wishes to assess their relative standing, how can one do so without examining the substance of their conduct and integrity? You, honored examiners, have issued a policy question and condescended to inquire of us students. Allow me to endeavor to answer even a small part of it. Looking back into antiquity, when Shun of Yu became emperor, although it is said that news of his profound virtue had reached those above, his achievement of the splendid transformation that spread like the wind depended upon such men as…

title: 弘治十四年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
禹稷契皐陶之輩焉周文之王也雖曰以
明德之肇造而其所以培王業之基者則
有太顛閎夭散宜生之徒焉是古之帝王
未有不資賢人而共理者載諸典籍漫無
可議姑舉漢世言之嬴秦鹿失漢室龍興
方其草昧之初則張良蕭何韓信之力居
多及其建儲之際則東園公夏黄公綺里
季甪里先生之功為最之數子者固皆一
時之偉人至其優劣則有可言者氣象近
===
儒良獨優矣出處不易四皓有焉而絾繫
夷族者又其下也及夫孝武繼世雄材大
略維時茂材應舉學富天人則董仲舒其
人也賢良有策名重經術則公孫弘兒寬
其人也之三儒者雖皆一代之英俊而其
優劣亦有可較者正誼明道董最高矣中
和立論寬其次焉而曲學阿世者風斯下
也自是之外則曹參之將相可觀也周昌
之剛正可取也王陵之仗義直言劉章之
punctuated:
禹、稷、契、皐陶之輩焉。周文之王也，雖曰以明德之肇造，而其所以培王業之基者，則有太顛、閎夭、散宜生之徒焉。是古之帝王，未有不資賢人而共理者。載諸典籍，漫無可議。姑舉漢世言之：嬴秦鹿失，漢室龍興，方其草昧之初，則張良、蕭何、韓信之力居多；及其建儲之際，則東園公、夏黄公、綺里季、甪里先生之功為最。之數子者，固皆一時之偉人，至其優劣，則有可言者。氣象近儒，良獨優矣；出處不易，四皓有焉；而絾繫夷族者，又其下也。
及夫孝武繼世，雄材大略，維時茂材應舉，學富天人，則董仲舒其人也；賢良有策，名重經術，則公孫弘、兒寬其人也。之三儒者，雖皆一代之英俊，而其優劣亦有可較者。正誼明道，董最高矣；中和立論，寬其次焉；而曲學阿世者，風斯下也。自是之外，則曹參之將相可觀也，周昌之剛正可取也，王陵之仗義直言、劉章之
translation_en:
…such men as Yu, Ji, Xie, and Gao Yao. When King Wen of Zhou became king, although he is said to have founded his undertaking through luminous virtue, among those who helped him lay the foundations of the royal enterprise were Tai Dian, Hong Yao, and San Yisheng. Thus, none of the emperors and kings of antiquity failed to rely upon worthy men to govern together with them. This is recorded in the canonical writings, leaving nothing to dispute.
Let us take the Han age as an example. The Qin house of Ying lost the deer—the empire—and the Han house rose like a dragon. In the turmoil of its beginnings, Zhang Liang, Xiao He, and Han Xin contributed the greatest share of effort. When it came to establishing the heir apparent, the greatest merit belonged to Dongyuan Gong, Xiahuang Gong, Qili Ji, and Master Luli. These men were certainly all outstanding figures of their time, but their relative merits admit of discussion. In a bearing approaching that of a Confucian scholar, Liang alone excelled. In remaining constant in their principles whether entering service or withdrawing, the Four Hoary Elders distinguished themselves. Those who suffered fetters [?] and the extermination of their clans ranked below them.
When Emperor Xiaowu succeeded to the throne, he possessed extraordinary ability and grand strategic vision. Among those recommended for outstanding talent, the man whose learning encompassed Heaven and humanity was Dong Zhongshu. Among the worthy and good who presented policy essays and won renown for mastery of the Classics were Gongsun Hong and Ni Kuan. Although these three Confucian scholars were all eminent men of their age, their relative merits can also be compared. In setting righteousness aright and illuminating the Way, Dong stood highest. In grounding his arguments in centrality and harmony, Kuan came next. The one who distorted learning to flatter his age was inferior in character [?]. Beyond these men, Cao Can’s achievements as general and chancellor merit attention, and Zhou Chang’s firmness and uprightness deserve esteem; Wang Ling’s championing of righteousness and forthright speech, and Liu Zhang’s…

title: 弘治十四年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
托田進諫賢可知矣卒之諸吕盡滅劉氏
無虞致治之功可少乎賈誼之治安時政
賈山之至言懇切賢可見矣卒之帝心知
嚮風俗少移致治之功可短乎軍法嚴明
則有周亞夫矣明習律曆則有張蒼者矣
斷獄明允終致無冤之譽非張釋之之能
乎而于定國則繼美者也性資忠直竟寢
淮南之謀非汲黯之賢乎而申屠嘉則庶
幾者也以霍光之性資重厚則立宣而有
===
功以嚴延年之正直不阿則彈劾而莫避
魏相之嚴毅廉正丙吉之深厚不伐則宰
相之得人也趙充國之料敵制勝張安世
之宿衞忠貞則將帥之得人也如黃霸龔
遂之善政如延壽文翁之教化非守令之
得人乎二疏之去有以長恬退之風龔勝
之死有以勵志行之士以至忠誠則有劉
向議論則有匡衡與夫或以文章顯或以
篤行聞或擅一職之勞或專一節之美璧
punctuated: 托田進諫，賢可知矣。卒之諸吕盡滅，劉氏無虞，致治之功可少乎？賈誼之治安時政，賈山之至言懇切，賢可見矣。卒之帝心知嚮，風俗少移，致治之功可短乎？軍法嚴明，則有周亞夫矣；明習律曆，則有張蒼者矣。斷獄明允，終致無冤之譽，非張釋之之能乎？而于定國則繼美者也。性資忠直，竟寢淮南之謀，非汲黯之賢乎？而申屠嘉則庶幾者也。以霍光之性資重厚，則立宣而有功；以嚴延年之正直不阿，則彈劾而莫避。魏相之嚴毅廉正，丙吉之深厚不伐，則宰相之得人也；趙充國之料敵制勝，張安世之宿衞忠貞，則將帥之得人也。如黃霸、龔遂之善政，如延壽、文翁之教化，非守令之得人乎？二疏之去，有以長恬退之風；龔勝之死，有以勵志行之士。以至忠誠則有劉向，議論則有匡衡，與夫或以文章顯，或以篤行聞，或擅一職之勞，或專一節之美，璧
translation_en:
…remonstrating by invoking farming: his worthiness can be understood from this. In the end, the Lü clan was entirely destroyed, and the Liu house was free from danger. Could such contributions to good government be considered slight? Jia Yi’s proposals on peace, security, and contemporary governance, and the earnest urgency of Jia Shan’s Utmost Words, reveal their worthiness. In the end, the emperor understood where to direct his efforts, and customs changed somewhat. Could their contributions to good government be considered deficient?

For strict and clear military discipline, there was Zhou Yafu; for thorough knowledge of pitch standards and calendrical science, there was Zhang Cang. Was it not Zhang Shizhi’s ability in deciding cases intelligently and fairly that ultimately earned him a reputation for leaving no one unjustly condemned? Yu Dingguo carried on this excellence. Was it not Ji An’s worthiness, his loyal and upright disposition, that finally held the Prince of Huainan’s plot in abeyance? Shentu Jia approached him in these qualities. Huo Guang, with his steady and substantial disposition, rendered meritorious service by enthroning Emperor Xuan; Yan Yannian, upright and unbending, spared no one in his impeachments. Wei Xiang’s stern resolve, integrity, and rectitude, and Bing Ji’s profound generosity and freedom from boastfulness, show that worthy men had been found to serve as chief councilors. Zhao Chongguo’s ability to assess the enemy and secure victory, and Zhang Anshi’s loyalty and constancy in guarding the palace, show that worthy men had been found as military commanders. Did not the good administration of Huang Ba and Gong Sui, and the moral instruction of Yanshou and Wen Weng, likewise show that worthy men had been found as commandery governors and county magistrates?

The retirement of the two Shus helped foster a disposition toward contented withdrawal from office; Gong Sheng’s death encouraged men of firm purpose and virtuous conduct. For loyalty and sincerity there was Liu Xiang; for reasoned discussion there was Kuang Heng. There were also those distinguished for literary composition, those renowned for steadfast conduct, those outstanding in the service of a particular office, and those eminent for a particular virtue—like jade discs…

title: 弘治十四年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
峙林立弗可僂指是皆西漢得人之盛而
當時致治之隆未有舎此而得之者也雖
然亦有憾焉迹近儒矣終於黄老之歸論
固高矣不免災異之惑忘親立功識者有
譏洛陽少年君子興嘆近社稷臣者失之
褊迫比伊尹功者病於不學數君子皆一
代人物之楚楚者其失如此他何道哉此
其回視五臣四友蓋有不可同年而語者
矣然則玉必琢磨而後可成瑚璉之器人
===
必自勵而後可希賢聖之域愚也脫與幸
進而竊祿于
朝以立玉堦方寸地誓當尚友古人以虞周
之臣自期待區區漢臣何足言哉管見如
斯惟執事進而教之幸甚
第叄問
王仲仁
同考試官教諭王批說出弭災之意詳盡
無遺該博之學經綸之才純正之識於此
punctuated:
峙林立，弗可僂指，是皆西漢得人之盛，而當時致治之隆，未有舎此而得之者也。雖然，亦有憾焉：迹近儒矣，終於黄老之歸；論固高矣，不免災異之惑；忘親立功，識者有譏；洛陽少年，君子興嘆；近社稷臣者，失之褊迫；比伊尹功者，病於不學。數君子皆一代人物之楚楚者，其失如此，他何道哉？此其回視五臣四友，蓋有不可同年而語者矣。然則玉必琢磨而後可成瑚璉之器，人必自勵而後可希賢聖之域。愚也，脫與幸進而竊祿于朝，以立玉堦方寸地，誓當尚友古人，以虞周之臣自期待，區區漢臣何足言哉？管見如斯，惟執事進而教之，幸甚。

第叄問
王仲仁

同考試官教諭王批：說出弭災之意，詳盡無遺。該博之學，經綸之才，純正之識，於此
translation_en:
…standing tall and clustered like trees, too numerous to count on one’s fingers. All these exemplify the Western Han’s abundance of worthy men, and the flourishing government of that age could never have been achieved without them. Even so, there are grounds for regret. One whose conduct approached that of the Confucians ultimately turned to the teachings of Huang-Lao; another whose arguments were indeed lofty could not escape confusion over disasters and anomalies. One forgot his parents in pursuit of achievement, earning the criticism of discerning men; the young man of Luoyang moved gentlemen to sigh. One who approached the stature of a minister safeguarding the altars of soil and grain fell short through narrowness and impatience; another whose achievements were compared to those of Yi Yin suffered from a lack of learning. These gentlemen were all outstanding figures of their age. If their failings were such, what need is there to speak of the others? Looking back from them to the Five Ministers and Four Friends of antiquity, surely they cannot be spoken of in the same terms.

Thus jade must be carved and polished before it can become a ritual vessel, a hu or lian; people must exert themselves before they can aspire to the realm of worthies and sages. Should I, foolish as I am, happen to gain advancement through good fortune and undeservedly draw a salary at court, securing a tiny foothold upon the jade steps, I vow to take the ancients as my friends and hold myself to the standard of the ministers of Yu and Zhou. What would there be worth mentioning about the mere ministers of the Han? Such is my limited view. I would be most fortunate if you, honored sir, would advance me with your instruction.

Third Question
Wang Zhongren 王仲仁

Comment by Associate Examiner Wang, Instructor: The meaning of averting disasters is explained thoroughly, with nothing omitted. Broad learning, talent for ordering affairs, and sound and upright judgment—in this…

title: 弘治十四年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
策見之他日效用其風采必自有動人者
考試官教諭髙批弭災一事議論是識
見髙可以觀子之志矣
考試官教諭歐陽批召災有由弭災有術
此策言之甚悉録之以為
今日脩省之助
天人不能無交感之理君臣當盡乎交修
之誠盖天人本乎一理而君臣貴於一心
也天之變異固將示戒於人使或君臣之
===
間所以消弭之者有一未至則亦何以收
格天之功哉此愚於明問之及而不能不
重有所感必欲吾
君臣上下更相戒飭以盡應天之實庶乎天意
可回民心可得而和氣可應也夫地何為
而震也周太史伯陽甫曰陽伏而不能出
陰迫而不能升則地震劉向五行傳曰治
宫室飾臺榭則稼穡不成土失其性而為
災則地震之異固非無自而然也然自古
punctuated:
策見之，他日效用，其風采必自有動人者。
考試官教諭髙批：弭災一事，議論是，識見髙，可以觀子之志矣。
考試官教諭歐陽批：召災有由，弭災有術，此策言之甚悉，録之以為今日脩省之助。
天人不能無交感之理，君臣當盡乎交修之誠。盖天人本乎一理，而君臣貴於一心也。天之變異，固將示戒於人，使或君臣之間所以消弭之者有一未至，則亦何以收格天之功哉？此愚於明問之及，而不能不重有所感，必欲吾君臣上下更相戒飭，以盡應天之實，庶乎天意可回，民心可得，而和氣可應也。夫地何為而震也？周太史伯陽甫曰：「陽伏而不能出，陰迫而不能升，則地震。」劉向《五行傳》曰：「治宫室，飾臺榭，則稼穡不成，土失其性而為災。」則地震之異，固非無自而然也。然自古
translation_en:
…are evident in this policy essay. When he enters service in the future, his bearing will surely impress others.

Comment by Examiner Gao, Instructor: On the matter of averting calamities, the argument is sound and the insight lofty. One can discern your aspirations from this.

Comment by Examiner Ouyang, Instructor: Calamities have causes that bring them on, and there are methods for averting them. This policy essay discusses these matters most fully. It is selected to assist the self-cultivation and self-examination required today.

Heaven and humanity necessarily operate through mutual influence; ruler and ministers must cultivate themselves together with the utmost sincerity. For Heaven and humanity are grounded in a single principle, while ruler and ministers must prize unity of purpose. Heaven’s anomalies are surely intended to warn human beings. If, in the efforts of ruler and ministers to dispel them, even one matter remains inadequately addressed, how can they succeed in moving Heaven? Thus, when your discerning question touches upon this subject, I cannot help feeling deeply stirred anew. I earnestly wish that our ruler and ministers, high and low, should admonish one another, fully carrying out the substantive acts required to respond to Heaven. Then perhaps Heaven’s intent may be turned, the people’s hearts won, and harmonious energies elicited in response.

Why does the earth quake? Boyang Fu, the Grand Astrologer of Zhou, said: “When yang lies concealed and cannot emerge, and yin presses upon it so that it cannot rise, the earth quakes.” Liu Xiang’s Commentary on the Five Phases says: “When palaces and chambers are built and terraces and pavilions embellished, crops fail to ripen; earth loses its proper nature and produces calamities.” Thus, the anomaly of an earthquake certainly does not occur without a cause. Yet since antiquity…

title: 弘治十四年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
以來無代無之姑即其已甚者言之則在
漢文帝同日地震二十六處在宣帝地震
河南以東四十七郡太宗貞觀之時京師
地震松業二州靈州河東地震穆宗之時
京師地震屋瓦皆墜戶牖間有聲是其在
治世則欲以警動人君使因之而戒懼不
以既治而驕也在季世則欲以譴告人君
使因之而修省不以有事而怠也是天之
於君誠如父母於子者矣方今
===
聖天子致中致和於上大臣奉職守法於下宜
乎災異無自而生而雲南之異乃如此豈
非天心仁愛所以答吾君敬天勤民之意
固有加而無已者哉惟人子事親之心無
所不至不以喜而少縱其心不以怒而少
衰其孝君之事天亦何異此則所以消災
弭異之心固不能不廑於
上矣然君者出令者也臣者行君之令而致之
民者也比者
punctuated: 以來，無代無之。姑即其已甚者言之，則在漢文帝，同日地震二十六處；在宣帝，地震河南以東四十七郡；太宗貞觀之時，京師地震，松業二州、靈州、河東地震；穆宗之時，京師地震，屋瓦皆墜，戶牖間有聲。是其在治世，則欲以警動人君，使因之而戒懼，不以既治而驕也；在季世，則欲以譴告人君，使因之而修省，不以有事而怠也。是天之於君，誠如父母於子者矣。方今聖天子致中致和於上，大臣奉職守法於下，宜乎災異無自而生，而雲南之異乃如此，豈非天心仁愛，所以答吾君敬天勤民之意，固有加而無已者哉？惟人子事親之心，無所不至，不以喜而少縱其心，不以怒而少衰其孝。君之事天，亦何異此？則所以消災弭異之心，固不能不廑於上矣。然君者，出令者也；臣者，行君之令而致之民者也。比者，
translation_en:
…onward, no dynasty has been without them. To speak only of the most severe instances: under Emperor Wen of Han, earthquakes struck twenty-six places on the same day; under Emperor Xuan, earthquakes struck forty-seven commanderies from Henan eastward. During the Zhenguan reign of Emperor Taizong, earthquakes struck the capital, the two prefectures of Song and Ye [?], Lingzhou, and Hedong. Under Emperor Muzong, an earthquake struck the capital: roof tiles all fell, and sounds arose among the doors and windows. When such events occur in an age of good government, Heaven intends thereby to alert and stir the ruler, prompting him to vigilance and fear, so that he does not grow arrogant because order has already been achieved. When they occur in a dynasty’s declining age, Heaven intends thereby to rebuke and admonish the ruler, prompting him to reform and self-examination, so that he does not become remiss amid troubles. Heaven’s relation to the ruler is indeed like that of parents to their child.

At present, our sagely Son of Heaven brings equilibrium and harmony to realization above, while the great ministers discharge their duties and observe the laws below. One would expect disasters and anomalies to have no cause to arise; yet the anomalies in Yunnan are such as these. Is this not because Heaven’s benevolent care, by which it responds to our ruler’s intention to revere Heaven and labor for the people, continually increases without ceasing? A child’s devotion in serving his parents leaves nothing undone: their pleasure does not make him indulge himself even slightly, nor does their anger make his filial devotion diminish even slightly. How is the ruler’s service to Heaven any different? Thus the concern to dispel disasters and quell anomalies must surely weigh upon His Majesty. Yet the ruler issues commands, while ministers carry out his commands and bring them to the people. Recently…

title: 弘治十四年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
聖天子一聞地震之異遂遣祭告之使凡所以
奉承天意以答天譴者或自得於
聖心或建白於臣庶無不極力行之則所以應
天者固至矣第不知奉行於下者果能一
一如此乎執事謂政事或有所缺失者愚
固不敢謂盡無也誠使為之臣者上以率
下下以事上一皆以奉法循理為意各懷
愛
君憂國之誠禁奢惜費不敢盡民之財止工節
===
役不敢盡民之力黜奸貪之官進循良之
吏民之所利在於必興不為流俗因循之
論所惑民之所弊在於必革不為讒邪柔
佞之人所沮則庶幾應天以實所謂上下
交而德業成也天意安有不回變異安有
不弭者哉迂疎之見固非特為一方言之
而亦未知是否惟執事進而教之
第四問
高輔
punctuated:
聖天子一聞地震之異，遂遣祭告之使。凡所以奉承天意以答天譴者，或自得於聖心，或建白於臣庶，無不極力行之，則所以應天者固至矣。第不知奉行於下者果能一一如此乎？執事謂政事或有所缺失者，愚固不敢謂盡無也。誠使為之臣者，上以率下，下以事上，一皆以奉法循理為意，各懷愛君憂國之誠，禁奢惜費，不敢盡民之財；止工節役，不敢盡民之力；黜奸貪之官，進循良之吏。民之所利，在於必興，不為流俗因循之論所惑；民之所弊，在於必革，不為讒邪柔佞之人所沮。則庶幾應天以實，所謂上下交而德業成也。天意安有不回，變異安有不弭者哉？迂疎之見，固非特為一方言之，而亦未知是否，惟執事進而教之。
第四問
高輔
translation_en:
…As soon as the sagely Son of Heaven heard of the anomalous earthquake, he dispatched envoys to offer sacrifices and report to Heaven. Every means of reverently complying with Heaven’s intent and responding to its rebuke, whether conceived in his sagely mind or proposed by officials and commoners, has been carried out with the utmost effort. His response to Heaven has thus indeed been consummate. Yet I do not know whether those charged with implementation below have truly fulfilled each measure in this manner. You suggest that there may be shortcomings in government; I certainly would not venture to say that there are none.
If those serving as his ministers—superiors in leading their subordinates and subordinates in serving their superiors—would all make it their purpose to uphold the law and follow principle, each sincerely cherishing love for the ruler and concern for the state; if they would prohibit extravagance and husband expenditure, not daring to exhaust the people’s wealth; halt construction and restrain labor service, not daring to exhaust the people’s strength; dismiss corrupt and avaricious officials and promote conscientious and upright ones; insist on undertaking whatever benefits the people, undeluded by conventional arguments for carrying on as before; and insist on reforming whatever harms the people, undeterred by slanderous, wicked, ingratiating flatterers—then they might respond to Heaven through concrete deeds. This is what is meant by “those above and below communicate, and virtuous achievements are accomplished.” How could Heaven’s disposition fail to turn favorable, or anomalies fail to subside?
These impractical and ill-informed views of mine are certainly not offered solely for this one region. Yet I do not know whether they are correct; I ask only that you guide and instruct me further.
Fourth Policy Question
Gao Fu

title: 弘治十四年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
同考試官訓導潘批此策援據前代考課
之法無遺而模寫
今日考核得宜之意殆盡非積學有待者不能是用錄出
考試官教諭高批論考課之法有考據
有斟酌子之學其博而通者歟
考試官教諭歐陽批歷代考課之法惟我
朝為最善是策條答詳明且一本於得人可謂知要者矣
歷代之考課各有其法而操之在乎人今
日之考課雖主于嚴而行之在乎恕蓋人
===
以濟法則或嚴或恕皆足以舉一時之吏
治而不必泥其迹恕以濟嚴則一張一弛
皆足以鼓天下之人才而不必求其備愚
也於歷代之法與今日之事蓋嘗畧聞之
矣請為執事一言之考課之法其所由來
者遠矣品式之疎密不同事權之分合亦
異虞有三考之黜陟周有歲終之大計計
簿之察責之御史州牧之奏下之三公此
漢之法也六載之考委之達官優劣之等
punctuated:
同考試官訓導潘批：此策援據前代考課之法無遺，而模寫今日考核得宜之意殆盡，非積學有待者不能，是用錄出。
考試官教諭高批：論考課之法，有考據，有斟酌。子之學，其博而通者歟！
考試官教諭歐陽批：歷代考課之法，惟我朝為最善。是策條答詳明，且一本於得人，可謂知要者矣。
歷代之考課，各有其法，而操之在乎人。今日之考課，雖主于嚴，而行之在乎恕。蓋人以濟法，則或嚴或恕，皆足以舉一時之吏治，而不必泥其迹；恕以濟嚴，則一張一弛，皆足以鼓天下之人才，而不必求其備。愚也於歷代之法與今日之事，蓋嘗畧聞之矣，請為執事一言之。考課之法，其所由來者遠矣。品式之疎密不同，事權之分合亦異。虞有三考之黜陟，周有歲終之大計。計簿之察，責之御史；州牧之奏，下之三公：此漢之法也。六載之考，委之達官；優劣之等，
translation_en:
Comment by Associate Examiner Pan, Assistant Instructor: This policy essay draws comprehensively upon the methods of evaluating officials under previous dynasties and conveys almost fully the intent behind the appropriately conducted evaluations of the present day. Only someone who has accumulated learning in readiness for service could achieve this; it has therefore been selected for inclusion.
Comment by Examiner Gao, Instructor: Your discussion of methods for evaluating officials offers both historical evidence and careful judgment. How broad and penetrating your learning is!
Comment by Examiner Ouyang, Instructor: Of all the methods for evaluating officials through the dynasties, those of our dynasty are the best. This policy essay answers point by point, clearly and thoroughly, and grounds everything in securing the right people. It may be said to grasp the essentials.
Each dynasty has had its own methods for evaluating officials, but their administration depends upon people. Although evaluations today emphasize strictness, their implementation depends upon forbearance. When human judgment supplements established methods, either strictness or forbearance can improve the administration of officials in a given age, without slavishly adhering to outward forms. When forbearance tempers strictness, alternate tightening and relaxation can encourage talented people throughout the realm, without demanding perfection of them. I, in my ignorance, have heard a little about the methods of past dynasties and the practices of today. Allow me to offer you an account of them.
Methods of evaluating officials have a long history. Their grading procedures have differed in the degree of detail, as has the division or concentration of administrative authority. Under Yu, demotion and promotion followed three evaluations; under the Zhou, there was a comprehensive assessment at the end of the year. Scrutiny of accounting registers was entrusted to the Censors, and reports from Regional Governors were referred to the Three Dukes: these were the methods of the Han. Evaluations at six-year intervals were entrusted to high officials; the grades of superior and inferior performance …

title: 弘治十四年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
上之每歲此晉之法也唐制則百司之長
歲較其屬之功過而差以九等宋制則內
外選人周一歲為一考而磨勘叙遷其甲
乙之等則若河南吳公之第一茂陵蕭育
之第六皆是也其批書之辭則若官無異
稱之中上催科政拙之考下皆是也法之
行于上也因時而損益法之用于下也因
人而操縱以丙吉之寬大好禮則掩惡揚
善而無所按驗以袁安之仁信道孚則不
===
鞫贓罪而猾惡自禁條奏貪殘而天下肅
然者楊秉之風裁可想也舉奏貪汙而四
海翕然者黃瓊之精明可尚也趙宗儒懲
至德之黜陟則考中上者纔五十人而不
為刻是亦矯枉之意也盧承慶重督運者
之雅量則改判註之語至一再變而不為
專是亦觀人之法也選人匿喪者賈黜廢
之終身將以振風義也韓億之意則不欲
錮人于聖世而以捃拾小過為大戒然但
punctuated: 上之每歲，此晉之法也。唐制則百司之長歲較其屬之功過，而差以九等。宋制則內外選人周一歲為一考，而磨勘叙遷。其甲乙之等，則若河南吳公之第一、茂陵蕭育之第六，皆是也。其批書之辭，則若官無異稱之中上、催科政拙之考下，皆是也。法之行于上也，因時而損益；法之用于下也，因人而操縱。以丙吉之寬大好禮，則掩惡揚善而無所按驗；以袁安之仁信道孚，則不鞫贓罪而猾惡自禁。條奏貪殘而天下肅然者，楊秉之風裁可想也；舉奏貪汙而四海翕然者，黃瓊之精明可尚也。趙宗儒懲至德之黜陟，則考中上者纔五十人而不為刻，是亦矯枉之意也。盧承慶重督運者之雅量，則改判註之語至一再變而不為專，是亦觀人之法也。選人匿喪者，賈黜廢之終身，將以振風義也。韓億之意則不欲錮人于聖世，而以捃拾小過為大戒。然但
translation_en:
…were submitted each year: this was the Jin system. Under the Tang system, the heads of the various offices annually compared the merits and faults of their subordinates and ranked them in nine grades. Under the Song system, lower-ranking officials serving within and outside the capital received one evaluation for each full year, and their records were scrutinized to determine advancement. Examples of their relative rankings include Lord Wu of Henan being placed first and Xiao Yu of Maoling being placed sixth. Examples of the wording entered in their evaluations include an upper-middle rating for “no exceptional reputation in office,” and a low rating for “inept administration in collecting taxes.”

When those above implement these regulations, they modify them according to the times; when applying them to those below, they tighten or relax them according to the individual. Bing Ji, being generous and devoted to ritual propriety, concealed faults and commended merits, conducting no investigations. Yuan An, through benevolence, trustworthiness, and the confidence inspired by his moral conduct, did not interrogate officials over corruption, yet the crafty and wicked restrained themselves. Yang Bing submitted itemized accusations against the greedy and oppressive, and all under Heaven stood in awe: we can imagine his moral authority and discernment. Huang Qiong impeached the corrupt, and all within the Four Seas united in approval: his acuity deserves esteem.

Taking warning from the promotions and demotions of the Zhide era, Zhao Zongru awarded upper-middle ratings to only fifty men, yet this was not deemed harsh; his intention, too, was to correct abuses. Lu Chengqing valued the composure of an official supervising transport and revised the wording of his assessment repeatedly, yet this was not deemed arbitrary; this, too, was a method of judging people. When a lower-ranking official concealed a bereavement, Jia [?] dismissed him and barred him from office for life, intending thereby to uphold moral conduct and duty. Han Yi, however, did not wish to exclude anyone permanently from office in a sage ruler’s age, and regarded picking out minor faults as something to guard against above all. Yet merely…

title: 弘治十四年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
曰小過而已則大者之不赦可知也監司
不才者范仲淹付之一筆將以利生民也
杜衍之意則欲使人改過遷善而以摘發
小節為不恕然但曰小節而已則大者之
必懲可知也嗟夫水火之用不同而同于
利物鹹酸之用不同而同于適口寛嚴之
用不同而同于奉法二者之用惟視其人
何如耳得其人則嚴者足以飭吏治而寛
者亦足以鎮雅俗不得其人則其嚴也或
===
至于矯激有假擊搏之威以肆其殘忍之
性者矣其恕也或流于姑息有借持重之
名以濟其不斷之私者矣我
朝考課之法一以虞周為準品式周詳體統
不紊以藩臬察郡守以郡守察縣令有巡
按者以莅之有巡撫者以總之行部則廉
其臧否之實代還則上其批書之語其後
恐風聞之失實而使人坐被空文也則令
歳終奏報下之吏部而明著于冊又其後
punctuated:
曰小過而已，則大者之不赦可知也。監司不才者，范仲淹付之一筆，將以利生民也。杜衍之意，則欲使人改過遷善，而以摘發小節為不恕。然但曰小節而已，則大者之必懲可知也。嗟夫！水火之用不同，而同于利物；鹹酸之用不同，而同于適口；寛嚴之用不同，而同于奉法。二者之用，惟視其人何如耳。得其人，則嚴者足以飭吏治，而寛者亦足以鎮雅俗；不得其人，則其嚴也或至于矯激，有假擊搏之威以肆其殘忍之性者矣；其恕也或流于姑息，有借持重之名以濟其不斷之私者矣。
我朝考課之法，一以虞周為準，品式周詳，體統不紊。以藩臬察郡守，以郡守察縣令，有巡按者以莅之，有巡撫者以總之。行部則廉其臧否之實，代還則上其批書之語。其後，恐風聞之失實，而使人坐被空文也，則令歳終奏報，下之吏部，而明著于冊。又其後，
translation_en:
…he spoke only of minor faults; thus it is clear that major ones were not to be pardoned. Fan Zhongyan dismissed incompetent surveillance officials with a stroke of his brush, intending thereby to benefit the people. Du Yan’s intention, however, was to encourage people to correct their faults and turn toward goodness; he considered exposing minor shortcomings unforgiving. Yet he spoke only of minor shortcomings; thus it is clear that major ones must be punished. Alas! Water and fire differ in their uses, yet both benefit things; salty and sour flavors differ in their uses, yet both please the palate; leniency and severity differ in their uses, yet both serve to uphold the law. The application of these two depends solely on the character of the person employing them. With the right person, severity suffices to put official administration in order, while leniency likewise suffices to bring stability to the refined and the common alike. Without the right person, severity may become excessive: some exploit the intimidating power of punitive action to indulge their cruel dispositions. Forbearance may likewise lapse into indulgence: some borrow the reputation of being cautious and deliberate to accommodate their own indecisiveness.
Our dynasty’s system for evaluating officials takes Yu and Zhou as its sole standards. Its classifications and procedures are comprehensive and detailed, and its institutional order is maintained without confusion. Provincial administration commissioners and surveillance commissioners inspect prefects, and prefects inspect county magistrates; regional inspecting censors oversee them, and grand coordinators exercise general supervision. When touring their jurisdictions, they investigate the actual merits and failings of officials; when they return upon being replaced, they submit their written appraisals. Later, out of concern that hearsay might prove inaccurate and cause people to suffer unjustly from unsupported written allegations, annual reports to the throne were required at the end of the year. These were referred to the Ministry of Personnel and clearly entered in its registers. Still later…

title: 弘治十四年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
恐胥吏之漏言而使人因緣為姦也則吏
部取每歲所報櫝而藏之臨事而後啓大
約總計所報以三分為率三分俱報其賢
者為上二分者次之俱無焉者為下其防
之也可謂周而察之也可謂審矣仕者雖
欲飾名以求功巧文以逃罪不可得也
皇上端居九重之上而遊念四海之遠愛惜人
才之意常寓于綜核名實之中往年吏部
上罷黜之數
===
聖諭則曰人才難得如有不公許其伸理于是
行覆考之令止欲去其太甚而新任者皆
復其官繼後臺諫言黜陟之事
聖諭又曰考察重事毋得偏聽致有枉抑于是
申明批考之法止據見任開報而既往者
不追其過盖立法雖嚴而行之甚恕即古
昔聖王使人以器與人不求備之盛心也
一時奉法之臣皆能將順
德意嚴重者有黃瓊范仲淹之風寬厚者有
punctuated:
恐胥吏之漏言而使人因緣為姦也，則吏部取每歲所報，櫝而藏之，臨事而後啓。大約總計所報，以三分為率：三分俱報其賢者為上，二分者次之，俱無焉者為下。其防之也可謂周，而察之也可謂審矣。仕者雖欲飾名以求功，巧文以逃罪，不可得也。
皇上端居九重之上，而遊念四海之遠，愛惜人才之意，常寓于綜核名實之中。往年吏部上罷黜之數，聖諭則曰：「人才難得，如有不公，許其伸理。」于是行覆考之令，止欲去其太甚，而新任者皆復其官。繼後臺諫言黜陟之事，聖諭又曰：「考察重事，毋得偏聽，致有枉抑。」于是申明批考之法，止據見任開報，而既往者不追其過。盖立法雖嚴，而行之甚恕，即古昔聖王使人以器、與人不求備之盛心也。一時奉法之臣，皆能將順德意，嚴重者有黃瓊、范仲淹之風，寬厚者有
translation_en:
…fearing that clerks might divulge information and thereby enable people to exploit their connections for wrongdoing, the Ministry of Personnel placed each year’s reports in boxes and stored them, opening them only when a case required it. Broadly speaking, it assessed the reports together, taking three reports as the standard: those whom all three reported as worthy were placed in the highest category; those endorsed by two came next; and those endorsed by none were placed in the lowest. Its safeguards may indeed be called comprehensive, and its scrutiny thorough. Even if officials wished to embellish their reputations to claim merit, or manipulate documents to escape punishment, they could not do so.
His Majesty resides in the innermost palace, yet his thoughts range to the farthest reaches of the realm. His concern to cherish men of talent is constantly expressed through comprehensive scrutiny of whether reputations accord with actual performance. In a previous year, when the Ministry of Personnel submitted the figures for dismissals, the imperial instruction declared: “Men of talent are difficult to obtain. If there has been any injustice, allow those concerned to seek redress.” An order for reassessment was therefore implemented, with the intention of removing only the worst offenders, and all newly appointed officials were restored to their posts. Subsequently, when the censorial and remonstrance officials spoke about dismissals and promotions, another imperial instruction declared: “The evaluation of officials is a weighty matter. You must not listen to only one side and thereby cause unjust treatment.” Accordingly, the rules for written assessments were clarified: reports were to concern only officials currently holding office, and those who had already left were not pursued for their past faults. Thus, although the rules were strict, their application was most forgiving. This was precisely the generous spirit of the sage kings of antiquity, who employed men according to their abilities and did not demand perfection of them. The ministers charged with carrying out the rules at that time all supported and fulfilled this virtuous intention. The stern and dignified among them displayed the qualities of Huang Qiong and Fan Zhongyan; the generous and forbearing possessed…

title: 弘治十四年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
丙吉杜衍之譽所以吏稱其職民安其業
治化之盛比隆虞周而非漢唐宋之所能
及也執事于此猶過為借聽之謀欲求可
以裨益時政者迂儒不知通變將何說以
應雖然言及之而不言亦君子所不與也
竊有所見願終言之盖聞異時之考課也
吏部就來
朝各官中簡其治行尤異者具疏以
聞寵以異數或陪祀于
===
南郊或賜燕于南宫或别記其姓名或亟擢
其顯位一時之仕者傾耳而聽企踵而瞻
往往咨嗟歎羡而耻己之不與則爭相磨
礪勉修職業以冀後日之或與焉此所謂
賞一人而千萬人勸亦轉移感動之一機
也其事未遠其効可徴不知今日亦可舉
而行之否乎僭妄之言承問而對執政者
聞之或有取焉則豈惟仕者之幸
第五問
punctuated:
丙吉、杜衍之譽。所以吏稱其職，民安其業，治化之盛，比隆虞周，而非漢唐宋之所能及也。執事于此猶過為借聽之謀，欲求可以裨益時政者，迂儒不知通變，將何說以應？雖然，言及之而不言，亦君子所不與也。竊有所見，願終言之。盖聞異時之考課也，吏部就來朝各官中，簡其治行尤異者，具疏以聞，寵以異數：或陪祀于南郊，或賜燕于南宫，或别記其姓名，或亟擢其顯位。一時之仕者，傾耳而聽，企踵而瞻，往往咨嗟歎羡，而耻己之不與，則爭相磨礪，勉修職業，以冀後日之或與焉。此所謂賞一人而千萬人勸，亦轉移感動之一機也。其事未遠，其効可徴，不知今日亦可舉而行之否乎？僭妄之言，承問而對，執政者聞之，或有取焉，則豈惟仕者之幸？

第五問
translation_en:
…enjoyed reputations like those of Bing Ji and Du Yan. Thus officials fulfilled their duties and the people pursued their livelihoods in peace. The flourishing of government and moral transformation rivaled that of Yu and Zhou, beyond anything the Han, Tang, or Song could attain. Yet you, sir, still take such pains to solicit opinions, seeking something that might benefit current government. What can an impractical scholar like myself, ignorant of how to adapt to changing circumstances, offer in reply? Nevertheless, to remain silent when invited to speak is also something a gentleman would not approve. I have some thoughts and ask leave to state them fully.

I have heard that, in earlier evaluations of officials, the Ministry of Personnel selected those with especially outstanding records of administration from among the officials who came to court, and submitted memorials reporting them to the throne. They were favored with exceptional honors: some were permitted to attend the sacrifices at the southern suburban altar; some were granted banquets at the Southern Palace; some had their names specially recorded; and some were promptly promoted to prominent offices. Officials of the time listened intently and stood on tiptoe to look on. They often sighed in admiration and envy, ashamed that they themselves were not among those honored. They therefore competed in honing their abilities and diligently discharging their official duties, hoping that they too might be included at a later date. This is what is meant by rewarding one person and encouraging thousands upon thousands; it is also a means of bringing about change and inspiring people. These events are not remote, and their effectiveness can be verified. Might this practice also be revived and implemented today?

These presumptuous words are offered in response to your question. If those who administer the government should hear them and find something worth adopting, would it be the officials alone who were fortunate?

Fifth Question

title: 弘治十四年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
趙儀
考試官教諭高批禦戎之策據古酌今
非尋常敷演者比充積如此明春
大廷之對知不多讓
考試官教諭歐陽批歷陳古人禦戎之法
參酌時勢非有卓見者能之耶
莫難於禦戎而得其法也易莫難於用法
而得其人也易不得其法則所以備於豫
者不固謀於變者不神戎狄之來也無以
===
應之不得其人則靜而玩愒無徹桑之謀
動而畏縮無鷹揚之勇法何從而出也必
既得其法又得其人以守則固以戰則克
尚何戎狄之足慮哉愚也草茅下士曷足
以與
廟堂之訏謨顧明問下及有不敢默焉者請
復其萬一夫中國之有夷狄猶晝之有夜
陽之有陰君子之有小人也故邊境自古
為患而備禦代不乏人試以自周而後者
punctuated:
趙儀

考試官教諭高批：禦戎之策，據古酌今，非尋常敷演者比。充積如此，明春大廷之對，知不多讓。

考試官教諭歐陽批：歷陳古人禦戎之法，參酌時勢，非有卓見者能之耶？

莫難於禦戎，而得其法也易；莫難於用法，而得其人也易。不得其法，則所以備於豫者不固，謀於變者不神，戎狄之來也，無以應之。不得其人，則靜而玩愒，無徹桑之謀；動而畏縮，無鷹揚之勇，法何從而出也？必既得其法，又得其人，以守則固，以戰則克，尚何戎狄之足慮哉？愚也，草茅下士，曷足以與廟堂之訏謨？顧明問下及，有不敢默焉者，請復其萬一。夫中國之有夷狄，猶晝之有夜，陽之有陰，君子之有小人也。故邊境自古為患，而備禦代不乏人。試以自周而後者
translation_en:
Zhao Yi

Comment by Examiner Gao, an Instructor: Your strategy for defending against the Rong draws upon antiquity while weighing present circumstances; it is beyond comparison with ordinary elaborations. With learning so amply accumulated, you will surely yield little to others in your response at the imperial court next spring.

Comment by Examiner Ouyang, an Instructor: You set out in detail the ancients’ methods of defending against the Rong, weighing them against the circumstances of the times. Could anyone without outstanding insight accomplish this?

Nothing is harder than defending against the Rong, yet with the right methods it becomes easy; nothing is harder than applying methods, yet with the right men it becomes easy. Without the right methods, advance preparations will lack solidity, and plans for responding to sudden changes will lack resourcefulness. When the Rong and Di arrive, there will be no means of meeting them. Without the right men, in quiet times they will idle away their days, lacking the foresight to gather mulberry roots and secure the nest before the storm; when action is required, they will shrink back in fear, lacking the courage of a soaring hawk. How, then, can methods be put into practice? One must obtain both the right methods and the right men: defense will then be secure, and battle victorious. What cause will there be to fear the Rong and Di?

I am but an unworthy scholar in rustic obscurity. How could I be fit to participate in the court’s grand deliberations? Yet since your discerning question has reached even me, there are things on which I dare not remain silent. Allow me to offer a response on the smallest part of the matter. The presence of the Yi and Di alongside the Central Kingdom is like night alongside day, yin alongside yang, or petty men alongside gentlemen. Thus the frontiers have been a source of trouble since antiquity, but no age has lacked men capable of preparing defenses. Let us take examples from the Zhou onward …

title: 弘治十四年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
言之若居代鴈門而匈奴十餘歲不敢犯
邊者李牧也為雲中太守而匈奴深畏其
略者李廣也祭彤誘鮮卑擊弱匈奴而邊
無寇警盖恩惠所感焉陳禪於學行禮陳
說道義而單于懷服盖天理所孚焉都督
并州而邊塵不驚比之長城者李勣之功
何著哉刺史隴州設為譙櫓以禦虜暴者
馬燧之威何震哉請城方渠以遏吐蕃歸
路楊朝晟萬全之計審矣總十一軍而築
===
===
三城於要路李德裕措置之方密矣定州
練兵精勁齊一而聲動虜中非韓琦之謀
猷克壯而致是乎以詔書犒賞諸羌受命
而始為漢用非范仲淹之能服人心而得
是乎之數君子者忠義著聞恩威並用其
一時邊塞寧謐未必非其功也洪惟我
國家之於夷狄來則厚金幣以賚之閒又遣
使臣以慰之綏之之道既善矣嚴城壘之
設以為之防命文武之臣以為之守馭之
punctuated: 言之，若居代鴈門而匈奴十餘歲不敢犯邊者，李牧也；為雲中太守而匈奴深畏其略者，李廣也。祭彤誘鮮卑擊弱匈奴，而邊無寇警，盖恩惠所感焉；陳禪於學行禮，陳說道義，而單于懷服，盖天理所孚焉。都督并州，而邊塵不驚，比之長城者，李勣之功何著哉！刺史隴州，設為譙櫓以禦虜暴者，馬燧之威何震哉！請城方渠，以遏吐蕃歸路，楊朝晟萬全之計審矣；總十一軍，而築三城於要路，李德裕措置之方密矣。定州練兵，精勁齊一，而聲動虜中，非韓琦之謀猷克壯而致是乎？以詔書犒賞諸羌，受命而始為漢用，非范仲淹之能服人心而得是乎？之數君子者，忠義著聞，恩威並用，其一時邊塞寧謐，未必非其功也。洪惟我國家之於夷狄，來則厚金幣以賚之，閒又遣使臣以慰之，綏之之道既善矣；嚴城壘之設以為之防，命文武之臣以為之守，馭之
translation_en:
…to speak of them: it was Li Mu who held Yanmen in Dai, so that the Xiongnu dared not violate the frontier for more than ten years; it was Li Guang who served as Grand Administrator of Yunzhong, whose strategy the Xiongnu deeply feared. Ji Tong induced the Xianbei to attack and weaken the Xiongnu, leaving the frontier free of alarms of invasion: surely they were moved by his kindness and generosity. Chen Chan performed ceremonies at the school and expounded the Way and righteousness, so that the chanyu was won over and submitted: surely the principles of Heaven inspired his trust. How illustrious were the achievements of Li Ji, who, as Area Commander of Bingzhou, kept the frontier free of the dust of war and was likened to the Great Wall! How awe-inspiring was the might of Ma Sui, who, as Prefect of Longzhou, erected watchtowers to ward off the enemy’s violence! Yang Chaosheng’s thoroughly secure plan was carefully considered: he requested the fortification of Fangqu to block the Tibetans’ route of retreat. Li Deyu’s arrangements were meticulous: he commanded eleven armies and built three fortified towns on strategic routes. At Dingzhou, troops were trained to be elite, vigorous, and united, and their renown shook the enemy’s lands. Was this not brought about by the strength of Han Qi’s strategic planning? When the various Qiang received rewards under an imperial edict, they accepted the commands and began to serve the Han. Was this not achieved through Fan Zhongyan’s ability to win people’s hearts? These several gentlemen [?] were renowned for loyalty and righteousness and employed both kindness and authority. The tranquillity of the frontier in their respective times may indeed have been due to their achievements.
Reflecting reverently upon our dynasty’s treatment of the peoples beyond its borders: when they come, it bestows generous gifts of gold and silks upon them; from time to time, it also dispatches envoys to reassure them. Its means of pacifying them are already excellent. It establishes strong fortified defenses to guard against them and appoints civil and military officials to hold those defenses. Its means of controlling them…

title: 弘治十四年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
之法又至矣柰何比來北虜負
恩敢於犯順及遣將出師也逐之則潛蹤而去
緩之則乘間而來此所以致厪
宵旰之慮然竊聞之夷狄不義縱暴必亡在
備禦之得其法將帥之得其人耳誠使為
邊將者如李牧之在鴈門廣儲積慎烽火
練習騎射恩遇士卒勿輕舉以損其威謹
妄動以蓄其銳俟彼之來也則以逸待勞
可一鼓而破之其鋒一挫自爾遠遁敢復
===
來乎如祭肜之處鮮卑結以恩惠示以財
利諭以逆順禍福諉以交相攻伐使於我
各售其功於彼各分其志若彼之動也則
以眾當寡可不戰而屈之其黨既散自然
孤立敢為患乎以至凡握兵守土者皆陳
禪李勣之流韓琦仲淹之輩或以德化或
以威畧而
國家明旌别之典嚴黜陟之條功多有厚賞
不迪有顯戮則人皆自奮爭樹功業將使
punctuated: 之法又至矣。柰何比來北虜負恩，敢於犯順？及遣將出師也，逐之則潛蹤而去，緩之則乘間而來，此所以致厪宵旰之慮。然竊聞之，夷狄不義，縱暴必亡，在備禦之得其法、將帥之得其人耳。誠使為邊將者如李牧之在鴈門，廣儲積，慎烽火，練習騎射，恩遇士卒，勿輕舉以損其威，謹妄動以蓄其銳，俟彼之來也，則以逸待勞，可一鼓而破之。其鋒一挫，自爾遠遁，敢復來乎？如祭肜之處鮮卑，結以恩惠，示以財利，諭以逆順禍福，諉以交相攻伐，使於我各售其功，於彼各分其志。若彼之動也，則以眾當寡，可不戰而屈之。其黨既散，自然孤立，敢為患乎？以至凡握兵守土者，皆陳禪、李勣之流，韓琦、仲淹之輩，或以德化，或以威畧，而國家明旌别之典，嚴黜陟之條，功多有厚賞，不迪有顯戮，則人皆自奮，爭樹功業，將使
translation_en:
…the methods for controlling them are also most thorough. Why, then, have the northern barbarians recently betrayed imperial kindness and dared to defy rightful authority? When generals are dispatched with troops, pursuit makes them disappear without a trace, while any relaxation allows them to exploit an opening and return. This is what burdens His Majesty with concerns from early morning until late at night. Yet I have humbly heard that the barbarians lack righteousness and, if they indulge in violence, must perish. It is simply a matter of employing the proper methods of defense and obtaining the right men as commanders.

If only our frontier generals were like Li Mu at Yanmen: amassing ample stores, carefully maintaining the beacon signals, training in mounted archery, and treating the soldiers with kindness; avoiding ill-considered expeditions that would diminish their authority, and guarding against rash action [?] to preserve their fighting strength. Then, when the enemy came, they could meet the exhausted with rested troops and rout them at a single beat of the drum. Once the enemy’s offensive strength had been broken, they would retreat far away of their own accord. Would they dare return?

Or let them act like Zhai Tong in his dealings with the Xianbei: bind them through kindness and favor, show them material advantages, explain the calamities and blessings attending defiance and submission, and charge them with attacking one another. Let each seek recognition from us for his achievements, while their purposes become divided among themselves. Then, should they move against us, we could oppose their few with our many and subdue them without battle. Once their alliances had scattered, they would naturally stand isolated. Would they dare cause trouble?

Furthermore, let all who command troops and defend territory be men of the stamp of Chen Chan and Li Ji, of Han Qi and Zhongyan: some transforming others through virtue, others employing military authority and strategy. Let the state clearly apply its rules for distinguishing merit and strictly enforce its provisions for dismissal and promotion, granting generous rewards for great achievements and imposing public execution upon the disobedient. Then everyone would exert himself and compete to establish meritorious achievements. This would bring it about that…

title: 弘治十四年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
隻輪匹馬絕跡於邊徼鬼馘獸形退伏於
窮荒保金甌之全勢紓
宵旰之憂勤恐於此而得其萬一矣雖然愚
又有說焉七旬苗格於誕敷文德之後四
夷咸賓於明王慎德之時今日夷狄之患
安知非天心仁愛欲如虞周之盛乎人事
修則天意得天意得則邊釁弭此只在
聖天子加之意而已區區芹曝之誠敢以是為
篇終獻
punctuated: 隻輪匹馬絕跡於邊徼，鬼馘獸形退伏於窮荒，保金甌之全勢，紓宵旰之憂勤，恐於此而得其萬一矣。雖然，愚又有說焉：七旬苗格於誕敷文德之後，四夷咸賓於明王慎德之時。今日夷狄之患，安知非天心仁愛，欲如虞周之盛乎？人事修則天意得，天意得則邊釁弭。此只在聖天子加之意而已。區區芹曝之誠，敢以是為篇終獻。
translation_en:
…so that not a single enemy wheel or horse leaves a trace along the frontier, and those with demonic heads [?] and bestial forms retreat into submission in the remotest wilds. We would preserve the realm intact, like an unbroken golden vessel, and ease the anxious toil that keeps Your Majesty occupied before dawn and after dusk. Perhaps these measures might accomplish some tiny part of that aim.
Even so, I have something further to say. The Miao submitted after seventy days, following the widespread propagation of civil virtue; the peoples of all four quarters acknowledged allegiance when the enlightened king attended carefully to his virtue. How do we know that today’s troubles with the foreign peoples are not an expression of Heaven’s benevolent concern, intended to bring about prosperity like that of Yu and Zhou? When human affairs are properly ordered, Heaven’s favor is secured; when Heaven’s favor is secured, frontier strife subsides. This depends only upon the sage Son of Heaven giving it his attention. With the humble sincerity of one offering celery or the warmth of the sun, I venture to present these words as the concluding offering of my essay.

title: 弘治十四年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
雲貴鄉試錄後序
弘治辛酉秋八月壬申雲貴
鄉試事竣取士五十人刻其
文之尤者二十篇合為錄以
獻于
上皆成法也巡按雲南監察御史
何琛實監臨之防範之嚴去
===
取之審蓋有法外意焉故事
錄有序叢幸與有司列謹序
其後曰於乎雲貴之取士至
此亦云盛矣嘗考之其初舉
者纔十數人而止漸益之至
四十有五人又再益之乃如
今日之數至今又三科矣士
punctuated:
雲貴鄉試錄後序

弘治辛酉秋八月壬申，雲貴鄉試事竣，取士五十人，刻其文之尤者二十篇，合為錄，以獻于上，皆成法也。巡按雲南監察御史何琛實監臨之，防範之嚴，去取之審，蓋有法外意焉。故事，錄有序。叢幸與有司列，謹序其後曰：於乎！雲貴之取士，至此亦云盛矣！嘗考之，其初舉者纔十數人而止，漸益之，至四十有五人，又再益之，乃如今日之數，至今又三科矣。士
translation_en:
Postface to the Record of the Yunnan-Guizhou Provincial Examination

On the renshen day of the eighth month in autumn of the xinyou year of the Hongzhi reign (1501), the Yunnan-Guizhou Provincial Examination concluded, and fifty men were selected. Twenty of their finest compositions were printed and compiled into a record for presentation to His Majesty, all in accordance with established regulations. He Chen 何琛, Investigating Censor serving as Regional Inspector of Yunnan, acted as Supervising Official. The strictness of his safeguards and the care with which he accepted or rejected candidates bespeak a concern extending beyond the prescribed rules.

By precedent, the record has a preface. I, Cong 叢, having been fortunate enough to serve among the responsible officials, respectfully append this postface: Ah! The selection of men in Yunnan and Guizhou may now indeed be called flourishing! I have examined its history: at first, only ten or so men were selected. The number was gradually increased to forty-five, then increased again to the present figure. Three examination cycles have now passed since that increase. The scholars …

title: 弘治十四年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
之進脩日益盛由今之試者
觀之雖更益數人亦可也然
而有不可者法也法之所在
不得以私意出入之者也豈
惟取士之數爲然由今錄中
所刻及諸得雋之文觀之爲
易義者不得如書如詩而春
===
秋不得如禮如易也爲論者
不得如義而爲判爲策對亦
不得如詔誥之類也何者亦
各有法故也夫取士之數裁
定於今因時而損益作文之
格沿習於古與時而高下是
二者皆以成法所在不容以
punctuated: 之進脩日益盛，由今之試者觀之，雖更益數人亦可也。然而有不可者，法也。法之所在，不得以私意出入之者也。豈惟取士之數爲然？由今錄中所刻及諸得雋之文觀之，爲《易》義者不得如《書》、如《詩》，而《春秋》不得如《禮》、如《易》也。爲論者不得如義，而爲判、爲策對亦不得如詔誥之類也。何者？亦各有法故也。夫取士之數，裁定於今，因時而損益；作文之格，沿習於古，與時而高下。是二者皆以成法所在，不容以
translation_en: …their advancement in learning and self-cultivation grows ever more flourishing. Judging by those who sat this examination, it would be reasonable to increase the quota by several more. Yet what prevents this is the regulation. Where a regulation applies, one may not depart from it according to personal preference. How could this be true only of the number of men selected? Judging from the writings printed in this record and the other compositions of successful candidates, an exposition on the Book of Changes must not resemble one on the Book of Documents or the Book of Odes; likewise, one on the Spring and Autumn Annals must not resemble one on the Book of Rites or the Book of Changes. A discourse must not resemble a classical exposition, and a legal judgment or a policy essay must not resemble an imperial edict or proclamation. Why? Because each likewise has its own rules. The quota for selecting men is determined in the present and reduced or increased according to the times; the forms of composition are inherited from antiquity and rise or decline with the times. Since both are governed by established rules, they do not permit…

title: 弘治十四年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
私意參之而况於士之自立
無時而可變者而獨無成法
乎哉盖自修己以至于安百
姓自一命以上至於宰天下
自戒慎恐懼以至于位天地
育萬物君子小人之分義利
公私之辨皆有聖賢之成法
===
在焉為士者當從事於此以
終其身隨其職守才力所至
以敬其事非可因時勢而為
之高下損益者也夫以取士
之有法也外之則罪矣作文
之有法也失之則黜矣士之
自立萬有一焉或悖於聖賢
punctuated: 私意參之。而况於士之自立，無時而可變者，而獨無成法乎哉？盖自修己以至于安百姓，自一命以上至於宰天下，自戒慎恐懼以至于位天地、育萬物，君子小人之分，義利公私之辨，皆有聖賢之成法在焉。為士者當從事於此，以終其身，隨其職守才力所至，以敬其事，非可因時勢而為之高下損益者也。夫以取士之有法也，外之則罪矣；作文之有法也，失之則黜矣。士之自立，萬有一焉，或悖於聖賢
translation_en: …to interfere with them through private judgment. How much more, then, must established standards exist for a scholar’s cultivation of his own character, which can never change with the times? From cultivating oneself to bringing peace to the common people; from receiving one’s first official appointment to governing all under Heaven; from vigilance and apprehension to bringing Heaven and Earth into their proper places and nurturing the myriad things; in distinguishing the gentleman from the petty man, righteousness from profit, and public from private interests—in all these matters there are established standards of the sages and worthies. A scholar should devote himself to these throughout his life, attending reverently to his duties according to his official responsibilities and the reach of his abilities. These standards cannot be raised or lowered, diminished or augmented, according to changing times and circumstances. Since there are rules for selecting scholars for office, those who depart from them are punished; since there are rules for composing examination essays, those who fail to meet them are rejected. If, in establishing his own character, a scholar should, even in one instance out of ten thousand, act contrary to the sages and worthies…

title: 弘治十四年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
之成法縱幸不為有司之所
罪與黜如內愧何如天下之
公議何諸生皆誦法孔氏者
孔氏之法士莫重乎其始進
故於其始進也以是瀆告之
有司者将考其後焉
湖廣長沙府湘陰縣儒學教
===
諭髙巖謹序
punctuated:
之成法，縱幸不為有司之所罪與黜，如內愧何？如天下之公議何？諸生皆誦法孔氏者，孔氏之法，士莫重乎其始進，故於其始進也，以是瀆告之。有司者将考其後焉。
湖廣長沙府湘陰縣儒學教諭髙巖謹序。
translation_en:
…the established standards of the sages and worthies, even if one should fortunately escape punishment and rejection by the responsible officials, how could one face one’s inward shame? How could one face the public judgment of all under Heaven? You students all recite the teachings of Confucius and take him as your model. According to Confucius’s standards, nothing is more important for a scholar than his first advancement into official life. Thus, at this first advancement, I venture to trouble you with these admonitions. The responsible officials will examine your subsequent conduct.
Preface respectfully written by Gao Yan, Instructor of the Confucian School of Xiangyin County, Changsha Prefecture, Huguang.
